<margin>June 5</margin>
-> Wednesday afternoon, around 2:00 PM, 1583. <-

[Delta]: E.K. <note>Edward Kelley</note> had been, ever since nine o'clock in the morning, in a marvelous state of mental disquiet, fury, and rage. This was because his brother Thomas had brought him news that:

1. A commission <note>A legal warrant</note> was out to attach and apprehend him as a felon for the coining of money <note>Counterfeiting, a capital offense</note>.
2. Secondly, that his wife had left Mistress Freeman’s house at Blockley, and that Mr. Hussey had reported him to be a cozener <note>term: a fraud or swindler</note> and had recently made very bitter and grievous reports about him.
3. And that his wife was now at home with her mother at Chipping Norton.

Whereupon, I—considering the great disorder and external trouble facing him, and his even greater offense against God through his furious impatience internally—remembered the entire premise of God’s service to be performed by us two (if we would be dutiful servants to His Divine Majesty). I was touched with a great pang of compassion, both that any Christian should use such speech as he used, or be of such a revenging mind and intent as he showed himself to be; and also in respect of my own reputation, which might be brought into doubt for keeping the company of such a person, a disorderly man. Thirdly, I feared that the good service of God might hereby be taken away from our execution, to our great danger in both body and soul. Therefore, to do my duty as a man resolute (based on our uniting for God’s service) to do for him as I would for myself, I made God my refuge for comfort.

**[Maid]:** Where have you been? If your dignity were as good as your old-fashioned hypocrisy <note>original: "ancient dissembling"</note>, I would tell you.

**Old man:** ... These words are very arrogant <note>original: "large"</note>; what is the reason you will not be acquainted with me? (I never did you harm), and I have desired to be acquainted with you for a long time.

**Maid:** ... Everything commonly teaches of itself.

<meta>This page continues the dialogue between the spirit Galathiel and John Dee ([delta]). Galathiel is responding to the theological and philosophical objections raised by Johannes Trithemius (a real-world historical polymath and abbot) regarding the nature of spirits and the spiritual status of women.</meta>

**Galathiel:** You think, then, that I have some understanding.

**Dee [$\Delta$]:** Yes, God knows I do.

**Galathiel:** First, it is evident that the spirits of God are beyond the understanding of those who are below them. For just as the higher orders of spirits are incomparable to God, so too, by degrees, those who are lower are incomparable to those above them. It follows, therefore, that because of this hierarchy among angels, certain things remain incomprehensible. <margin>G1 Angels</margin> Angels, I say, are in themselves neither man nor woman. Therefore, they do not take on physical forms based on any literal shape in the imagination, but according to the wise and purposeful will of both God and the specific task they are administering. For we are all spirits serving the will of God—and for whom? For everything within the realm of nature, solely for His glory and for the use of humanity.

It follows, therefore—considering that we do not serve by our own authority—that we should serve in that mysterious form within which our duties are defined. But if Trithemius <note>original: "Tritemius" – Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot and occultist whose writings on spirits John Dee studied closely.</note> can argue that a woman does not possess the spirit of God—despite being formed and fashioned from the very same substance, albeit in a different proportion—if Trithemius can separate the dignity of a woman's soul from the excellence of a man's, except by the physical form of their bodies, then his argument might hold weight. 

But because there is a shared proportion and preparation for holiness in eternity for both man and woman, those who are the eternal ministers <margin>G2 Eternal Ministers</margin> of God may, in accordance with that holiness, take on the forms of either. I mean this in terms of their outward appearance; for just as you read the word "human" <note>original Latin: *Homo*</note> for both, so too in both you find the exact same dignity in their inner essence. 

However, Trithemius spoke regarding the "filthiness" (which is actually no filthiness at all) with which all women are allegedly stained. He used the reasoning of natural philosophers, acting as a man who understands the physical world better than he understands the Creator or the supernatural Master. He concluded his physical theories based on nature. Regarding myself, I answer Trithemius <margin>G3 Galathiel's answer to Trithemius</margin> this way: I am the Goal <note>original Latin: *Finis*</note>; I am a beam of that Wisdom which is the ultimate purpose of human excellence. 

Those who are called the "daughters" <note>original Latin: *Filiæ*</note> and the "daughters of daughters" <note>original Latin: *Filiæ filiarum*</note> are all contained within me, and they attend <margin>G4 Wisdom</margin> upon True Wisdom. If Trithemius pays attention, he will see that true Wisdom is always depicted wearing a woman's garment; for nothing is more praiseworthy than the purity of a virgin. God in His judgment knows how Trithemius has been rewarded. <margin>G5 Trithemius's reward</margin>

If you think these arguments are not sufficient—the one regarding the fundamental basis, and the other regarding the significance of my name—I will offer even greater ones.

**Dee [$\Delta$]:** These arguments satisfy me. However, to have the means to silence others who might use petty objections <term>cavillation</term> <note>original: "cavillation" – the use of frivolous or deceptive objections</note> regarding such matters, it would be quite helpful to hear your...

<meta>This page continues a spiritual revelation or angelic communication, likely from the journals of John Dee and Edward Kelley, focusing on the nature of the soul, divine judgment, and the necessity of spiritual vigilance.</meta>

In this is the power spread of the greatest working in all creatures. For just as there is a particular soul or fire inflaming every body (I mean those that are rational), so there is a universal fire and a general brightness giving light to them all. This light is but one and shines through the whole; indeed, it has been measured equally unto every thing from the beginning. The life of all things is known here: the reward of death to those who are rewarded for life <note>This likely refers to the "wages of sin" or the spiritual outcome of one's earthly life</note>. None are rewarded except according to their deserts, of which there are two kinds: 
1. These are rewarded with death for their wickedness. 
2. So are they rewarded with life for their constant living <note>original: "constant living," meaning steadfastness in faith or righteousness</note>. 

Amongst the angels there may be error, and sin may make them fall from the brightness of their glory. But to the soul of man (once it is glorified), sin is utterly—indeed, most extensively—opposite. Neither shall that dignity ever be lost, stained, or defaced, which is obtained here through the works of righteousness and true wisdom. Whatsoever has existed from the beginning (since it was said in Divine Determination <note>original: "Divine Determination," referring to the Latin *Fiat*, "Let it be done"</note>, "Be it done") is enclosed here. 

Therefore, this day should be hallowed and sanctified before the Lord by you. For if the prophets worshipped this day of his ascension, much more ought you—who have tasted of the first things and shall now taste of the secrets of his judgments—glorify his coming. But Satan is busy with you; his bristles stand up, and his feathers are spread out. <margin>G3</margin> Therefore watch and pray; for those who go to banquets put on their wedding garments <note>original: "upper garments," an allusion to the Parable of the Wedding Feast in Matthew 22</note>. 

Amongst you, therefore, there is no sound belief, nor do you consider the scope of this blessedness. But such is the greatness and excellency of God's foreknowledge that he suffers the enemy to carry a burden—yes, sometimes even to preach upon a stage. For it is said, "He shall triumph until the end, and place himself here as he would have done above"; neither shall he be thrust out of doors until the end is determined. 

Therefore watch and pray, and look about with diligence; for those things shall be opened unto you which have not been disclosed even unto the Holy Ones. Oh, how hard a thing it is for flesh <term>flesh: human nature or the physical body, often seen as prone to sin</term> to continue in the works of justice! Yes, oh how hard a thing it is for Wisdom to be acquainted with a hotchpotch of filthiness? Cleanse your garments, lift up your hearts, and tear your faults in pieces, so that there may be one heart with one consent, and toward one end, unto him who is One and the end of all things. To him be praise for and in his truth, and for the greatness of his mercies, forever. Amen. 

**E.K.** <note>Edward Kelley, John Dee's medium or "scryer"</note> All the while she spoke, there came a bright beam from the mystical stone <note>The "shew-stone" or crystal ball used for scrying</note> to her body, and at the end, she mounted upward and disappeared.

This is the true fear of God; and when we fear sin, we do so because we hate it. When we strive to do good, it is a sign of our fear, in that it shows we fear him whom we love, and for whose honor we strive to do well. This is all that can be said of living and lifeless fear.

### Saturday, June 22. Afternoon, around 6:00 PM.

Upon perusing and examining this prayer that Gabriel revealed to us, I found certain imperfections and some doubts. We thought it good to ask counsel and require Gabriel's advice, so that the prayer might be perfect and pleasing to him, for God's honor and our comfort. 

At length: nothing appeared to the eye, but there was the noise of a sound about E.K.'s <note>Edward Kelley</note> head, and with it a mighty weight or visible burden on his right shoulder as he sat in the green chair by the holy Table. To certain places of the prayer which I noted and repeated, these words and answers were given by Gabriel:

**Gabriel:** The Preface must be included; for if our hearts are not prepared for prayer, our prayers are in vain. Why do you delay, O Lord? Strengthen my heart for the better. Through you and in your name I shall rise again; that is, Hallelujah. <note>original: "Quid differs Domine, Cor meum in melius Comfortare. Per te et in nomine tuo resurgam; id est, Halleluja."</note> The first way is more effectual. Say "My Angel," <note>original: "Angele mee"</note> but the other is more effectual: "Care for me, making me whole." <note>original: "Cura me sanum."</note> Regard me, and look unto me, being whole.

**John Dee:** Concerning the inscription which I have written before the prayer: I would gladly know whether it is to your liking.

**Gabriel:** Let all things be done to the praise of God. <note>original: "Fiant omnia ad laudem Dei."</note> My own doings are of no such importance. What I have done is done; so long as your additions are to the honor of God, it is sufficient. The effect of his prayer is greater than the form. The Creator <note>term: "Former"</note> is greater than the thing formed. That is to say, he who has formed it is mightier than any virtue in which it is formed. Wheresoever, therefore, the mind forms it within you with perfect humility and consent, there also is the Creator. As you are formed by him, therefore, I leave you to the end of his workmanship, which continually forms all things according to his own fashion.

**Sins:** Your sins have banished me from saying the things I would.

**John Dee:** O cleanse our hearts, and wash away our sins. Wash me yet more from my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin. <note>original: "amplius lava me ab iniquitate mea et a peccato meo munda me."</note>

**Gabriel:** Sins are never washed away or forgotten by the Highest, except for those who are sorry and also make satisfaction. <note>term: "satisfaction" refers to the theological concept of making amends for sin.</note>

**John Dee:** O Lord, I am full sorry for my sins, and whatever satisfaction is required, I would gladly...

know. Gabriel: ... The offense was not yours. Everyone must make satisfaction <note>original: "satisfie"</note>, or else he shall be damned.

Δ: Good Lord, expound to us the mystery of satisfaction.

Gabriel: ... When the Soul offends and consents to wickedness, he is then to make a spiritual satisfaction, which is the end and perfect fruit of Contrition <note>Sincere repentance or remorse for sins.</note>. For those who are truly contrite do truly satisfy. There is another satisfaction which is external. This satisfaction is to be made for sins committed against your neighbor. For if you offend your neighbor and do him wrong, or take anything from him by fraud or violence, it is a great sin. For this, you can never be contrite if you do not make satisfaction—not only confessing it, but satisfying the desires of the one who is offended, and doing so with sorrow. This is true doctrine and shall never be overthrown by the spirits of false invention, which indeed is the first eye of the Devil. If you may offend your brother and be therefore accursed, how much more shall you be accursed when you offend the messenger of him who is your Father? Behold, he says not, "I have once done amiss." May God be merciful to you, so that his mercies might be the greater upon you. Be mindful of my sayings.

(Based on my former promises to him) I told him that I would then guarantee him fifty pounds yearly. #### Thursday, July 4, 11:00 AM, 1583.

Note. When I came home yesterday from the Court, and from London, and from the Lord Laskie <note>Albertus Laski, a Polish nobleman visiting Dee.</note>, I found that E.K. was purposed to ride out of town and intended to be away (as he expressly told me) for five days. Certain companions and his acquaintances had arranged this with him, some waiting for him in Mortlake and some at Brentford <note>original: *Brainford*</note> (as was perceived later today, and as he confessed to me). 

Whereupon I thought it good to notify the Lord Laskie, who meant to come and refresh himself at my house as he was accustomed to do before, either today or within two or three days after. Because he also delighted in E.K., I wrote these lines, intending to send them immediately to the Lord Laskie so that word might be returned of his intent before E.K. should ride; I meant and hoped to persuade E.K. to stay that long for that reason.

> Most Noble Prince, upon my return, I found our Edward with a happy face, but nevertheless preparing himself for a journey of five days, as he says. And at this morning hour, he is attempting to begin that departure or journey, intending to return (as he affirms) after five days. What the truth itself is, only our Almighty God knows. I wanted to signify this to you very early this morning so that you might consider what is best to be done. Concerning other matters, in their own time. Your Highness's most faithful humble client, July 4, 1583. John Dee.

The meaning is this: whereas you said that you intended to return within five days, or at the end of those same days, it is uncertain whether you will, or shall, return later or sooner. Therefore, <note>original: "Quid sit ipsa veritas"</note> what the actual truth is regarding your return, or your intent to return, only God knows. He <note>Edward Kelley</note> would by no means accept my sincere explanation, but seemed suspicious of some other improper interpretations of those former words. Thereupon, I took the letter and tore it into three pieces and sent nothing. But in my mind, I referred all things to God’s disposition, assuring myself of God’s most constant proceeding in His own affairs.

Shortly after, the said E.K. said to me, "Certainly there is a spiritual creature on my right <margin>Sowle. Evil spirits.</margin> shoulder, who perceptibly says to me, 'Come away.'"

"So," said I, "did one say to Sowle <note>A person previously mentioned in Dee's diaries who was plagued by spirits</note> when they would have had him go away to drown himself. I restrained him in this study by force, and so hindered the Devil of his purpose then, as is shown by that unhappy man who is yet alive."

"Nay," said E.K., "they have told me that if I stay here, I shall be hanged; and if I go with this Prince, he will cut off my head; and that you do not mean to keep your promise with me. And therefore, even if I might have a thousand pounds to stay—yes, even a kingdom—I cannot. Therefore, I release <margin>Fifty pound yearly stipend.</margin> you of your promise of a 50-pound yearly stipend <note>A fixed regular salary</note> to me. You need not doubt that God will defend you and prosper you, and can from the very stones raise up children to Abraham <note>A biblical reference to God's omnipotence from Matthew 3:9</note>. And again, I cannot abide my wife; I do not love her; no, I abhor her. And there in the house I am disliked <margin>E.K.'s wife.</margin> because I do not treat her better."

To these words of his, spoken in great pangs and disquietness of mind, I replied and said that these doings and sayings of his were not of God. I told him that by my whole proceeding he might perceive what confidence I placed in his dealings with the spirits, our friends, seeing that even to the very last penny (and more than my ability conveniently allowed), I continually spent money on the preparation of such things as I was required to do, and so forth.

Well, suddenly, down he went; he got upon his mare and rode away toward <margin>E.K. is marvelously out of quiet.</margin> Brentford. After his departure, my wife came up into my study, and I said, "Jane, this man is marvelously unsettled against his wife because of her friends' bitter reports against him behind his back, and her silence regarding them, and so forth. He is gone," said I, "but I beseech Almighty God to guide him and to defend him from danger and shame. I do not doubt but that God will be merciful to him and bring him at length to such order that he shall be a faithful servant unto God," and so forth.

Note: within three hours after, E.K. came up my study stairs without his riding boots, for he had returned in a boat.

From Brentford <note>original: "Brainford"</note>. When I saw him, I was very glad inwardly; but I remained writing those records which I still had to finish regarding last Tuesday's actions. He took up in his hand the books which I had brought from London concerning Lord Laskie <note>Albertus Laski, a Polish nobleman and patron of Dee</note>, written to him in his commendation, and so forth. I heard the strikes myself several times. At length, Edward Kelley said, "I see the handsome maiden Madimi here, and have for a good while."

# THE FIRST BOOK OF THE JOURNEY:
### Namely, from Mortlake in England to Kraków in Poland.

**Saturday, September 21, 1583. The Feast of Saint Matthew.**

We departed from Mortlake <note>Dee’s home in Surrey</note> about three o'clock in the afternoon. The Lord Albert Lasky (Voivode <note>original: Vaywode; a high-ranking governor or prince</note> of Sieradz in Poland) met me on the water as we had appointed. We reached London by nightfall, and in the dead of night, we traveled by wherry boats to Greenwich to the house of my friend Goodman Fern the potter. There we refreshed ourselves, and a large tilt-boat <note>a large rowboat with a canopy</note> came from Gravesend to pick us up (as arranged by myself and Mr. Stanley) to take us to our ships, which we had ordered to lie seven or eight miles beyond Gravesend.

We reached those ships on Sunday morning at sunrise. My Lord Lasky, myself, and E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s medium and assistant</note>, along with my wife and children, etc., went in the larger of them (which was a double fly-boat <note>a fast, flat-bottomed Dutch vessel</note> from Denmark). In another ship, which I also hired for this passage, went some of my Lord’s men, two horses, etc.; that ship was a "boyer," a very pretty vessel. With a light wind, we immediately hoisted sail and began our voyage in the ship.

<margin>September 22</margin> This 22nd day, we were in great danger of perishing on the sands called the Spits <note>sandbanks in the Thames Estuary</note> around midnight. Due to a contrary wind, we had anchored near them, but the anchor "came home" <note>the anchor failed to grip the seabed and dragged</note> without anyone noticing until the ship was ready to strike the sands. Then, through the great diligence and skill used by our mariners in hoisting sail and cutting our cable (leaving our sheet anchor behind), and committing ourselves into the hands of God and most earnestly praying for a favorable wind, it pleased the Almighty and most merciful God suddenly to change the wind. This allowed us to steer away from the sands and return to Queenborough <note>original: Quinborrough</note>.

<margin>September 23</margin> On the 23rd day (being Monday), we arrived at the mouth and entrance of Queenborough Creek, or Haven. As we headed for land in small fishing boats—Lord Lasky, my wife, and children in one boat, and I with E.K., Mary, Elizabeth, and John Crokar in another—it so happened that at the ship's side, our fishing boat's sail-yard and sail became entangled with the main-yard of the fly-boat (which had been lowered). 

As we moved away from the ship's side, the top of our boat was held fast above while the wind and current pushed the boat away below. It tilted so far to one side that nearly half the fishing boat was underwater. The water poured in because of the entanglement mentioned before (which was not easily undone or loosened), so that my Lord, my wife, and everyone who saw us thought our boat must inevitably sink and that we would perish. 

But God, in His providence and mercy, had greater [care] for us, so that we broke clear. The boat was half full of water, so that we sat wet to our knees, and the waves of the sea kept beating in more and more. In the midst of this trouble, one of our two boatmen lost his long oar out of the boat into the...

Saturday, September 28, we reached the coast of Holland, and none of our mariners, master, nor pilot knew the coast. At Brielle, October 2, at 9:00 in the morning, Wednesday. 

**E.K.** Nothing appears in the stone <note>the crystal used for scrying</note>, neither the curtain nor anything else. Let us pray constantly, etc.

**Gabriel:** ...... And hereby I teach you, that those afflictions which you suffer in soul—either for your offenses toward God, or for the imperfections of your minds, being void of brotherly charity toward your neighbors; (and so from you generally hereafter, how great or how many soever)—ought not to be manifested or made open to the world. Instead, they should be perfectly shadowed in charity, bearing your own infirmities, and so the infirmity of others with a quiet and hidden mind. 

For the anguish of the soul is compared with prayer, dwelling in one house which ought to laugh with the world, and to weep toward heaven. For every sin is noted, and the least thing—as well among the celestial bodies as the terrestrial—is perfectly considered. For sin has its end, and its end is punishment. And so, conversely, of virtue. 

Wisdom (in the twenty-first <term>Entry</term> or <term>Lesson</term>) has its ground upon mildness <note>original: "mildnesse"; here meaning gentleness or humility</note>, which mildness purifies the body and exalts the soul, making it apt and ready to behold the heavens, receive glorious illuminations, and finally brings the soul to participate with us in—not earthly, but everlasting—wisdom. 

The Son of God was sanctified in his flesh through mildness, and was not of this world because he was the mildness of his Father. Therefore be you meek: be fervent in meekness. Then shall you take up that cross which Christ spoke of, following him: which cross is the compassion in mildness over your brothers, for sin’s sake—not as worldlings do, looking but not lamenting. The other part is in suffering mildly the afflictions of the world and flesh: hereby you become martyrs for that you...

Mortify yourselves, which is true martyrdom <note>original: "mortifie your selves"; in this context, to "mortify" means to practice self-discipline and overcome physical desires</note>. He who forsakes the world for the love of God, in his Son Christ, shall have his reward. But he who forsakes himself shall be crowned with a diadem of glory. Thus says the Lord: I am jealous over you because you have vowed yourselves unto me. But great are the temptations of the flesh, and mighty is its strength where the spirit is weak.

But thus says God: It is better to fill up the soul with heavenly contemplation and celestial food, to reign in heaven and to be beloved of him, than to pamper the filthy flesh, whose delight destroys both body and soul. It is written: He who does not bridle his flesh is given to riotousness <note>original: "riotousnesse"; meaning unrestrained or dissolute living</note>, which is the sleep of death and the slumber toward destruction. But this is true abstinence: when, scorning the world, you flee from the delights within it, refraining from the pleasures of the body, tempering the flesh and making it weak, and doing so for the Lord’s sake. For the flesh and the spirit do not rejoice at the same time. Neither can a full belly groan out true prayers. Feed the soul, therefore, with the love of our society. And bridle your flesh, for it is insolent.

One thing I say: look to your servants. See that in one house there do not dwell those who delight in virtue and holiness mingled with such as harbor vice upon vice—those whose drunkenness is an abomination and whose diet stirs up fornication. For wickedness is among them; they do not fear God, nor do they abstain according to what the Holy Ghost has taught through his Church. Make them clean; then you shall feel our presence among you. And we will all defend you from the rage of wickedness. We delight in the God of truth and in the worshippers of justice.

Thus says the Holy Ghost: "Behold, I have made myself a tabernacle where the God of gods reigns in justice. And I will sanctify those places which rejoice in charity." Mingle your alms <note>charitable donations or acts of mercy</note> with charity, therefore. And let your prayers and fasting be mingled with deeds of alms. For he who prays and fastes without mercy is a liar. Moreover, let your friendship be such as comes from charity and not from this world—neither for the world's sake, but for the service of God. All other friendship is vain and of no account. Charity is the gift of the Holy Ghost, which is a kindling fire, knitting things together through Jesus Christ in the true wisdom of the Father. This fire is of no small account, nor is it to be thought of as the heathens <note>non-Christians or pagans</note> have done. For happy are those who are fed with charity. For it is the food of us who are anointed, which is the Son of God and the light of the world.

<meta>This page continues a spiritual discourse regarding the nature of redemption, the responsibilities of the faithful servant, and the necessity of holiness in worship.</meta>

Think of him who has entered into your weakness and weighed out his blood for your **Redemption** <note>original: "Redemption"; the act of being saved from sin</note>. He is the one who has paid the very last penny of your ransom. And why? Not so that you should brag about yourselves, but he has commanded, as a condition, that you should maintain justice through works of **Righteousness**. 

To whom is Heaven a seat? Only to those who are faithful servants. In this, the dignity of your Master is known, of whom it is said, "Blessed are those that serve the **God of Hosts** <note>original: "God of Hosts"; a title for God as commander of heavenly armies</note>." If anything now happens to you that adds to the riches of your Master, be thankful for it and consider his liberality. The more he opens his treasures to you, be that much more thankful; for to such people belongs the ownership of more, and the reward of those who are ten times faithful. Happy are those to whom it is said, "You good servant." 

Do not be wanderers <note>original: "Gadders"; those who roam restlessly</note>, for there is no house like the house of your Master. Take heed also, lest you provide his bread to those who are his enemies and are therefore unworthy; for to both of these <note>the wanderer and the unworthy recipient</note> belongs the reward of unfaithfulness. Do not be proud when you borrow your riches, lest the moths enter in and corrupt your garments; for pride is the depth of sin. 

Do not cease to rebuke those who dishonor him, nor maintain the honor of any other. For he who entertains you has sealed you for others and has strengthened you with authority—the rod of his justice. Generally, these things have been spoken to you, and these lessons are not yet fully learned. But happy are those whom God sanctifies, they being previously unholy; and ten times blessed are the temples wherein his holiness dwells. 

It is true as you say: generally, men are sanctified—the people of the Earth through all nations—mystically through the mercies of God. But where the **sanctification** <note>the process of being made holy</note> does not agree with the thing being sanctified, wickedness enters there. The Spirit of God is not sanctified in Hell, nor is his holy temple beautified by the feet of the unrighteous. It is written, "Dogs do not honor bread, nor do defiled places honor things that are holy." For just as Hell dishonors Heaven in respect to unrighteousness, so those who are wicked dishonor the virtuous and those who are truly holy by their company; they stink of their wickedness. For it is written, "And Satan went from the presence of the Lord, leaving a stink behind him." 

The light of the Sun is taken from the Earth by the frozen cloud. The sins of the people and the filthiness of places are put between virtue and **Sacramental** <note>sacred or holy</note> things. Therefore, it is not true that you may lawfully call upon the name of God in unhallowed places.

**Δ** <note>The Greek letter Delta, likely representing a specific speaker in this dialogue</note>: I crave pardon for my ignorance and error in this. The servants of God: Not for your own sakes, but because it is the glory of him who has called you <note>original: "G1" - likely a reference to a specific spiritual grade or gathering</note> to this exercise—which is troublesome to the world, but rewarded with glory. If, therefore, your imperfections rise up and resist the will of God, saying blasphemously as you do, "Let us seek other ways," then you are not counted as those who persevere, nor are your works worthy of reward. Even human reason can persuade and give judgment against these follies; how much more are they damnable and deserving of correction in the voice and judgment of those who are pure? He who deals with the wicked is a liar and shall have his reward, but the end of comfort is found in the purity of the spirit.

But oh, you of little wisdom! You rise up against the winds and yoke your wits against the mountains. No, you cast yourselves down headlong where there is no mercy. For what blasphemy is it to say, "If it be the will of God, it must follow"? Is not man subject to the results of his own labors? And are they not allowed for his comfort once they are brought forth? 

The soul of man is the image of God, made after his form, which keeps within itself the power of his divinity in the heavenly spirit. By this, man has the authority to consent with God in the workmanship of his will and his creatures. This power, being already sealed, gives to man (as king of himself) the ability to consent to his own salvation—joining and knitting himself together either with perseverance in the assured hope of mercy, or (with willful drunkenness) to the reward of those who fall. 

Therefore, become holy. For the soul beautifies itself when it is beautified within. Resist not the will of God, which is mighty upon you; do not be obstinate. Be humble. Do not rejoice for this world, but be glad that your names are sealed and that you shall correct the world. Do not despair through weakness, for from whom does strength come? If puddles become seas, the end is more wonderful; but it is even greater when sinners are called to the knowledge and performance of God's will through his mercies. 

Just as one day perishes and is no more, even though it once existed, so it is and shall be the state of this world. And Jerusalem <note>original: "Herusalem"</note> shall descend with a horn of glory to the end. The sun and moon shall be witnesses and wonder at their own stopping. Of you, [pointing to **E.K.**] thus says the Lord: <margin>G4</margin> You are flesh and have become stubborn. Your judgment grows dull and your heart is sealed. Angels: After (I say) more than half an hour of waiting, E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s medium or "scryer"</note> seemed to feel and thought he felt something about his head, as if it were clawed with hawks' claws. Honor God in his messengers of truth. In our doctrine, nothing is taught but the state of the world, both here and to come. It contains the prophecies of time and the gathering together of God's mysteries, opened from time to time to those who are his sanctified ones. ### The Knowledge of God’s Creatures

Unto me are delivered five parts of a time, wherein I will open, teach, and uncover the secrets of that speech—that holy mystery—to the intent that the *Cabala* <term>Cabala: here referring to a mystical or secret tradition of divine knowledge</term> of nature may be known in voice, physical substance, and measure in all its parts. For there is nothing secret that shall not be revealed, and the Son of God shall be known in power and establish a kingdom with righteousness on the earth, and then comes the end. The word of God endures forever. His promises are just. His spirit is truth. His judgments are inscrutable <term>inscrutable: impossible to understand or interpret</term>. He himself is universal. ### Saturday, February 22, 1584, Before Noon. Lasko.
### (March 3, New Style)

**John Dee:** The questions necessary to be asked of Madimi:

1. Good counsel for recovering and confirming my health.
2. If the pedestal (for the Holy Table) being made here should be carried with us to Cracow, rather than making a new one there—both to save time and to keep our activities more secret?
3. What is your knowledge and judgment of Albert Laski's wife, in respect to her life past, present, and to come? For we doubt she is a true friend to us.
4. It is our very earnest desire that the Danish Treasure in England, in the ten places (located by Edward Kelley), might be brought here very speedily. By this, Albert Laski might redeem the mortgaged lands of Keysmark and Lasko, and also pay his debts in and around Cracow. For otherwise, he can neither come to Cracow with any credit (as he is commanded), nor can he come to us there as conveniently and often as our conferences may require. Thirdly, the day of the forfeiture of Keysmark (without the Emperor's favorable help) draws near, specifically on St. George's Day this coming April.

**John Dee:** And by your speech of England, you give me occasion to inquire whether her Majesty <note>Queen Elizabeth I</note> causes my rents to be received by my assigned deputy or not? Your knowledge is not merely to possess, but to learn to [understand?], so that you may be both possessing and learned. 

Small are the treasures of this world in respect to the wisdom that judges **NATURE**. For to him who judges truly, what secret is hidden? Those who seek the world shall be despised by it; but he who flies from the world shall use her as a slave, or as a stepmother <note>original: "second mother"</note> does her daughter. Nevertheless, for my part, I will be more compliant toward you than you shall be followers of me. For that reason, I have become like a child. Therefore, cease: He is truly <margin>G1</margin> wise who says, "God knows at all times what we have need of." Do not be tempters. Be patient. 

5. Even as your desire is, so are all things in England. Nothing is kept back. But for your sake, those who are yours are treated friendly by them. 

6. If you should not be called home, how should you enjoy the benefit of God's promise, which has said: "You shall call her back to her preservation." But first, these things must come to pass: The country shall be divided, one rising up against another. Great treasons shall be committed. Yes, and people shall cut one another's throats. And when the greatest troubles occur, then shall you save her life. Then shall the wall be broken down, and free passage shall be made. And those who are scorners, and those who ascend the narrow steps or show themselves on the walls, shall be trodden down and defaced. Here is understanding.

That which you, Edward Kelley, have, is a part of four and has become the fifth; yet it is none of the four, dignified in a cube whose root is 252. I will know it shortly. You have no power yet (for the time has not yet come), but it must be brought forth shortly, so that it may be...

<summary>The spirit Madimi offers a discourse on the dangers of unrefined knowledge and provides a prophetic warning regarding civil strife and future treasons in England. She promises that John Dee will eventually return home to save a woman's life (likely Queen Elizabeth I) during a time of great upheaval.</summary>

But immediately after that, the servant's messenger [returned].

The father of the household came, and he looked, but his servant was not there. And he sent for him and commanded him to be [seized] and to be brought with violence. But the servant said, "Do not deal with me this way, for it is violent." But the master answered and said: "I command you... for servants have no freedom of themselves." And it came to pass that after the master had gathered together his friends, he said unto them, "Arise, and find me one who is **FAITHFUL** with **OBEDIENCE**." Then he stretched out his hand, and he said unto his servant: "Hold, take your reward; for you are banished from me." How say you, was this justice that he did unto his servant?

# THE MYSTIC SABBATH MONTH
## The first part of the same.
### Tuesday morning, Year 1584. April 10, New Style Gregorian.
### AT KRAKOW.

After our various prayers and the declaration of our humility, obedience, and faith in these actions; and having now come to Krakow, the sanctified place where we were commanded to hurry, etc. At length appeared Nalvage <note>An angelic being in Dee's spiritual system</note>.

**Edward Kelley:** He has a gown of white silk, with a cape with three pendants with tassels on the ends of them, all green. It is fur, white, and seems to shine with a wavering, glittering light. On his head is nothing; he has no beard. His face <note>original: "physiognomy"</note> is like the picture of King Edward the Sixth; his hair hangs down a quarter of the length of the cape, somewhat curling and yellow. He has a rod or wand in his hand, almost as big as my little finger; it is of gold, and divided into three equal parts with a brighter gold than the rest. He stands upon his round table of crystal, or rather mother-of-pearl. There appear an infinite number of letters on the same, as thick as one can stand by another. The table is somewhat tilted on one side; he stands in the very middle; his garment covers his feet. His breast seems smooth as the down remaining on a swan when all the feathers are off; so is his neck, etc. He is lean and long-faced.

**Dee:** The infinite mercies of God be on us; and the light of his countenance shine on us; and his favorable countenance be on us.

**Nalvage:** ...... Amen, unto him that is, and was, and lives forever.

**Edward Kelley:** He looks earnestly on his table and turns himself to view it.

**Nalvage:** ...... All things are in order. Thus—

<meta>This page continues the spiritual exhortation and angelic communication typical of the Enochian manuscripts, emphasizing the unworthiness of the human participants compared to the divine grace being offered.</meta>

So says the Messenger of him who is the God of Wisdom. Is your worthiness such that you can merit so great a mercy? Or are your vessels cleansed and made fit to receive and hold the sweet liquor—pure understanding itself? <note>The "vessels" refer to the souls or minds of the practitioners; the "sweet liquor" is a metaphor for divine knowledge.</note> [delta]. Has the Sun entered into your bowels, or have you tasted of the night-dew? Where are your wedding garments, or in what way do you provide for your marriage? <note>A reference to the Parable of the Wedding Feast (Matthew 22), symbolizing spiritual readiness for union with the divine.</note> You are unseasoned and withered flesh, yet you are partakers of those things which make you holy. Through this participation and the secret providence of him who is the Highest, you became dignified for this purpose and are sufficiently washed for the time of entrance. 

O stiff-necked <term>stubborn or obstinate</term> people, you deserve nothing, and yet you have the wages of those who labor. But how can corruption be a partaker of those things that are incorruptible? Or how can man, who only perceives worldly things within himself, also perceive the Almighty? O you weaklings, O you of no faith, O you cankers <term>spreading sores or blights</term> of the earth! Where is the shame you should have? Where are the tears you let fall? Where is the humility you are taught? Instead, you are the kind who say in your hearts, "If the spring is fair, the harvest is likely to be good; if these things come to pass, it is the finger of the Lord." Such is your imperfection, such are the fruits of the flesh and the vanity of mortality. 

Nevertheless, consider that you are servants: therefore, do the will of your Master. You have become free: be faithful and thankful to him who is the giver of liberty. Indeed, you have become children: partakers of the counsel of him who sits and sees, and says, "I am." <note>original: "Ego Sum" (implied biblical reference to the divine name).</note> Therefore be sober, faithful, and do not waver, for the inheritance of your Father is great; your freedom is given without cost, and your Master is the King of Justice.

Where are the people, or in what generation did they dwell, who have been so well-acquainted and drawn into familiarity with the true servants and angels of God? To whom have these mysteries been opened? Is it not said of those who are sanctified, "The Lord appeared to them in a vision"? But he comes to you while you are awake. To them he came unexpectedly; to you he comes because he was requested. 

Rise up, therefore, and do not be forgetful of what the Lord has done for you; for <margin>G1</margin> the things of this world do not truly exist until they are done, nor is anything certain until the end. It was said to Abraham, "And I will destroy them." He believed it, but he did not ask "when?" Great is the reward of faith, for it gives strength; but those who are faithful are not of this world. Nevertheless, you have said (just as the disciples said to Christ when they were still impure and blind), "When shall these things come to pass? Lord, what is meant by <margin>G2</margin> this or that?" Simple faith excels...

<summary>An angelic messenger rebukes the human participants for their lack of humility and faith, contrasting their direct access to divine mysteries with the veiled visions given to holy figures of the past.</summary>

appeared. <note>E.K. refers to Edward Kelley, John Dee’s scryer or medium.</note> E.K.: They have real eyes which twinkle just as other men's eyes do, and <margin>G5</margin> therefore I see them with my physical eye, not within my imagination, as... <note>original: "Cracoviæ"</note>

After various prayers <note>original: "Ejaculations"</note> appropriate to the action, and while the curtain of white water still remained, E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee's scryer.</note> thought several times that he saw through the white veil, the stone and all, with nothing appearing within it. E.K. immediately fell into a new state of doubting the truth of these actions. He said he had a vision from a good creature last night, who said these creatures with whom we dealt would no longer appear to him. 

Upon this, he said that both the "scorner" from the previous days and these current instructors were all devils, and that he would no longer sit to receive the alphabet <note>original: "A.B.C."</note> or any doctrine of theirs by letters, unless they would otherwise expressly and vividly deliver a plain rule for it. He used many other arguments to disprove the truth of our actions, whereupon he said, "John your boy can deliver you their letters well enough, and so you do not need me," etc. 

I referred everything to God, His will, and His mercies. For, as I had requested wisdom and true knowledge from His hands only, by His order, and for His service, I do not doubt that God will—according to His accustomed goodness—provide for me what is best for my calling <note>original: "vocation"</note> here on earth, etc. E.K. rose and went away, leaving me alone in my study, as appointed.

for these actions. O God, come to my assistance; O Lord, make haste to help me. <note>original: "Deus in adjutorium meum intende, Domine ad adjuvandum me festina." This is the opening of the Roman Catholic Liturgy of the Hours.</note> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. <note>original: "Gloria Patri and Filio and Spiritui Sancto, sicut erat in principio and nunc and semper and in secula seculorum."</note> Amen.

Thursday, around 9:00 AM. As I was in my upper study, I had gathered the holy words of the second and third calls <note>The "calls" or "keys" were poetic incantations in the Enochian language</note> and had compared them with the English translations delivered to us. E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s scryer or medium</note> came up the stairs and went into his study, then came out again. As he was going down the stairs, I opened my study door and greeted him. He then came back up and entered my study.

There, I showed him what I had done and how I had gained some understanding of those holy words and their meanings by carefully applying the English translation to the word of Christ. <note>original: "Christus"</note> I intended to persuade E.K. to better appreciate the orderly and methodical way our "friends" <note>The angels or spiritual beings Dee believed he was communicating with</note> were proceeding with us. I told him that unless I received this strange language letter by letter, we might make mistakes in spelling <note>term: Orthography</note>; furthermore, without the true pronunciation of the words and the correct punctuation, we might fail to achieve the expected results.

But just as he did last Tuesday, he said again that our teachers were deceivers and were not good or capable instructors, since they had not made us able to understand or accomplish anything in two years' time. He claimed that he could have learned all the seven liberal sciences <note>The traditional medieval curriculum: grammar, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy</note> in two years if he had first learned logic, and so on. Therefore, he said he would have nothing more to do with them in any way. He wished himself back in England and said that if these books were his, he would burn them immediately. He also mentioned that he had written to my Lord <note>likely Albertus Laski, their patron</note> (via Pirmis) stating that he believed our teachers to be deceivers and wicked, and not good creatures of God. He used many such speeches and arguments which he thought were strong enough to justify his refusal to deal with them any longer.

He urged me to use my boy, John, as my scryer <note>term: Skryer; a person who looks into a crystal ball or mirror to see visions</note> instead, because these spiritual creatures were not bound to him. I answered all these points and arguments as time allowed, declaring my perfect trust in God. I explained that since I have for many years desired and prayed to God for wisdom (of the kind these actions involve), and sought it by whatever means seemed best to His Divine Majesty, God would not dislike my prayer or betray my constant hope in His goodness and mercy. Therefore, I concluded that I referred everything to the merciful will of God and did not doubt that my requests and prayers would eventually be satisfied.

So he left me for the second time. May God enlighten his heart with the knowledge of the truth, if it be His divine will and pleasure.

<note>Note: Pirmis left last Wednesday morning, having received our letters on Tuesday afternoon. But on the Monday before, the wicked Prince of Darkness did what he could to hinder our progress.</note>

<meta>This page continues the record of spiritual conferences held in Krakow, involving John Dee (represented by the Greek letter delta), Edward Kelley (E.K.), and the angelic beings Gabriel and Nalvage.</meta>

News came to Krakow <note>original: "Cracovia"</note> that my Lord Lasky <note>Albertus Laski, a Polish nobleman and patron of Dee and Kelley</note> was coming toward Krakow. Emericus came from Kesmark and returned back again. Tabius rode from Krakow toward Kesmark.

### Saturday, April 21, Afternoon

After our prayers were made, Gabriel and Nalvage appeared shortly. E.K. proposed six questions in order, which had caused great doubt in his mind, and requested their answers.

[delta] <note>John Dee</note>. He would have our spiritual friends promise him the performance of the Prints <note>likely referring to the spiritual or alchemical results promised by the angels</note>.

**Gabriel:** If we were masters of our own actions, we might well promise; but we are servants and do the will of our Master. But let me ask you one question: Do you not think that all things are possible with God?

**E.K.:** I do think so, and I know so.

**Gabriel:** Then there is no cause why you should distrust. Let him who is a servant and is commanded to go, go; and let not the earth rise up and strive against the plowman. What sin is it when the creature rises up and says in his heart, "Let the Lord make a covenant with me," considering he is a bondman?

[E.K. says: Both voices seem to come to my ear at once.]

**Gabriel:** None but he who becomes disobedient and refuses his Master.

[delta] would do so.

**Gabriel and Nalvage:** These things—that is to say, this doctrine delivered by us—are from God and granted to you by His mercies, which cannot be in vain; and therefore they are to be performed. For the secret determinations of God are unknown to us. He never heard of any man who would ask if God would perform His promises.

**E.K.:** By August next?

**Gabriel:** What if it were a hundred Augusts? You may be weary before next August, just as the children of Israel were weary of their Manna.

**E.K.:** Why do you join numbers with these letters, and added none to those of the former Table?

**Gabriel:** Brother, what is the cause that all the world is made by numbers? The numbers we speak of are of reason and form, and not the numbers of merchants.

[delta]. I beseech you concerning the powder, of which he <note>Kelley</note> thinks he has made a proper assay <note>a test of metal or ore for purity</note>, as if it should have been the Philosopher's Stone <note>the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold</note>, and was affirmed to be so by the minister of this action? I beseech you to answer this so that his reason may be satisfied.

[delta]. They gave no answer to this, but proceeded in the former matter of numbers.

**Gabriel:** Every letter signifies a member of the substance of which it speaks. Every word signifies the essence <note>original: "quiddity," a philosophical term for the inherent nature or "whatness" of a thing</note> of the substance. The letters are separated and in confusion; therefore, they are gathered together by numbers. These gathered letters also signify a number; for as every greater thing contains its lesser parts, so are the secret and unknown forms of things knit up in their origins <note>original: "parents"</note>. When these are known in number, they are easily distinguished; so that in this, we teach places to be numbered.

Kelley expresses skepticism about the timing of their success and inquires about the nature of a powder he believes to be the Philosopher's Stone.</summary>

<meta>This page continues a dialogue between the angelic entity Gabriel and the medium Edward Kelley (E.K.), facilitated by John Dee, regarding the origins and power of a primordial language.</meta>

Letters are to be chosen from the numbered forms, and proper words from those letters, which substantially signify the thing spoken of in the center of its Creator. Just as the human mind is moved by orderly speech and is easily persuaded by truths, so are the creatures of God stirred up within themselves when they hear the words by which they were nourished and brought forth. For nothing moves that is not persuaded, and nothing can be persuaded of that which is unknown. 

<margin>Understanding, Persuasion, Motion.</margin> The creatures of God do not understand you; you are not of their cities. You have become enemies because you are separated by ignorance from Him who governs the city. 

**E.K.:** Is this language known in any part of the world or not? If it is, where and to whom? 

**Gabriel:** When man was first created as an innocent, he was authorized and made a partaker of the power and spirit of God. Because of this, he not only knew all things within his creation and spoke of them properly—naming them as they truly were—but he also shared in our presence and society. Indeed, he was a speaker of the mysteries of God, and even spoke with God himself. 

<margin>Adam.</margin> Thus, in his state of innocence, the power he shared with God and us, his good angels, was exalted, and he became holy in the sight of God. This continued until **Coronzon** <note>original: "CoronZon"; identified in Dee's system as a powerful demonic entity or "mighty devil."</note> (for that is the true name of that mighty devil), envying man’s happiness and perceiving that the substance of man's lower nature was frail and imperfect compared to his pure being <note>original: "Esse"; Latin for "essence" or "being."</note>, began to attack him. 

The devil prevailed, and man, by offending God, became accursed in His sight. He lost the garden of happiness and the clarity of his understanding. However, he did not utterly lose the favor of God. He was driven out (as your Scriptures record) onto the Earth, which was covered with brambles. There, being as if mute and unable to speak, he was forced by necessity to learn the language which you, E.K., call Hebrew. Yet even that was not the same Hebrew used among you today. 

In that language, he delivered to his descendants the closest knowledge he had of God and His creatures. He divided his speech into three parts: twelve, three, and seven. The numbers of that language remain, but the true forms and pronunciations are missing. Therefore, it does not have the force it possessed in its original dignity—much less can it be compared with this language we are now delivering to you. 

Adam truly spoke this language in his state of innocence. It has never been uttered or disclosed to man from that time until now. In this language, the power of God shall work, and wisdom shall be delivered in her true kind. These mysteries are not to be expressed by any other means, nor discussed through human imagination. For as this work and gift come from God, who is all power, so does He reveal it in a tongue of power.

<margin>Formal Numbers. Pulius.</margin>

the unrighteous? Or where do you read that he ever visited the reprobate <note>original: "reprobate"; those predestined to damnation</note>? For the reprobate has no visitation except through the rod of Justice. <margin>An objection and answer.</margin> But you may rise up among yourselves, saying, "Look, we are perverse <note>original: "froward"</note>, we lack faith." It is true you lack the *acts* of faith, but not the *roots* of faith.

But here there is a warning <note>original: "Caveat"</note>: that a man, imagining his own predestination and perfect election, must not justify himself. For wherever this self-justification is found—or this doctrine is preached among you, whether privately in a man or publicly in a congregation—it is the sure sign and token of their perpetual ignorance and confusion. 

For the Will and Power of God do not belong to our limited measure (for seeking such measure was the cause of rebellion among us <note>Likely referring to the fall of the angels</note>), much less among men, who are still fighting for the glory of their reward. Behold, it is a sin in him who judges his brother's conscience; it is much more a threefold error to form imaginations of sin based on those whose imaginations they are. 

Do not be proud, therefore, of the gifts of God, but become humble. Neither justify yourself simply because this is the word of God delivered to you for your own sake. But the more you receive, be the more thankful; and the more you stand in the strength of God, the more you should practice the purity of humility. Of whom it is said, "Behold, my Spirit has entered, even into my servants, and they have become humble and meek in the sight of men." 

But if we are the servants of the God of Abraham, then we are <margin>Good Angels.</margin> the spirits of truth and understanding; for our faith is honored in the sight of the heavens, and we have become mighty in the power of the Almighty. Therefore, we ought to be believed. Now, if you will confess yourselves to be the children of Abraham, then you must also accept our doctrine. For the meat <note>original: "meat"; used here to mean spiritual food or sustenance</note> by which Abraham lived is the same food we administer to you; of whom it is said, "He believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness." Do the same, <margin>April 24, this afternoon.</margin> so that you also may be righteous. 

In what way do you differ from Abraham? Were you not barren? Who has made you fruitful? <margin>Note.</margin> Did God make a covenant with Abraham? He does the same with you. Did the Lord appear to him through his ministers? So he does, and will do, to you. Were the sins of Sodom (the city that perished) brought into Abraham's bosom as the secret determination of the Lord? Are they not also made manifest to you (even by the same God) regarding the timing and corruption of this world? Did he not rise up in the morning and behold the confusion and headlong ruins of the wicked? And shall you not also see the same?

After prayers, there appeared Gabriel and Nalvage <note>Nalvage: An angelic figure in Dee's visions</note> with the Table, and Gabriel with his rod <note>original: "Dare," likely a transcription error for "wand" or "rod"</note> in his hand. The beginning of this river was a spring, which was unknown to the city because of the height <note>OCR unclear: "yth"</note> from which it descended. 

It came to pass that a serpent groaned for her time, and lo, she brought forth offspring; and they were such as herself. And she lifted up her head and leaned upon her twice-twisted tail, and beheld the sun steadfastly (for her envy was toward that city). And she said within herself: "My children are yet young." Time passed and they grew large. And she went unto the spring, and smiled, and said with a laughing voice: "The earth has fallen into you; you are choked. But listen to my voice, and you shall receive comfort." But the spring would not. 

And the serpent lifted up her voice and roared, for she was full of craft and deceit. And she said unto the shingles <note>term: shingles: small stones or pebbles in a riverbed</note> through which the spring runs (or rather seeps): "You are full of emptiness and void places. Let my children, therefore, hide themselves within you for a season." And the stones were contented. And she departed willingly, and said within herself: "Now I know I shall be Lady of the city."

And after a few years, the young serpents became large, so that one half of their bodies lived within the shingles <note>original: "Shingles"; here meaning loose stones or gravel, likely representing worldly debris or spiritual obstructions</note>, and the rest blocked the passage of the spring. **E.K.:** My judgment is that the shingles and the serpent should be removed by an earthquake from the place which they encumber and obstruct, so that there may be a fit new place and course for that spring to relieve that city as it did before.

Now listen to what the Lord says: The people and the city of the hill represent the world, which is from time to time relieved and quenched by the mercy and spring of God's wisdom, according to the extremity and necessity of their thirst. But the people and the city are specifically those of the Temple and Church of God, who drink of His mercy for their comfort. The camels and other beasts are the people of the Earth who delight in sin and in their own imagination; they are also relieved alongside those of the city, but the differences in their natures <note>original: "bodies"</note> cause a difference in the ultimate results of their comfort.

The hill where the spring is located signifies His prophets and those who are 'drunk in the Lord' <note>meaning those overwhelmed or filled with the Holy Spirit</note>. Through them, the mercies and will of God and of the Highest are revealed inwardly from time to time, according to the secret will and determination regarding those who are outside the city of His elect. But the frailties and passions of their flesh and outward man are their foolish imaginations and loose shingles, wherein the serpent—the old Devil—has harbored her children, the spirits of..."

<meta>This page continues a spiritual dialogue involving E.K. (Edward Kelley) and an angelic or divine entity, focusing on the necessity of renouncing worldly "wickedness" and magical "trash" to receive God's secrets.</meta>

Darkness and deceit always resist the Will of God and are placed between the mercies of God and his people. Moses, Daniel, Esdras <note>original: "Esdras"; the biblical Ezra</note>, and all the rest of the Prophets—as well as Christ’s twelve apostles and Paul, the Messenger of God—all of them burdened the Congregation of the Faithful in their flesh until they gave sentence against themselves (as you have done) with an amendment of life. For who is worthy to know the secrets of our God, except he who delights in righteousness, is obedient, full of faith, and possesses the spirit of understanding? Let it therefore be done for you as you have said. Let the shingles <note>original: "Shingles"; likely referring to debris, dross, or scaly coverings</note> and serpents be separated so that the Fountain may feed as before. All the trash that you have from the wicked, burn it.

**E.K.** I do not know if they are wicked.

...... Their dealings with you are the hindrance of the Will of God, and therefore they are wicked. ...... You have given judgment against yourself; take heed that you do not offend your own soul.

**Δ** <note>This symbol represents John Dee</note> Send down your Spirit, O Lord, and illuminate E.K.’s heart with a perception of his wrong opinion, etc.

**E.K.** If Moses and Daniel were skillful in the arts of the Egyptian Magicians and were not thereby hindered from being the servants of God, why may I not deal with these things without hindrance to the Will of God?

...... Darkness yielded unto light; the greater excluded the lesser. The more a man knows wickedness, the more he shall hate it once he is called back. The more they knew the shadow, the more they delighted in the body <note>meaning the substance or reality</note>. For the works of the Egyptians seem to be something, but are not. The works of the Lord truly exist and continue. Just as a painter imitates the gestures of a man through his skill, so does the Devil imitate the substances and things created and made by God. Stand up and look into the whole world—into her youth and middle age—for they are past. Where are the monuments that Satan has built?

**E.K.** Has Satan built any monuments?

...... Yes. Has he not built himself a fort upon the whole earth? Does he not have the victory over the Saints? Does he not dwell in the Temple of the Highest? Does he not triumph in the cities of the whole world? Yes. ...... But his victories are without comfort; his dwelling places are without pleasure. For he knows his time is at hand. He who now gives freedom shall become bound; and for him to whom the whole world is currently like a garden, there shall not be one foot of land left. Therefore, all his pleasures are vanity, all his triumphs are smoke, and his authority is nothing indeed but a mere shadow. For that which is not <note>i.e., lacks divine reality</note> cannot truly be; where it is said of the Lord, it shall not be. Neither can truth, light, or wisdom ascend from the earth, but must descend from the heavens. 

Compare the earth (into which the Devil is thrust as into his dwelling) with the heavens, which are provided for the holy. Consider the pain of the one and the pleasure of the other: the seat of God’s Justice and the Fountain of his Mercy; the Cave of Darkness and the Diadem <note>original: "Diadew"; a crown or emblem of royalty</note> of Light. And then cry: woe, woe, woe, woe unto those who err!

<meta>This page continues the record of spiritual actions or "calls" conducted by John Dee and Edward Kelley in Krakow, Poland, during May 1584.</meta>

To our [God], be all praise, victory, triumph, and rejoicing, Amen. <note>original: "nostro, laus omnis, Victoria, Triumphus, and Jubilatio, Amen."</note>
Monday, Krakow, May 21, 1584. <note>original: "Cracovie Maii, 21. 1564" - Note: The OCR date 1564 is a likely error for 1584, the year of Dee's Polish travels.</note> In the morning, at 5 o'clock. The third action, Lunar.

**Edward Kelley:** There appears neither a veil nor anything else in the stone. <note>The "stone" refers to the crystal or "shew-stone" used for scrying.</note> At length one appeared, but none of those seen before. He is joyful and dressed in green, with a long robe (like green velvet). His hair is long, like yellow gold, with nothing on his head but his hair. He stands as though he were in a cloud, above the usual floor in the air.

<margin>The promise of God is confirmed anew.</margin>
**The Spirit:** Look, the sun shines, and men do not fear rain; the clouds are dispersed, and they do not expect a storm. But when it rains heavily, or the heavens frown, then they stay in their houses, saying to one another, "What an unreasonable storm is this? What hailstones are these? Good Lord, who ever saw such winds? Were there ever such winds?" 

<margin>To be received the Monday next.</margin>
So shall it be regarding the power of God, who holds the winds in his hands and scatters clouds abroad with his feet. For of his coming, it shall be said among you: "My spirit has troubled me, and I am distressed. Why have you brought in things greater than yourself? Or where shall this power dwell that overshadows me?" 

<margin>God is not tied to time.</margin>
Lacking, you shall desire (as you do now), and being filled, you shall think you have too much. Flesh can never be thoroughly mortified <note>term: mortified; the subduing of physical appetites or the "death" of the sinful nature</note> except by death. Do not think that the Lord is like the Sun, which keeps its continual watch through the heavens; because the Sun is made for a period of time, it is also tied to time. He who sits and judges keeps no set course, but rather a continual performance of his long-established providence. For he who treats Him otherwise shall be rejected, because his dwellings are not in the mansions of the faithful. <note>The spirit suggests God's presence is constant and eternal, unlike the cyclical nature of the sun.</note> Lift up your ears, therefore; for thus says the Greatest:

### Page 218

Who made the heavens, or spread them out like a garment? Who breathed into man the spirit of understanding? Who overthrew the proud world with waters? <note>A reference to the Great Flood of Noah.</note> Who smiled at the ruin of Pharaoh? Who rooted the wicked out of their seats and made them become vineyards for my people—even the stiff-necked generation? Who threw down the towers of Babylon and the Great Harlot? Who dwelt upon the earth and became flesh to pay for your wickedness? <note>A reference to the Incarnation of Jesus Christ.</note> Who tumbled the stone from the wells so that the sheep might drink? 

It is He who gave all these things their appointed times. He it is who is as able to make you understand as those who cast into the waters and said, "Let us draw up our fish." He always deals with the weakest, to the intent that he might prove himself the strongest.

**Edward Kelley:** He...

<summary>During a spiritual session in Krakow, a golden-haired spirit in green velvet appears to Edward Kelley, delivering a discourse on God's eternal providence and power over nature and history. The spirit emphasizes that God is not bound by time like the sun and uses the weak to demonstrate His strength.</summary>

<meta>This page continues a series of spiritual instructions or angelic communications, focusing on the necessity of patience and obedience during divine trials.</meta>

I speak this for your instruction: many have the power of God, but not for the sake of righteousness. This was evident among the Jews in the choice of their Kings, and even in the house of God among those who entered into the holy place. For not everyone whom the Prophets anointed was good. It was not that they were evil at the time of their anointing, but because their "unction" <note>original: "In-unction"; the act of being formally anointed with oil for a holy office</note> and the dignity of their office was eventually defiled by their own perverse stubbornness <note>original: "frowardnesse"</note>. The High Priests were also chosen in righteousness and by the spirit of God, yet they became rebels in the holy house; it is of such people that it is said, *The Most High became a stumbling block to them* <note>original: "Altissimus autem fuit scandalum illis"</note>.

Even so, my brothers, it may be with you. Jesus defend us from such a misfortune. For although it has pleased God to show himself to you, you are not ashamed to say: "If the harvest does not come at the appointed time, I will become a deserter <note>original: "runnagate"</note>." But, oh Metatron <note>original: "mytrethron"; likely referring to the archangel Metatron</note>, does the Lord have need of you? It does not need to be told to you; you know the contrary. It follows, then, that you have need of God. 

But for what purpose, and why? So that your souls may overcome this world and overcome the body, reaching the dignity of an Angel. And because you are miserable and cast out into the field—full of brambles and misery, lean, naked, and unarmed—to fight against him <note>referring to the Devil or spiritual adversary</note> who resists the might of God. Consider these last two points, and then answer for yourselves regarding the rest. 

I give you a short warning. God will fulfill his promises, and (as he has said) by this August, you shall understand:
1. How to know and use God's creatures, both good and bad.
2. But when and for what purpose this occurs is the gift of the Highest. It shall be fulfilled in you (if you will be obedient) when it pleases him, even with a sound from his own mouth, saying, *Come and hear* <note>original: "Venite and audite"</note>. 

For these actions are twofold: consider this, if you can. They are the greatest actions because they are the last, and they contain everything that has been done before them. If you consider this well, and the nature of your calling, you shall perceive that the judgments of God are not a tennis ball <note>meaning they are not to be played with or tossed about lightly</note>. I thought it necessary to warn you of this, my brothers. Have a little patience for the Action. He who stirs from his place shall find the reward for doing so <note>implying a punishment for lack of steadfastness</note>.

***

-> **Thursday, May 24** <-

**Dee:** Because Edward Kelley did not come (as was commanded yesterday) to follow the Action, I went to his study door and knocked for him. I requested him to come, but he refused to do so and gave me a short and resolute answer: that he would never again have anything to do with these Actions. I asked him the reason why; he would give none, but earnestly refused to proceed. I told him that his words <margin>G1: Those words he spoke after the Action ended, more than an hour later, in the chamber before my study of practice.</margin> last night (saying that he could not deal with this today) did very much grieve me, etc., which he made little account of. So I went into my study again and committed the cause to God.

After less than half an hour, he came speedily out of his study and brought in his hand one volume of Cornelius Agrippa’s works. In one chapter of that book, he read the names of countries and provinces collected out of Ptolemy <note>original: Prolemein</note> (as the author notes there). Based on this, he inferred that our spiritual instructors were deceivers <note>original: Ceseners/Cozeners</note> for giving us a description of the world taken out of other books; therefore, he would have no more to do with them.

I replied and said, "I am very glad that you have a book of your own wherein these geographical names are expressed, such as (for the most part) our instructors had delivered unto us—and that they were delivered according to the tenor and form of my request to him, to have them expressed for our more perfect [understanding]..."

### Saturday, at Krakow. In the morning around 7:00.

After several prayers and my petitions: he appeared almost immediately. E.K. says: I see him whom we call Gabriel, sitting in his chair alone. Gabriel...... God is a spirit, essential in himself: essential and working by himself: essential in all works, and dignifying them by himself. So it is that the beginning and ending of all things—those that already exist, or are already in him and yet to come—is placed in the fountain and well-spring of all life, comfort, and increase. By this we see that the heavens and the mighty powers within them, from the highest to the lowest; things that shall have an end; and the earth with all that she brings forth; yes, even the lower parts (though after another manner and by another course) all hang and are established in and upon the unspeakable power in his providence. How, therefore, can the Heavens run angry? Or the earth (for the sake of the Elect) want for a comforter? Or the lowest places look for comfort? If it is so, therefore, that the heavens cannot err; or if the power of God is so mighty and so full of prevailing; if in the house of light there is no darkness, and from the Heavens no wickedness can descend (And why? Because they are dignified in the power of God), who is he that should live and yet distrust the Lord?

The Devil is not only manifest, but also still fights against the power and will of God, stirring up and provoking man to fast at full banquets <note>original: "Bankers"; likely meaning to abstain or behave hypocritically amidst plenty</note> and to study both good and evil. Is it not a greater sin than the sin of the Devil? For the Devil sins in himself, and therefore had his fall; but your sin is in yourselves and caused by the Devil, and therefore it is the greater. 

But, as it was said before, where is there a monument upon the earth that the people have raised up in the remembrance of wickedness? There are many who say, "Look, there is Jerusalem; look, there the Lord was buried; look, there the floods divided themselves," and all the rest in remembrance of the Lord. But there are none who say, "Look, in this place the wicked rose up and prevailed." 

Therefore, to cling to the Lord is good, and to follow a sensible doctrine which brings with it a loathing of wickedness and a desire to do well, so that the wicked may be defeated. Alas! In the morning at 7:15 AM. Krakow. <note>original: "Cracoviæ"</note> [delta]. After our proper prayers and thanks to the Almighty for His great mercies and power shown in the conversion of E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee's scryer</note>, we stayed still, waiting for some vision <note>original: "shew"</note> such as we were accustomed to receive. Among our various short discourses regarding our faith, hope, patience, constancy, humility, and our other duties required in this action and in the service of God, E.K. spoke these sentences of his own accord, which are worthy to be recorded as the evident token of his sound and faithful turning and his intent to cling unto the Lord:

To be "of the world" was to be in love with the trade of the vanities of this world and to follow them. Money and riches were things indifferent: good if they were well used, and evil if they were evilly used. And that "for the good, all things worked together for good" <note>original Latin: Bonis omnia cooperabantur ad bonum; a reference to Romans 8:28</note>. Therefore the godly (as the Patriarchs and many nowadays) might have money, but to use it, not abuse it; and such is our case and necessary request to God, and so forth.
