The Lord appeared unto Enoch and was merciful unto him. He opened his eyes so that he might see and judge the earth, which was unknown unto his parents because of their fall <note>referring to the Fall of Adam and Eve</note>. For the Lord said, "Let us show unto Enoch the use of the earth." And lo, Enoch was wise and full of the spirit of wisdom. And he said unto the Lord, "Let there be a remembrance of your mercy, and let those who love you taste of this after me; O, let not your mercy be forgotten." And the Lord was pleased. 

And after fifty days, Enoch had finished writing; and this was the title of his books: *Let those who fear God and are worthy read.* 

But behold, the people grew wicked and became unrighteous, and the spirit of the Lord was far off and gone away from them. Consequently, those who were unworthy began to read. And the kings of the earth spoke thus against the Lord: "What is it that we cannot do? Or who is he that can resist us?" And the Lord was provoked, and he sent among them a hundred and fifty lions, and spirits of wickedness, error, and deceit; and these appeared unto them. For the Lord had placed them between those who are wicked and his good angels. 

And they began to counterfeit the doings of God and his power—for they were given the power to do so—so that the memory of Enoch was washed away. These spirits of error began to teach them doctrines which, from time to time until this age and even unto this day, have spread abroad into all parts of the world; this is the skill and cunning of the wicked. 

By this means, they speak with devils—not because they have power over the devils, but because they are joined to them in the league and discipline of their own doctrine. For behold, just as the knowledge of the mystical figures and the use of their presence is the gift of God (delivered to Enoch, and by Enoch’s request to the faithful, so that they might have the true use of God’s creatures and of the earth whereon they dwell), so has the Devil delivered unto the wicked the signs and tokens of his error and hatred toward God. By using these, they might consent to their own fall and so become partakers with the devils in their reward, which is eternal damnation. These they call <term>Characters</term> <note>In this context, "Characters" refers to magical symbols, sigils, or talismans used in dark magic or sorcery</note>; a lamentable thing. For by these, many souls have perished. 

Now it has pleased God to deliver this doctrine again out of darkness, and to fulfill his promise with you concerning the books of Enoch; to whom he says, as he said unto...

<meta>This page continues the detailed explanation of the Great Table or Seal of God, focusing on the formation of divine names and angelic hierarchies from specific letter grids.</meta>

<margin>Three names of God on the banners.</margin> This line is called the "Line of the Holy Spirit" <note>original: *linea Spiritus Sancti*</note>. Out of that line come the three names of God from the East Gate, consisting of 3, 4, and 5 letters, which were the coats of arms on the banners <note>original: *Ensignes*</note> mentioned previously: *Oro*, *Ibah*, and *Aozpi* <note>original: *203pi*, likely an OCR error for the Enochian name Aozpi</note>. I said before that God the Father is a mighty pillar divided by a straight line. The Father himself exists without the line; the Father and Son exist by the addition of the line. These two lines begin with *J Aidar*, and so on. <margin>East.</margin> That is the Great Cross that came out of the East Gate.

**Dee:** With that line of the Holy Spirit?

**Angel:** Yes. In the upper left angle, in the second line, you have *a r d z a*. You have that which makes the cross downward: first *i*, then the same *d, o, i, g, o*.

**Dee:** Will you have six letters downward?

**Angel:** Yes. So then you have the three other crosses in their angles.

**Dee:** Will you give me leave to repeat them, for fear of making a mistake? *I L a c z a* is the downward line of six letters, and *p a L a m* is the cross line.

**Angel:** It is so.

**Dee:** Now to the other on the left side below: *a i a o a i* <margin>Ten faces on the crosses.</margin> is the downward right line. Now the cross line is *O i i i t*. Here those crosses have ten faces.

**Dee:** One letter is counted twice because it is in the center of the cross; therefore, it would seem there are eleven.

---

**Angel:** This is true knowledge.

**Dee:** The last cross is thus: its downward line is *a O u r r z*. The cross line is *a L O a i*. So I have the four crosses attending the principal cross.

**Angel:** Here you may see the reason why Pilate wrote with four letters <note>A reference to the INRI inscription on the Cross of Christ</note>.

**Dee:** How does the reason appear?

**Angel:** Because above every cross stand four letters. It is not that Pilate knew this, but that it was the pre-determination of God. They are to be read thus: in the upper left angle you have *r z l a*. Pronounce it: *Urzla*. <margin>The four Angels over every cross of the four attendant crosses.</margin> In this name, the first Angel appears. Take *z l a*, then go back to the first *r*, and pronounce it *Zlar*. The letter that was the first letter of the first Angel is the last letter of the second. For example, in *r z l a*, the *r* was the first letter of the name; that *r* is now the last letter of the name of the second Angel, which begins at *z* (as *z l a*) and then goes back to the *r*.

**Dee:** So the third begins at *l*, and its last letter is the first of the second name, and it is called *Larz*. And so with the last: *a r z l*, to be pronounced *Arzel*.

**Dee:** So from those four letters, you have four Angels' names gathered out in this way. But how are they to be used?

**Angel:** Let it be enough that you know these names. I will teach you how to use them later.

**Dee:** Shall we work by the same method for every set of four letters over the crosses to make four such names?

**Angel:** They are also to be made in that way.

Up to this point, the knowledge of Solomon reached. <note>The author suggests that the following revelation exceeds even the legendary wisdom of King Solomon.</note> Now, regarding your six Seniors <note>Seniors: High-ranking angelic entities in the Enochian system.</note> whose judgment is of God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost:

In the line "Of the Holy Spirit" <note>original: "De Spiritu Sancto"</note>, you have **Abioro**, consisting of six letters. The second name of the second Senior has seven letters, such as **Aaixa** (the same, ascending). If the third is like the second, in the Father and the Son, it is **Hcmorda**. If you wish to make them all consist of seven letters (because two of them currently have only six), which is done when the wrath of God is to be increased— <margin>The increasing of names by adding a letter.</margin> —then where you would say **Abioro**, say **Habioro**; and where you would say **Haozpi**, say **Ahahozpi**. You have 'b', the fifth, in the left part of the line "Of the Holy Spirit." You have 'a', the sixth (the first part of the line "Of the Father and Son," descending). -> Saturday, at Krakow, June 30. In the morning, around 9 o'clock. <-

After finishing the Lord's Prayer and proposing those seven doubts, we rested for a little while. **The Spirit:** Hearken to my voice.

<margin>G6</margin> Modesty, patience, and humility of heart and body belong to these actions. Tell me, how many thunders does the Lord have in store for the wicked?

<note>Dee</note>: O Lord, we do not know.

**The Spirit:** Were you ever in the secret caves of the Earth?

<note>Dee</note>: No, Lord, never.

**The Spirit:** Then tell me, how many winds has the Lord prepared for a year?

<note>Dee</note>: We cannot tell that either; we are not part of the Lord's Council in these matters of his providence.

<note>Dee</note>: God only knows, and no creature knows except through him; for all things are kept uncertain until the end.

**The Spirit:** You beget children; do you know the hour in which they shall be born? You begin labor; can you tell at what point in time you shall finish?

<note>Dee</note>: God alone is the fountain of all wisdom and truth.

**The Spirit:** Well, then I see you are drowned in ignorance and know nothing.

**Edward Kelley:** He turns around very swiftly.

<margin>G7</margin> **The Spirit:** Even as the adder <note>a type of venomous snake</note> leads out her young ones—the first day only one foot out of her nest <note>original: bale</note>, not so they should eat, but so they might acquaint themselves with the air and her cunning. The second day, she leads them a yard or more; she circles her hole, winds to and fro, and teaches them to creep. She does this for five or six days until they know how to move and stir their bodies. After the seventh day, she leads them further and practices deceit, striking the ground with her tail as if it were the sound of someone nearby. Then, gaping, she begins to hiss and stirs up fear in her young ones so that they retreat into her mouth. She does this until they are 12 or 13 days old. Then she leads them a stone's throw away and exercises them both in fear and in hiding themselves. And when they sleep (being young and weary from labor), she steals away from them and makes a noise among the leaves and small stones by moving her hind parts.

To the intent she might see what shift her worms <note>original: "wormes"; here meaning young serpents</note> can make, which, stirred up with fear and missing their mother, so learn to couch themselves in the chimneys <note>original: "Chymnes"; meaning crevices or openings</note> of the earth. At length, after silence, the mother trusts herself out and doubles her tongue (with the sound of which she is accustomed to call them). They come together and rejoice, wreathing themselves diversely about her body for joy. She, for a recompense, allows them to hang upon her back, and so wallows to her hole where she gathers the leaves of the earth. After she has chewed them small and tender with her teeth and mingled them with the dust, she spews them out again and begins to lick them little by little, as though she herself were hungry. This she subtly does so that her worms might eat and forget their hungriness. Finally, in twenty days, they become big and as skillful in the instincts of their kind. She (I say) <note>original: "Isay"</note> leads them out into a fertile place, full of dew and full of bushes—places apt to cover them—where they feed, dwell, observe their craft, and at last forsake their mother. 

Even so, it is with you. So the Lord (the true Serpent and worm) leads you out from day to day, according <margin>G1</margin> to your strength; and as you grow, it is to the intent that you might at last be brought unto the pleasant dew and food of His mercy, which is triumphing true wisdom. # The First Eight Questions

**Dee:** Regarding the first eight questions. 1. Concerning the five Princes who held up the King's train.
**Ave:** Knowledge of them is of no help at this time.
**Dee:** 2. Secondly, regarding the Trumpeter—what did that signify?
**Ave:** It has no relation to these Tables.
**Dee:** 3. Regarding the letters in the Transversary <note>The cross-bar or horizontal section of a symbolic diagram</note>, I would know your will.
**Ave:** They are, like the others, only for a specific ritual practice.
**Dee:** 4. Regarding *Docepax* and *Tedoand* <note>Names of spiritual entities or governors</note> being referred to in different ways, as I have noted—what is the cause of this diversity?
**Ave:** It was the fault of Edward Kelley in his reporting.
**Dee:** What is the actual truth?
**Ave:** You shall be taught that when you have their "Calls" <note>The Enochian Invocations or Keys</note>. It falls under the correction of Nalvage <note>Another spiritual entity who delivered parts of the system</note>.
**Dee:** 5. Concerning the etymologies <note>The linguistic origins and meanings</note> of these names of God, we would like to be satisfied.
**Ave:** God is a Spirit and cannot be fully comprehended.
**Dee:** I only ask for some sign or declaration, not a full comprehension.

<margin>The Coming of Christ.</margin>
<margin>Our bodies to be cast out into the fields.</margin>
<margin>Prophecy.</margin>
<margin>The future Kingdom.</margin>
<margin>Dee: Be gone to the Emperor.</margin>
<margin>Those that hold up the grapes. Satan. The Faithful. The Holy Spirit.</margin>
<margin>Docepax. Tedoand.</margin>
<margin>The Calls. Nalvage is to correct them.</margin>

***

**Ave:** It is not within the reach of human understanding. These names signify all things, and they signify nothing.
**Ave:** Who can express what "Jehovah" signifies? *God's name signifies that which He does.* <note>original: "Deus significat ad id quod agit"</note>
**Dee:** Regarding the form of our petition or invitation to the good Angels—what sort of form should it take?
**Ave:** A short and brief speech.
**Dee:** We beseech you to give us an example; we would have more confidence if it were of greater effect.
**Ave:** I am not permitted to do so.
**Kelley:** And why?
**Ave:** Invocation proceeds from the goodwill of man and from the heat and fervency of the spirit. Therefore, prayer is of such effect with God.
**Dee:** We beseech you, shall we use one form of prayer for all of them?
**Ave:** Each one should have a different form.
**Dee:** You mean, if the mind dictates or prompts a different form?
**Ave:** I do not know, for I do not dwell within the soul of man.

**Dee:** Is it *Aydropl* or *Andropl*?

**Dee:** Regarding the capital letters, have I done well?
**Ave:** You have easily corrected that, and to a good end; for every letter, and every part of a letter, has its own significance.
**Dee:** I beseech you to say something about the letter "N" in *Paraoan*, of which you said that as far as it stretched, it should sink to hell.
**Ave:** Every letter in *Paraoan* is a living fire, but all are of one quality and one creation. However, unto the letter "N" is delivered a vial of Destruction.

How much more, do you think, does the God of wisdom forge, test, and beat out those whom he intends to use in the execution of his divine and eternal purposes? How, therefore, can you find fault with the Lord? How can you say he deals unjustly with you when he allows you to be tested to the uttermost? After finishing the Lord's Prayer <note>original: "Oratione Dominica"</note> and other petitions both to God and to Ave <note>Ave is the name of the angelic being communicating with Dee</note> himself, I requested Ave’s judgment regarding the prayers I had made to God and His good angels. After barely a quarter of an hour, Ave appeared.

**Ave:** If the words or the truth of our testimony and message were within the capacity of man, or contained by it, then the Devil might thrust himself in and mimic the image of Truth. But because this message is of Truth, and from Him who bears testimony of Himself, it can have no connection with the flesh, nor be spoken of in that sense. Look: this is how the Devil has deceitfully entered into man.

**Δ:** <note>The symbol Delta (Δ) represents John Dee</note> Blessed be the Lord of all truth.

**Ave:** Therefore, seeing that the Word is not corruptible, those who minister the Word cannot dwell in corruption. I do not say this without a cause, my brethren.

**Δ:** I pray you to proceed accordingly, so that we may know the cause, if it be your will. Otherwise, leaving this warning <term>Caveat</term> with us, please proceed to the matter where we requested your helping hand—to correct, confirm, or do whatever is necessary.

**Ave:** For which of you has sought the Lord for the Lord’s own cause or sake?

**Δ:** God can be the judge of that.

**Ave:** Or in which of you has due obedience—either to the Word or to us who are sanctified by the Word—been faithfully performed?

**Δ:** I beseech you to point out <term>Notifie</term> my errors and acts of disobedience, so that I may amend them.

**Ave:** Perhaps you will say, "We have labored, and we have watched; yes, we have called on the name of the Lord." What have you done that you ought not to do—yes, a thousand times more?

**Δ:** We boast of none of our actions, nor do we claim anything based on any perfection in our deeds.

**Ave:** Shall the hired hand <term>hireling</term> say, "I have labored hard"? Or does the good servant think he has earned his wages? It is not so. But you act this way; therefore, you are worthy of neither your reward nor the name of faithful servants.

**Δ:** No, Lord, we claim nothing based on any merits; instead, we fly to Your mercy, and that is what we crave and call for.

**Ave:** You act wickedly and unjustly; yes, you trust the Lord only as much as you trust yourselves. Your faith is the faith of men, and not of the faithful. "Many things have I said to you from the beginning," says the God of Justice, "which you have heard and not believed. Instead, you tempt me and provoke me; yes, you stir me up to be angry with you."

**Δ:** If Your anger falls upon us, in addition to the sorrow of this world and the temptations of the Fiend, etc., then we will not be able to endure it.

**Ave:** Answer not.

Listen to me, and hear what the Lord says to you: Satan laughs you to scorn. For he says to the Lord, standing before Him, "Are these the ones whom You delivered from the <margin>The great and peculiar mercies of God shown to us.</margin> perils of the seas and from the bonds of the wicked? Were the winds a comfort to them, and Your countenance a lantern <note>original: "Lanthorn"</note> to guide them?" But the Lord seems to endure his taunts, for He knows it is true. My brethren, you seek the world more than you seek to perform the will of God—as though God could not rain gold and pearls <note>original: "Margarits"</note> among you; as though the breath of God were not able to beat down the whole earth before you. 

O you faithless creatures! O you hypocrites in the vineyard of the Lord! O you unworthy servants of such a Master! Neither to Abraham, nor to Noah <note>original: "Noe"</note>, nor to any other patriarchs or prophets has God shown more mercy than He has to you. To Abraham He said, "When I return at this time of year, you shall have a son." To Noah He said, "Build yourself a ship; make the Ark in this and that way, for the people shall perish." <margin>Genesis 27 <note>The author likely intends a general reference to the Patriarchs; Genesis 27 actually concerns Jacob and Esau.</note></margin> You do not remember that Joseph was sold by his brothers; or if you do, perhaps you think it is a fable. If you believe it to be true, then consider how he escaped the pit. Consider that he was sold and so became a slave <note>original: "bondman"</note>. But who changed the thoughts and feelings of his brothers? Who, I ask, came between their tyranny and his innocence? Who was it that made him free? That brought him before Pharaoh? Yes, and what is more, made him rule over Pharaoh? Was it not the same God who deals with you? 

O you of little faith—you starvelings, withered grass, and blasted willows! What if you were in hell? Could He not deliver you? If you become slaves, cannot He make you free? If you are in prison, cannot He deliver you? Cannot He encircle your neck with a chain of honor? But Satan says, "Look, they say they have a long journey." It is necessary that God comfort those who put their trust in Him. Well done! <note>original: "Euge" (Latin: an exclamation of joy or approval, here used ironically)</note> O, you beggarly starvelings! Has not the same God the same Raphael <note>The Archangel Raphael, known as a healer and guide in the Book of Tobit.</note> that He had then? Yes, truly—a thousand, a hundred, and a hundred thousand thousands more than Raphael for the help and comfort of the faithful. 

When Herod sought to kill the Son of God in His human form, His Father did not deliver Him with a mighty wind, nor by tearing down the palaces of lords. Instead, He appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, "Flee, for Herod seeks the child's life." Note the manner of His warning; note the manner of His departure. But hear what the Lord said in the end: "Return, for he who sought the child's life is now dead." Why, I say, you rotten reeds—worse than the waste of the fields <note>original: "excrements of the Fees"</note>—

Have you not been given a greater warning? Why is it said to you, "Get up and be gone," except that the Lord sees the thoughts of man—even the thoughts of him who seeks your destruction? Even this wicked King who seeks to destroy Laskie <note>Albertus Laski, a Polish nobleman and patron of Dee and Kelley</note>. Those who are righteous are often taken away because of temptations that are to come; but the wicked are allowed to continue so that their burden might be heavier and they might sink deeper. 

But, out of love, I say to you, my brothers: flee the mischiefs that are to come and go forward in the service of the Most High, so that you may enjoy the promises made to you and be partakers of the happy days to come. **Gabriel:** Thus has God kept his promise with you, and has delivered to you the keys of his storehouses. Within them you shall find—if you enter wisely, humbly, and patiently—treasures worth more than the very structures of the heavens. But August has not yet arrived; nevertheless, the Lord has kept his promise with you before <margin>G2 God's promise fulfilled before August.</margin> the appointed time. Therefore, now examine your books, compare one passage with another, and learn to be perfect for the practice and the entrance. 

<margin>G3 Counsel for preparation.</margin> See that your garments are clean. Do not be rash in this, nor over-hasty; for those who are hasty and rash, and are loathsomely dressed, may knock a long time before they are allowed to enter. 

<margin>G4 The reading of the Book. The letters.</margin> There is no other way to "read" the Book than by the appearing of the Ministers and Creatures of God. By showing what they are themselves, they show how they are joined together in power, and how they are formally represented by those letters. 

**Edward Kelley:** Now he takes the Table <note>The "Table of Nalvage" or a similar visionary chart used in their rituals</note> and seems to wrap it up together.

**Gabriel:** You play with me like a child. 

**Dee:** I have finished.

**Gabriel:** Do you think that we say anything that is not true? <margin>G5 The mysteries of this Book. Dwell together.</margin> You shall never know the mysteries of all things that have been spoken. If you love one another, and dwell together, and in one God, then that same God will be merciful to you. May he bless you, comfort you, and strengthen you until the end. I would say more, but words are of no use. God be among you.

**Edward Kelley:** Now they have both gone upward in a great flame of fire.

Remember on Wednesday night, the eighteenth of July, as I walked alone about nine o'clock in the evening in the chamber in front of my study (upstairs), flashes of fire appeared in various places of that chamber, but they did not spread light further abroad.

->**YEAR 1584**<-

On Wednesday, the first day of August, at three o'clock in the afternoon, we entered on our journey toward Prague, in the Kingdom of Bohemia <note>original: "Beame"</note>, where we arrived on Thursday a week later by three o'clock—that is, exactly in eight days. We traveled by coach: I, Edward Kelley, and his brother, and Edmond Hilton; so that we came to Prague on August 9th by the New Calendar <note>The Gregorian calendar, which was 10 days ahead of the Julian calendar used in England at the time.</note>, but by the Old Calendar it was July 30th—two days before August in the Old Calendar. 

May our God have mercy on us, and do not be angry with us forever. <note>original: "Miserere Nostri Deus Noster neque in eternum irascaris nobis."</note>

**PRAGUE 1584.**

On August 15th, Wednesday, we began on the day of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary, in the excellent little heated room <note>original: "Stove"</note> or study of Doctor Hageck’s house, which he lent to me, near Bethlehem in Old Prague. This study seemed in times past (the year 1518) to have been the study of some student or Alchemist <note>original: "A--"</note> skillful in the Holy Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone.</note>. His name was noted in various places of the study in letters of gold and silver: *Simon Baccalaureus Pragensis*. Among many other things written very beautifully in the study (including many philosophical hieroglyphic notes of birds, fishes, flowers, fruits, leaves, and six vessels for the work of the philosophers), these verses were over the door: 

*Immortal glory...* <note>The text cuts off here; the Latin "Immortal glory" suggests a dedication to the lasting fame of the alchemical arts.</note>

Nor does it truly depart, but wishes to remain with it, clearly illuminating the dead body. If you knew what the *Rebis* was, you would find what it is. This art is precious, brief, easy, and rare. Our art is a game for boys and labor for women. Know all you sons of this art, that no one can gather the fruits of our Elixir except through the entrance of our elemental Stone; if he seeks another way, he shall never enter nor reach the path. The Redness is the Work, which is made from gold alone when it has entered into its own moisture.

## THE FIRST BOOK OF THE PRAGUE MYSTERIES, The Imperial Book, Begun in the Year 1584, New Style, on August 15. To the Praise, Honor, and Glory of Almighty God. Amen.

It may be that the calculation for the year 1588 and others has its beginning from the very day of Christ’s Passion or His Ascension into Heaven. For this reason, 33 or 34 more years ought to be considered, because Christ was that many years old at the time of His passion or ascension. Therefore, if you add 34 to the year 1588, the year 1622 emerges from it. This number comes closer to the span of years of the Flood and the Ark, the likeness of which the Scriptures teach will occur around the second coming of Christ. 

Alternatively, since in the year of the world 1655 after the creation of Adam, the Flood of Water destroyed all living things; so after the restoration of Christ (our spiritual Adam) into Heaven, in the year 1655 (which will be the year 1688), we expect a Flood of Fire <note>original: "Diluvium ignis"</note> by which all things are to be transformed—or perhaps a great display of Christian charity and fervor. 

The Lord GOD will do nothing unless He reveals His secret to His servants the prophets. The lion shall roar; who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken; who will not prophesy? **Amos, Chapter 3:8.** 

We find no evil in this man; what if a spirit or an Angel has spoken to him? **Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 23:9.** 

For I tell you, that many Prophets and Kings have desired to see those things which you see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which you hear, and have not heard them. **Luke 10:24; Matthew 13:17.** 

Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God; because many false prophets have gone out...

Thursday, August 16, 1584. In the morning, around 8:40 AM. Prague.

Δ. After finishing my prayers, I made a proposal concerning the book to be prepared for the "Angelical writing" <note>The Enochian script or celestial language</note> and so forth. Behold, your labors are in vain compared to what you might have received. ...For August passed for you on the first day. And Mapsama is missing—not by his own fault, but through your negligence. His fingers worked and finished another task which was bound to a specific time. Nalvage <note>Another angelic spirit</note> was driven back from you; but you do not consider his struggle, nor do you thank God for what he has finished for you. You now have no power over Nalvage. For the Receiver and Giver for that period were bound to that time.

But so that the Heavens may agree (because they are the light of Him, who is the light of His Father), I say to you that you must prepare a book of fine and decent paper. This is so that the paper itself may bear witness against you and receive that which should have been printed in gold.

For Lasky doubted your faith and mocked God. But hear the voice of Him who sits on the throne: Lepers and defiled people are not permitted to carve meat at a King's table; for when his carvers become lepers, they cease to be carvers because they are expelled. Even so, the incredulous, proud, and scornful sinners do not enter into my chambers and secret judgments. Because he became worse than a leper, I banished him from my chambers, for I am more than a King. Nevertheless, because I have sworn to you on his behalf, I will allow him <margin>An oath to God for A. L. (Albertus Laski)</margin> to be exalted. But in the midst of his triumph he shall fall, just as a proud tree does when its roots are unstable.

It seems to approach a single (and likewise wonderful) combination and divine agreement. Two most illustrious Emperors sought me out when I was a young man: that most victorious Charles V and his brother Ferdinand, the most magnificent grandfather of your Imperial Majesty. The latter met me in Pozsony <note>modern-day Bratislava</note>, Hungary; the former in Brussels, Brabant. This was in the year 1563 for Ferdinand, and in the year 1549 for Charles. Furthermore, I began to hold in high esteem the most merciful Emperor Maximilian—your Imperial Majesty’s father, worthy of immortal glory—who was then already the crowned King of Hungary (much against the will of the Turkish Tyrant) in that same city of Pozsony in the year 1563. I endeavored, in a certain *Hieroglyphic* work <note>referring to Dee's book, *Monas Hieroglyphica*</note>, both to faithfully honor his rarest virtues and to recommend them most highly to posterity. While laboring through that task, my mind foresaw that there would one day be another member of the Austrian family in whom my greatest hope—and the best and greatest state of the public Christian world—would be confirmed (or could be confirmed). Therefore, to your Imperial Majesty, the **FOURTH** of the Roman Emperors from the most noble family of Austrian Princes to flourish in my lifetime: I am present, even I, the fourth letter of a triple alphabet. I am present in such a way that I offer myself to humbly kiss the feet of your Imperial Majesty, being greatly rejoiced if, in any matter, I can be pleasing or useful to so great and such an Emperor of the Christian Commonwealth.

The superscription was this: *To the most serene and powerful Prince and Lord, Lord Rudolph, by the Grace of God ever-august Emperor of the Romans, and King of Germany, Hungary, Bohemia, etc., Archduke of Austria, Duke of Burgundy, Styria, Carinthia, etc., Count of Tyrol, etc., my most merciful Lord.* If you will allow these things to be known to your Sacred Imperial Majesty alone (and are willing to reveal them to no one), you will be doing a most necessary thing. Prague, August 17, 1584. Your Imperial Majesty’s most humble and faithful little client, John Dee.

Tuesday, August 21. At Prague. After dinner, as we <note>Edward Kelley and John Dee</note> were in my study and conferring about my choice, and very sorry that we had not made the best choice, Edward Kelley saw the angel Uriel in the stone <note>The "stone" refers to the crystal or "shew-stone" used for scrying.</note>, which had not yet been put away. He said he had seen him there ever since we began. So, coming to the stone, he said as follows:

**Uriel:** Murmur not among yourselves, but rejoice and be glad, and sound out the greatness of God’s mercies, which bear all your weakness and lead you through the foggy and perilous mists of your daily temptations even by the hand. And now, he not only gives, but also exhorts. I speak with you as a man. Yea, let me speak with you as a man: you are oppressed with sin and with the world, and are not yet fit for the visitation of God. <margin>Wisdom shall not enter into a malevolent soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins. <note>original: "Kodolohus"</note> Rudolf II, first by letter, and then by speech: I thought it good to send the letter written previously for the Emperor by the Noble Don Guillermo de San Clemente, the King of Spain’s <term>Prefect of Affairs</term><note>original: "Præfectus Negotiorum"; an ambassador or high-ranking diplomatic agent</note> with this Emperor. Thereupon, by Emericus Sunttag, the Lord Laskie’s Secretary, I wrote this following letter to the aforementioned Don Clemente and sent it this St. Bartholomew’s Day [August 24].

"Such is the condition of men on earth (most Noble Sir) that no one seems to be born for himself alone. Indeed, no one receives all things necessary for himself by their own spontaneous growth, nor are they offered freely by others. From this, mutual societies of men have emerged: mutual friendships, mutual labors, mutual gifts, the exchange of goods, and contracts for buying and selling. Various other states of man exist, from which multiple duties and commerce are managed among men and with men.

Nor is the only goal or end which men strive to reach based on utility or (that which will perish) pleasure. Rather, for some, there is another purpose which is indeed more Divine, which we might call Virtue or Integrity. This, sent down from heaven, informs and adorns the minds of men and adapts them to itself, so much so that it renders them worthy of the celestial seats.

That—that, therefore, most Illustrious Sir—is what made your Excellency so attentive, kind, and thoroughly human toward me the other day. That is what will refresh your memory and notably sharpen your intellect in my cause, which is to be both proposed and commended to his Imperial Majesty. It must be handled in the manner that those Secrets <note>original: "Arcana"</note> ought to be handled: which are believed by few and understood by fewer still, even though they are most true and, in themselves, most useful. The sooner his Imperial Majesty embraces this wonderful and greatest Providence—and not only Providence, but also the goodness of God—the sooner and more abundantly the sincerity, goodness, and utility of my mission to him will be proven.

I would have wished to bring this enclosed book and the letters included for your Excellency myself. But (if I may be pardoned for saying so) because of a small injury to the skin of my toe, I cannot very conveniently come on foot today. Therefore, I have laid this burden upon my friend so that (with the kissing of your Excellency’s hands) he might offer you all my services and deliver this small gift, whatever it may be, for his Imperial Majesty. Prague, August 24, 1584. John Dee."

The <term>superscription</term><note>The address written on the outside of the letter</note> of this letter was as follows:

At length we let him go in his doublet and hose <note>term: doublet and hose; the standard male attire of the period, consisting of a close-fitting jacket and breeches</note>, without a cap or hat on his head. Into the street he hasted with his brother’s rapier drawn, and challenged Alexander to fight. But Alexander went away from him and said, "I will not, Mr. Kelley, I will not" <note>original: Nolo Domine Kelleie, Nolo</note>. 

Hereupon E.K. <note>Edward Kelley</note> took up a stone and threw it after him, as if at a dog, and so came into the house again in a most furious rage because he was not permitted to fight with Alexander. The rage and fury were so great in words and gestures that it might plainly prove that the wicked enemy <note>Satan</note> sought either E.K.’s own self-destruction, or the destruction of me, or his brother, and so forth. 

This may suffice to notify the mighty temptation and vehement working of the subtle spiritual enemy Satan, with which God suffered E.K. to be tempted and almost overcome. This was to my great grief, discomfort, and most great discredit; if it should have come to the Emperor’s understanding (as indeed it was the truth), it would have ruined me, unless he had known me well. I was in great doubt how God would take this offense, and I devised with myself how I might, with honesty, be cleared from the shame and danger that might arise if these two should fight. At the least, it would cross all good hope here with the Emperor for a time, until God redressed it. 

After I had brought E.K. to some quietness (by yielding much to his humor and saying little), not long after, a message came from my wife at Krakow <note>original: Cracovia</note>, and my servant Hugh came with him. This was to my great comfort through her letters, and the full satisfying of me by my servant Hugh’s knowledge of matters further than could conveniently be written. 

About 2 o'clock in the afternoon, this letter came to me regarding the Emperor sending for me:

> Noble and most illustrious Sir, my most respected Lord. The Emperor <note>original: Caesar</note> has just now signaled to the Spanish Ambassador, my master, that he should summon your Lordship to him at two o'clock, as he desires to hear certain things. If your Lordship can come at the stated hour, go immediately to Lord Octavius Spinola, who is the Master of the Stables and Chamberlain to his Imperial Majesty. He will introduce you to his Majesty. For the rest, I commend myself most dutifully again and again to your Lordship. Your Lordship’s most devoted, Arnold Vander Boxe.

<note>Note: The original letter itself is in this book. Octavius Spinola is Chamberlain and Master of the Stables in the absence of the officer who was sent into Spain.</note>

Emericus came up to me, and by that time the Chamberlain had come out to meet me. Through Emericus, he understood that I was the man the Emperor waited for. He came to me very courteously and told me of the Emperor’s desire...

heard of it from the Spanish Ambassador, as well as of my zealous mind toward his Grace. He commended the book *Monas*, but said that it was too difficult for his Majesty’s understanding. He added that the Spanish Ambassador told him I had something to say to him "which would be for his own benefit" <note>original Latin: "Quod esset pro sua utilitate"</note>. 

I answered, "So I have," and looking back to see if any other man was in the chamber, I found that we were alone. Thereupon I began to declare that I had spent my entire lifetime in learning. For forty years continually, in various ways and in diverse countries, with great pain, care, and cost, I had sought step by step to acquire the best knowledge that a man might attain in this world. I found at length that neither any living man, nor any book I could yet find, was able to teach me those truths I desired and longed for. 

Therefore, I resolved to make intercession and prayer to the Giver of wisdom and all good things, asking Him to send me such wisdom that I might know the natures of His creatures, and also enjoy the means to use them for His honor and glory. In this pursuit, I made various attempts; at length, it pleased God to send me His light <note>indicated by the Greek letter Delta, Dee's symbol for divine illumination</note>, by which I am assured of His merciful hearing of my long, fervent, constant, and continual prayer in the cause mentioned before. I told him that His holy Angels, for these past two years and a half, have been informing me; they have completed such works in my hands to be seen as no man's heart could have wished for more. Indeed, they have even brought me a stone <note>The "shew-stone" or crystal used by Dee and Edward Kelley for spirit scrying</note>...

And that these things are true, I protested, and took to witness the God of Heaven and Earth, "by whose commandment I am now before your Majesty," (said I) "and have a message from Him to say unto you; and that is this: The Angel of the Lord has appeared to me, and rebukes you for your sin. If you will hear me, and believe me, you shall triumph. If you will not hear me, the Lord—the God that made Heaven and Earth (under whom you breathe and have your spirit)—puts His foot against your breast, and will throw you headlong down from your seat. Moreover, the Lord has made this covenant with me (by oath) that He will do and perform: If you will forsake your wickedness and turn unto Him, your seat shall be the greatest that ever was, and the Devil shall become your prisoner." (Which Devil, I conjectured to be the Great Turk <note>The Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, often viewed as a primary spiritual and political enemy in this period.</note>, I said).

If I speak otherwise than I have just cause, I forsake my salvation," I said. The Emperor said he did believe me, and said that he thought I loved him unfeignedly, and said that I should not need such earnest protestations; and he would not willingly have had me kneel as often as I did. 

Furthermore, I said His Majesty was to see and understand plainly <note>original: "nakedly"</note>, from the beginning, the whole course of this angelical leading, instructing, and comforting of me. For I was commanded that I should, from the beginning, plainly open unto Rudolf <note>Emperor Rudolf II</note> the manner of God's visitation, and show unto him the holy vision; which charge I am ready to do. The Emperor said that at another time he would hear and understand more. I spoke yet somewhat more on the previous topics, with the intent they might take root or better stick in his mind. 

To be short, he thanked me and said he would henceforth take me into his recommendation and care; he used some such words of promised favor which I did not hear well, as he spoke so low. In the end, perceiving that his will was to finish for this time, I did my duty with a curtsy <note>A formal bow or gesture of respect used by both men and women at the time.</note>; and at the door going out, I turned back and curtsied, and so came into the next chamber. There, the noble Octavius Spinola came to me again and, with courteous words, offered me great friendship. I took my leave of him, and so came through the *Rittersaal* <note>original: "Ritters Stove," the Knight's Hall or Guard Chamber</note>, and so down and home. I had a full hour's audience with His Majesty.

To the most illustrious and magnificent Lord, the Chamberlain to his most respected Master:

Most Illustrious and Magnificent Lord: I cannot give sufficient or worthy enough thanks to your Magnificence for that singular humanity and benevolence with which you welcomed me yesterday. Though I am a man unknown to you, I am nonetheless a most devoted student of virtue and truth. I have decreed that I shall spend the entire remaining course of my life (God willing) ensuring that his Holy Imperial Majesty <note>Emperor Rudolf II</note> clearly perceives that the awesome Majesty of Almighty God will be incredibly (and almost certainly) favorable toward him. 

And although I see that his Holy Imperial Majesty is very often kept extremely busy with the manifold business of many regions, and that he neither can, nor by any evident reason should, easily find the leisure for other matters—specifically those causes I wish to propose to his Holy Imperial Majesty—**NEVERTHELESS**, if any way can be devised, according to the occasion of place, time, and circumstances, by which his Holy Imperial Majesty might deign to see those things in my possession, or understand from me those things which would be pleasing to him: in that matter, I would most willingly hear or receive the information and judgment of your most Illustrious Magnificence. 

For I shall be entirely devoted to this: that in due time it may appear that I am, and shall be, a most dedicated, most devoted, and most faithful servant of his Holy Imperial Majesty, for the service of Almighty God and his Holy Imperial Majesty (and especially for the illustration of the most Holy, Orthodox, Catholic, and Apostolic faith, and the defense and expansion of the Christian Commonwealth). 

September 5, 1584. 

The flower of opportunity must be gathered early, for it will quickly become withered. 

Your most Illustrious Magnificence’s most ready servant, 
**John Dee**.

***

Emericus went and delivered my letter to the Spanish Ambassador; but he brought it back again, saying that the Emperor had ridden out very early to Brandeis <note>original: Brandeish; a castle near Prague</note> or elsewhere (the location not being certainly known), and that this noble Octavius Spinola had gone with his Majesty. Thereupon I determined, by changing the date, to send it to him upon the Emperor’s Majesty returning to Prague. May God turn it to good. 

At noon today, I sent letters to my wife, to my Lord Lasky <note>Albertus Laski, a Polish nobleman and Dee's patron</note>, and to Mr. Paul Hertoll, by the messenger of Reichenstein, on this side of Neisse <note>original: Nisse</note>. Mr. Doctor Hagek’s son was present.

**Monday, September 7, 9:00 AM at Prague.**

**Tuesday, September 11, about 9:00 AM.**
I sent those letters to Lord Octavius Spinola—which I transcribed above—by way of Mr. Emericus Sontag, the Secretary to the Lord Palatine of Sieradz. **Wednesday, September 12, Morning.**
**[delta]**: This morning, when Emericus Sontag went up to the Castle for an answer from the Emperor by way of the Noble Octavius Spinola, he received the substance of this answer. I requested the same Emericus to write this down with his own hand (for various reasons); I have annexed his original handwriting here for greater credibility <note>original: "ad majorem rei fidem"</note>. **The Emperor’s Response, delivered through Lord Spinola:**
His Sacred Imperial Majesty has kindly understood what Mr. John Dee arranged to be proposed through His Majesty’s Chamberlain, Lord Octavius Spinola. To these matters, His Majesty has graciously resolved the following: Since he does not possess a perfect command of the Latin language in every respect, and furthermore, being occupied with various and manifold business, he cannot always find the leisure for an audience, it seems best to His Majesty that the same Mr. Dee should be willing to treat with and entrust his business to the Magnificent Lord Doctor Kurtz <note>Jacob Kurtz, a trusted advisor to Rudolph II</note>. Kurtz is a member of His Majesty’s Secret Council, is sufficiently faithful, and possesses distinguished learning. His Majesty will see to it that this is reported to his aforementioned Counselor, Kurtz. However, if it should seem otherwise to Mr. John Dee, His Majesty will satisfy Mr. Dee’s desire whenever he is eventually able to do so amidst his preoccupations. 

September 12, 1584. Written by Emericus Sontag’s own hand at Prague. **[delta]**.

This answer was received both by word of mouth and in writing. This service is intended chiefly for His honor and glory; secondly, for the comfort of the godly and the elect; and thirdly, for the confusion of the proud, arrogant, and scornful enemies of truth and virtue. I suspected that some of our misdeeds were the cause of the Lord refraining from answering. Thereupon, I began to pray for mercy, grace, and deliverance from the assaults and malicious purposes of the Devil against us. I did this especially because, just as I felt the presence of my good Angel (or another good friend) in virtue, I also sensibly felt *Pilosum* <note>Latin: "The Hairy One," a term often used for a demonic or satyr-like spirit</note> busily working to terrify me with my past offenses, or to make me lose hope of being heard at this time. But I continued to pray various Psalms, and at length, I prayed specifically against the wicked tempters. 

After my prayers, I assured E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s medium or "scryer"</note> that the spiritual enemy was busy here and intended to frustrate today’s Action. He answered that the enemy could not prevail against him or accuse him for his recent notable fault; for he had made an account and sorrowfully bewailed that trespass to the Lord, and he did not doubt he was forgiven. He said he was so reconciled to God that neither Satan nor any other wicked accuser could make him doubt God’s mercy. He spoke very well regarding repentance, God’s mercies, His justice, and these spiritual Actions. However, he confessed that, by reason of his nature, he himself was an unfit person to come before the Emperor or Princes; therefore, if it would please God to discharge him of further involvement, he might feel more at ease. 

At length, after an hour, Uriel appeared, but with a scarf before his face, just as he had last time.

And therefore, you are sinners unworthy to behold the face of true light and understanding. 

For there is a double reconciliation: 
1. One (and the first) is between the Conscience and the Judge, through the force of faith and repentance; that is to say, reconciliation against Judgment. 
2. Another (the second) is reconciliation between the Spirit of Truth (the Church of God) and man’s conscience. <margin>See above, September 5: The eye was commanded to be reconciled to the Spirit of Truth.</margin>

Behold, I teach you a mystery: 
1. Those who are at one with God shall not be judged with the wicked in the last Judgment. Nevertheless, the Justice of God is pure and undefiled, and does not suffer man’s faults to go unpunished. 
2. But he who is at one with the Spirit of God is made one with Him, and is without punishment. For there are many things that God bears witness of in the soul and secret chambers of man, which neither the blessed (already dignified or yet to be dignified) do or can know; which is the cause that the soul...

May they be protected. Amen. Saturday, September 15. About one o'clock in the afternoon. At Prague.

I came to the aforementioned man (called Doctor) Curtz <note>original: Cirtz; likely Jacob Curtz von Senftenau, a diplomat and scientist</note> about one o'clock in the afternoon. He had been ready to hear me all day if I had wished it, but I had sent him word in the morning by Emericus that I would come to him in the afternoon, as I have now done at this hour. 

Upon my arrival, he entertained me courteously. Two chairs being placed at the end of the table, he gave me the seat of honor (through a friendly kind of earnestness). Then he told me that long ago in Germany, he had heard of my fame and had seen my writings. He said he was very glad for the opportunity of my coming to this city and was otherwise desirous of my acquaintance—but chiefly because His Majesty the Emperor, by word of his own mouth <note>original: Ore tenus</note>, had commanded him to hear what I had to say to His Majesty.

I began by declaring my long course of study over forty years, always advancing by degrees and desiring the best and purest truths in every field of study I had pursued. I explained that I had mastered as many subjects as are commonly known, and more than are commonly heard of. But at length, I perceived that only God (and through his good Angels) could satisfy my <gloss>the goal of my studies</gloss> desire: which was to understand the natures of all His creatures, and the best way to use them for His divine honor and glory, the comfort of the chosen <term>the elect</term>, and also for the rebuke and confusion of those who oppose His name and honor. 

I explained that I had attempted this in various ways. At length, I found the mercies of God were such that He sent me the instruction of Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Uriel, and various others of His good and faithful messengers. I told him I had now brought about eighteen books here to show him the manner of their proceedings. I thought it best to begin with the last book, which most concerned the current Emperor, Rudolf. 

And so I did; and by moving lightly from book to book, I gave him a taste or sight of the greater part of them. I also let him see the Stone <note>The "shew-stone" or crystal used by Dee for scrying</note> brought to me by angelic ministry, and so forth. After he had seen and heard everything I could show him over the course of six hours, he finally asked me what conclusion or summary report he should make to the Emperor. 

I answered that he should report based on what he had seen and heard. However, I suggested that if he would follow my counsel (as one somewhat <gloss>My counsel to Doctor Curtz</gloss> experienced in these divine and angelic dealings), he should tell His Majesty to thank God for His great mercies and graces offered. I told him that I was one who most sincerely and faithfully informed His Majesty of the will of God in this matter. I said His Majesty should do as Mary (the blessed Virgin) did: to lay up all these informations in his heart, and to say, "Behold <note>original: Ecce; likely referring to 'Ecce ancilla Domini'—Behold the handmaid of the Lord</note>..."

"I am the servant of the Lord; let your will be done," <note>original Latin: *servus Domini, fiat voluntas tua*</note> and so I intended to wait for the manner of the Lord's proceeding, while framing my life as it becomes every Christian to do. He said that he would write down (to help his own memory) some short notes of his observations regarding my speeches and the things he had seen and noted. He added that tomorrow (being Sunday) or on Monday, if he conveniently could, he would make a report to the Emperor, and then with all speed let me know further of his Imperial Majesty's will and pleasure. Thereupon, he courteously escorted me down to the street door of his house; and I came home after half-past seven in the evening. The mercies of God be upon me, and may his name be magnified and extolled in this world and forever. Amen.

**Note.** In the meantime, while I was thus occupied with the aforementioned Mr. Curtz, E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s scryer and assistant</note> was visited at our lodging by a wicked tempter <note>likely a spiritual apparition or demonic entity</note> who denied that any Christ existed. This tempter claimed that just as the heart receives comfort from all the members of the body, so he who is God receives comfort from all things through the Angels and other members of the world. He also claimed that I was now with a man who would use me like a serpent, encircling me from head to tail to bring about my confusion, and so on. He earnestly reviled E.K. in various ways, saying that E.K. would be damned, and moreover, that no fruitful end would ever come of our practices. <note>The Greek letter delta [Δ] is Dee's personal symbol for himself.</note> May the eternal and Almighty God confound the adversaries of his truth and glory, and of his Son Jesus Christ, our Redeemer and the triumphant conqueror over Hell, sin, and the Devil. Amen.

->**PRAGUE**<-

On Monday and Tuesday, the 17th and 18th of September, I sent Emericus <note>Emeric Sontag, Dee's servant</note> up to the Castle to listen for an answer regarding Doctor Curtz's report to the Emperor about what he had gathered from me. (But on Monday, Octavius Spinola <note>A chamberlain to Emperor Rudolf II</note> had sent into the town for Emericus and told him that the Emperor was anxious and desired to understand my dealings with the Doctor. Therefore, he asked Emericus if I had been with the Doctor, and he confirmed that I had. "The Emperor will be glad of this," he said. And yet, as I began to note, when Emericus came on Tuesday into the presence of the Doctor in the *Rittersaal* <note>original: "Ritters stove," meaning the Knights' Hall or a heated assembly room in the palace</note>, not one word was spoken to him regarding whether the Doctor had spoken to the Emperor or not.)

Therefore, I suspect that the Doctor is not dealing honestly, faithfully, or wisely in such a weighty case. And since he told me that his Majesty the Emperor was persuaded that he <note>the Emperor</note> was pious, etc., perhaps the Doctor would be loath now to introduce me to speak with the Emperor, seeing that both he himself and the rest of his council were persuaded to the contrary regarding this King <note>likely referring to the spiritual "King" or authority Dee claimed to represent</note>. Because of this, a great delay might follow based on a malicious <note>original: "sinister"</note> report made to the Emperor.

**Note.** Friday, September 21. Around 10 o'clock, nearly. <note>original Latin: *Circa horam 10. Ferè*</note>

# Morning. At Prague. <note>original: Mane. + Pragæ.</note>

As I and Edward Kelley <note>original: E.K.</note> were together in my study, earnestly discussing private confession <note>original: Auricular confession</note>, public confession, and confessing to God alone, as well as the authority of the Church and the way that same authority is used to release or retain sins, Edward Kelley saw someone walking on the table between him and me. Thereupon, I prepared myself to write and note what should be shown or said. Edward Kelley asked me to set down the crystal ball <note>original: shew-stone</note>; so I did, and he looked into it.

**Edward Kelley:** I see him here with a scarf over his head and face down to his waist, but I see his hair is yellow on the back of his head, etc.

> Send out your light, O God, and your truth, so that they may lead us out of this valley of misery to the Holy Mount Zion, and to your heavenly Tabernacles. Amen. <note>original: Mitte lucem tuam, O Deus et veritatem tuam ut ipsæ nos ducant ex hac valle miseriæ ad montem Sanctum Sion, et ad cælestia tua Tabernacula. Amen.</note>

**Uriel:** I am Uriel, the servant of the most wise, mighty, and everlasting God. I visit you for two reasons. The first is that I may open unto you true and perfect light—such as darkness cannot understand—infallible and true nourishment, the power and spirit of the everlasting God. The second is that I may counsel you against the world and teach you to triumph against her stubbornness <note>original: frowardness</note>. For who has trusted in the Lord and been cast down? Or who is he that has cried aloud and is not heard? Therefore, I say to you: Hear my voice. For I am of the truth, set against darkness, and through me are published the light and mysteries of the Trinity from time to time, and in all ages, to those who fear and obey God. There are two things which are the seals and marks of Satan, which bring eternal death and damnation to all those who are marked or branded with them: that is to say, lying and stubborn silence.

Behold the words of Christ regarding the subtle: "Your father is a liar from the beginning, and the Devil." Hearken to my voice: He that [1] teaches false doctrine, [2] opens his mouth against the truth, or [3] defrauds his brother is a liar and shall not be forgiven. 

1. For first, he sins against his Creator, who created all things in truth. 
2. Secondly, he offends against the truth and his Redeemer, who is the Son of God, the true Christ. 
3. Thirdly, he offends against the Spirit of God (of the Father and the Son), the Holy Ghost; which shall not be forgiven. 

And therefore, he incurs the rigor of God’s justice: his eternal damnation. But, I say, give ear to my words: for I will sift the dust and find out the pearl that for a long time has lain...

### Monday, September 24. 8:00 AM. Prague.

**[delta]** <note>Dee uses the Greek letter delta to represent himself in his journals.</note> At the first looking, **Edward Kelley** saw **Uriel**, but he was covered with his scarf, etc. Nevertheless, I said some prayers to God on my knees, and came and said here:

> Send out your light and your truth, O God: let them lead us to Mount Zion, etc. <note>original Latin: "Mitte lucem tuam et veritatem tuam O Deus: ut ipsæ nos ducant ad montem Sion, etc."</note>

It should be remembered that we returned to the **Shew-stone** <term>a polished stone or crystal used for scrying or spirit communication</term> for two reasons. First, because of the letter I had written to the **Emperor** <note>Rudolf II, Holy Roman Emperor</note>; I intended to show it to the **Spanish Ambassador** before sending it to the Emperor, to get his opinion on it and to have him deliver it. 

Secondly, because of foul, slanderous words spoken about me here at this Ambassador’s table: namely, that I was a **conjurer** <term>a magician who summons spirits, often used pejoratively</term> and a bankrupt **alchemist**, and that I came here only to get money from the Emperor. They also claimed I had sold my goods and given the money to **Lord Lasky** <note>Albertus Laski, a Polish nobleman and patron of Dee and Kelley</note>, and that he had deceived me. Just as the accursed and cast down <note>referring to fallen angels or demons</note> most willfully abhor, hate, and dishonor the God of Justice because of His might and power over them; so do all those who suck and hang upon the breasts of the world—those who are covetous and desirous of worldly promotion, and who gape and thirst after the glory of this world. For truly, as they are, so shall you be; and as they are made righteous by reason of their election <term>divine choice or predestination</term> and crowned for eternal joy, so shall your election establish your righteousness and give you garlands of eternal comfort.

But it is not so with you; for you dwell in castles made of marble, carved out of the middle of a sure rock—a most stable foundation. For why? I am sure that God dwells in you, and you in Him. For God, and for the sake of God, as befits a servant of your Sacred Imperial Majesty: I see, however, that since I have received no response to my previous messages, I am somewhat driven by the sting of such a deep silence to admonish your Imperial Majesty a second time. 

Do not suspect or believe in any way that this divine Mercy—offered by God, so unexpected, so great, so unheard of, so wonderful, so multifaceted, so necessary to the state of the Empire and the Christian Commonwealth, so certain, so ready, and to be confirmed and administered to you in actual fact by the faithful servant of Almighty God and your Imperial Majesty (if your Sacred Imperial Majesty had willed it)—is, was, or will be a matter of small importance, or some human invention, or a Diabolical fraud. 

For I greatly fear that by such a grave error on the part of your Imperial Majesty, the fury of Almighty God could be kindled. I deeply dread that by rejecting this mercy of God, you may provoke His indignant vengeance. Therefore, since I see that Heaven itself and such celestial mysteries are not yet of such great concern to your Sacred Imperial Majesty as I had indeed hoped, I have reached a decision. 

Rather than allow God to have absolutely no visible judgment, proof, testimony, or experiment among men regarding this (previously unheard of) Mercy—offered spontaneously to your Imperial Majesty—and rather than let my often-mentioned faithfulness, sincerity, and devotion (or vow) toward God and your Imperial Majesty lack all credibility and the strength of manifest truth among our descendants: In the Name of God, and to His praise, honor, and glory, and so that I may satisfy your Serene Imperial Majesty’s heroic desire regarding that **Blessed Stone** (called the **Philosophers' Stone** <note>original: *lapide Philosophorum*; the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and granting long life</note>), I assert to your Sacred Imperial Majesty that I can, by seeing, possessing, and using it infallibly, manufacture that same stone with Divine help and favor.

After my return home, I found E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s spirit medium</note> resolved to leave from here tomorrow to get his wife, <gloss>E.K. ready to go into England, as he claimed.</gloss> and then go straightway into England. **Friday, September 28. Prague.**

Intending to send the Emperor’s letter (written here previously) to his Majesty by my good friend, the Spanish Ambassador, I wrote this letter to send to the Ambassador on that behalf, and concerning the credibility of these Actions:

To the most illustrious Lord, Lord Don Guillermo de San Clemente, Ambassador of the most serene and Catholic King of the Spains to his Sacred Imperial Majesty, etc., his most respected Lord.

Illustrious and Magnificent Hero:

It can be proven by many testimonies and examples that those mysteries which are divinely revealed to men (even to those who are indeed pious and sincere)—mysteries which are new and beyond the decrees of common arts and sciences, and above the common expectation of scholars—are either understood by very few with the greatest difficulty, or are hardly admitted or believed by the many without suspicion. 

But what kind of suspicion can there be in our affairs, if a right and piously informed judgment is applied? For wisdom has been sought from Almighty God faithfully, ardently, and constantly through prayers for many years now. This alone (namely, that which is within our power) seems to be the root and occasion for obtaining so great a gift. But the mercy and grace of Almighty God toward us, determined and assigned in His celestial Palace before the world was founded, must be considered the chief, solid, and immovable foundation of this great mystery. 

In this mystery, there shines such introductory information <note>original: "Isagogica Informatio"</note> through powerful and faithful Angels concerning the secret counsels of God—as much in the creation of the world and the natures and true use of Creatures, as in the state of the present and soon-to-be future world. And furthermore, concerning the holiness, dignity, and authority of the one Catholic Church (the most dear spouse of Jesus Christ and our pious mother), just as in her there is also the Communion of Saints and the remission of sins; and concerning many great secrets and determinations of God not yet to be revealed by us. 

This is so far from the truth that any Christian of sound mind should strive to contend—or even be able to suspect—that our mystical actions are diabolical frauds. Rather, one should incredibly admire such a secret purpose of God, subjugate human reason in examining the same, and [praise] God’s admirable [mercy] toward His elect...

I most humbly and with the greatest trembling wish to confess that mercy is manifest in these matters. Indeed, until now, I find myself to be nothing else in these affairs but the pen of a scribe writing swiftly through me. For I have been accustomed to record most faithfully the things seen and heard in my presence—sometimes letter for letter, sometimes word for word, and sometimes receiving many words at the same moment they are delivered. But now, into how many volumes has this labor of ours grown? From all of these, we expect such fruit and success as He has ordained, to whose nod all things obey. 

As for these letters of mine to his Sacred Imperial Majesty: when your Magnificence finds the first opportunity, if you would deign to present them most humbly to him in my name, then I shall be relieved of a great burden enjoined upon me by God. Then, too, I shall have received a great favor from your Magnificence. 

In the meantime, while a response from his Sacred Imperial Majesty to these letters is awaited (certainly if it must be waited for 14 or 16 days), or immediately after receiving a response (if I can receive it as quickly as I received the last one), I must prepare myself for a journey. This is on account of my family, books, and some of my household goods, which must be transferred here before the harshness of winter. There, with the gracious favor of his Imperial Majesty and under his Imperial Protection, I will be able to be ready from time to time to fulfill the will of Almighty God to the best of my strength, and to serve his Sacred Imperial Majesty most faithfully as his Philosopher and Mathematician.

Your Illustrious Magnificence’s most devoted,
John Dee.

However, as far as I was concerned, His Imperial Majesty was prepared to gratify and benefit me in whatever matter might fall under his Authority.** <note>original: *Quantum autem ad me attinebat, paratam esse suam Cæsaream Majestatem mihi gratificari et benefacere in quacumque re quæ illius subjiceret Authoritati*</note>

Thereupon I answered and said: **I am sorry that my words were understood or conceived by His Imperial Majesty in a different sense than they ought to have been understood. For I did not desire to become his Confessor, but I was commanded to signify to him—as I have done—that his sins had been rebuked from heaven. From this he could draw more consolation than from the counsel of any of his friends or his Confessor rebuking his sins; for it declared the extraordinary favor of the Lord God, etc.** <note>original: *Doleo verba mea in alio sensu intellecta... **As for that favor which His Imperial Majesty offered me, I accepted it most humbly. Now, the reason I desire to be honored with the title of Imperial Philosopher and Mathematician is manifold: partly in respect to my secret service to the Emperor, using that title as a pretext to hide it; and partly for the sake of having greater authority and favor among the Imperialists and my fellow Englishmen. This is so that I do not appear to be dealing in trifles or to be of no reputation, and so that I do not seem a fit target for those who have begun to exercise their envious and most slanderous tongues against me with impunity, etc.** <note>original: *Nunc vero quod desiderem titulo Philosophi... exercerent linguam impune*</note>

I therefore prayed **Dr. Curtz** <note>Jacob Curtz von Senftenau, an Imperial diplomat and scientist</note> to remind His Imperial Majesty of the undue interpretation of those words by which his vices were rebuked, etc.

<note>Jacob Curtz (also known as Curtius) was the Vice-Chancellor to Holy Roman Emperor Rudolf II and a fellow mathematician.</note> Curtz came out from the Emperor to meet me. I asked him if he had told the Emperor of the grief I felt because he had misunderstood my words. He said yes, and that the Emperor did not take it in a bad way. We talked of various other things while walking up and down together for about a quarter of an hour. Among other things, I told him that the Lord Ambassador <note>likely the English Ambassador to the Imperial Court</note> would deliver my letters himself to the Emperor’s Majesty. Then I departed, and he returned back to the Emperor in the privy chamber.

**Sunday, October 7, at 7:00 in the morning.** <note>original: "Mane bora 7"</note> I sent a messenger to the Lord Ambassador’s house, and there I learned that the Ambassador had yesterday delivered my letter to his Majesty, and that an answer was to be expected through Doctor Curtz. 

After dinner, I went to Doctor Curtz’s lodging. He had nothing as yet to say regarding the letter delivered by the Lord Ambassador. However, we fell into other conversation, and I told him plainly that I had not lived in obscurity until now, nor had I been careless in maintaining and increasing my good reputation and name. Therefore, if I should seem to be despised, disregarded, or treated as a mere trifler despite my sincere dealings here, I felt I would be greatly wronged. I told him I was sure that the Emperor’s Majesty was much guided by him, and that as he formed his judgment, so did his Majesty very often resolve matters such as mine. Therefore, if I were not treated reasonably in my affairs, and in a manner befitting the Emperor’s honor, the blame would be laid to no other man’s charge but his, and so on. He promised that he would deliver everything in the best words he could, in a friendly manner, and so on. 

After this, he showed me several of his labors and inventions—mathematical and especially arithmetical tables—both for improving <term>Nomius's</term> <note>referring to Pedro Nunes, a Portuguese mathematician</note> invention of the quadrant divided into 90, 91, 92, 93 parts, and so on. I then revealed to him the secret of my glass <note>likely a concave mirror or optical device</note> for battering <note>possibly signaling or projecting light</note> in a dark night, and so on. He said that such a device would be very acceptable to his Majesty. I told him that the glass was at <term>Cracovia</term> <note>modern Krakow, Poland</note>, and his Majesty should see it by God’s leave. 

After this, I told him that I would very much like to have a passport or safe conduct to pass quietly and safely through any of the Emperor’s dominions. He thought his Majesty would willingly grant that, and asked me to write three or four lines as I would have it. He instructed me to write thus: 

*John Dee, an Englishman and most devoted servant of his most Serene Majesty, most humbly prays his Imperial Majesty that, for his greater security of conscience during his travels through the most extensive Empire of his Imperial Majesty, he would deign to grant him letters of safe passage. John Dee.* <note>original Latin: "Cæsaream suam Majestatem humillime orat Joannes Dee Anglus, serenissime suæ Majestatis Devotissimus servitor, ut pro sua majora in Intineribus per amplissimum suæ Cæsareæ Majestatis Imperium conscientis securitate, literas salvi passus sibi concedere dignaretur. Joannes Dee."</note>

Upon coming home, I reconsidered that I would prefer the said passport, safe conduct, or letters of passage to be more ample and beneficial—covering my wife, children, family, servants, and all my goods whatsoever.

Is the workmanship of God revealed fully to sinners? God forbid. Moses saw only the back parts of God <note>referring to Exodus 33:23</note>. To whom you are hateful, or crave the bread which is due and necessary for his children and servants. Notwithstanding, out of his mercy—and because he knew before the beginning of all worlds the corruption of your vessels <note>The "vessel" refers to the human body or soul as a container for spirit.</note>, and remembering that you have been of his household—he has mercifully winked at you and your presumption until now. But now, considering that you continue in your wickedness, continue in your rebellion against his Majesty, and fight daily <note>original: "das'y", likely an OCR error for "daily"</note> under his banner which is accursed, he takes his bread from you, shuts his doors against you, warns his servants against you, and has become a firebrand of wrath against you. 

But here you will say: "Were we not of that number to whom he made a promise?" You were so, but upon condition: that you would bridle your tongues from speaking evil and become wholly his. But you are neither his, nor do you bridle your tongues; instead, you speak blasphemy before the Lord and the messengers of his light and covenant. Therefore, you are not inheritors of his promise.

Behold, while the grapes grew and the corn ripened, God expected your return, for no hour is unacceptable to him. But now the harvest comes when the corn must be cut down and the grapes pressed; you are not as you said you would be, nor as you promised. Therefore you are excluded, for no strangers enter the vineyard, nor do any hirelings enter this harvest, for it is not the harvest of man. 

Now, either fulfill your promise and return from the multitude of your sins, or do not murmur though you be sent out of doors. The earth of itself brings forth nothing, for it is the lump and excrement of darkness, whose bowels are a burning lake. But where the heavens <note>original: "beavens", an OCR error for "heavens"</note> yield, and the Sun pours down his force, she opens herself and becomes spongy, receiving mixture for generation, and so is exalted above herself and brings forth for the use of man. Even so is the body when it lies in the puddle and hotchpotch of its earthly filthiness and darkness, making itself equal with beasts, whose dignity exists only in their usefulness.

**E.K.** <note>Edward Kelley, John Dee's medium or "scryer."</note> Now he is here again. 

Two things you have to be instructed in: in <term>Rlodnr</term> <note>An Enochian term likely related to the alchemical or spiritual process being described.</note> and in the <term>Law of Coition and Mixture</term> <note>In this context, "coition" refers to the alchemical joining or union of substances or spiritual forces.</note>. The first is the instrument working and drawing things together of one nature. The second is the bounds and terms wherein every mixture consists, and beyond which it cannot go. The first consists of four parts; every part containing its contents doubled. The first is <term>Topens</term> <note>Another Enochian term; here described as the foundational principle that teaches the others.</note>; this teaches the rest. These two things I can open to you in two revolutions, which is but one day's work. But now I cease to reveal any more to you until I see the favor of God more open toward you. After seven days I will come again; until then, I neither am, nor speak.

part of Nothing distributed, as it were approaching near unto God: God made the soul of <margin>Time. Angels. The soul was made spiritual and increasing, a concept wherein the philosophers—the wise men of this world—are deceived. The Spirit of God (joined with the Trinity) works with him in his infinity.

Behold, in the beginning God did not formally number all souls that shall enter into these vessels <note>original: "vessels," meaning human bodies</note> or any other part. Adam fell; he transgressed God's commandment, and therefore was his soul darkened, bare, and naked. This was because he lacked the beauty and excellency of God's Spirit, with which God had dignified him and made him like unto Himself, being a living soul. He was cast out, and now casts off misery, lacking the knowledge of those things for which he was created.

Now God, the image of his Father, grieved at the fall of man and moved with pity, vouchsafed <note>condescended or granted out of grace</note>—because of the excellency of man—to enter into man. He entered into this "part of nothing," into man, though he had been separated before. It was not that he would beautify himself with anything that man had, but that, having become man and being begotten of the Holy Ghost, he might (as you know by the Scriptures) make man acceptable again to God his Father.

God himself exists with God in unity: for Justice and Terror is God the Father; Mercy and Love is God the Son; Wisdom and Knowledge is God the Holy Ghost. Since he became man, he did not put on the flesh of man to become a liar, but so that the flesh of man might be full of the spirit of truth and understanding.

If his Apostles have left us examples of belief, have taught us how to believe, and upon what rock and foundation to fasten our belief, then simply and nakedly follow the steps of true Faith, and laying reason aside, believe. 

But note here, that this Sacrament is to be ministered among the Apostles—among the Ministers and true Servants of God in his Church—and not in the temple of the Scribes and Pharisees, Hypocrites, and Deceivers. While they tear Jesus Christ and his body according to the perversity <note>original: "frowardnesse"</note> of their own senses, they eat (as Judas did) and so perish eternally. But I say...
