<meta>This page continues a theological discourse regarding the nature of the Eucharist and the Real Presence of Christ in the Sacrament.</meta>

unto you, and teach you, that wheresoever in the true Church of God remembrance is made, and the use of this Sacrament is celebrated—the true body and blood of Jesus Christ crucified—there is also the true body of Christ, God and man substantially, and the bread of eternal comfort and food. This is for those who humbly, openly, and penitently receive it, acting as an atonement <note>original: "propitiatory"</note> for the living <note>original: "quick"</note> and the dead. This does not apply to those who are dead in sin, in hell, or departed from this life, but to those who are sinners here, and thus "dead" in spirit and in need of revival. For he who dwells in Christ is alive, because he dwells in life and light. But he who leaves Christ through sin, and in whom Christ does not dwell, he is dead. For this, I have spoken.

<margin>The words of Consecration pronounced.</margin>
[delta] Lord, what shall we say to the Priests when they want us to acknowledge Transubstantiation <note>The doctrine that the bread and wine change entirely into the substance of Christ's body and blood.</note>, and so forth?

The bread that was administered by Christ to his Disciples was not a mere figure of his body, but his true body. So the Minister, acting in the office and person of Christ, by pronouncing the words of consecration, also gives to the people not mere bread, but the true body. But hear me: You must consider it as a Sacrament, and must believe as the Disciples did, that it is the true Body of Christ which you eat in the form of bread <note>original: "Sub forma panis"</note>.

[delta] Concerning receiving the sacrament under both kinds <note>The practice of the laity receiving both the bread and the wine, rather than just the bread.</note>, what is your doctrine?

Flesh and blood make and constitute the body <note>original: "Caro et sanguis faciunt corpus et constituunt"</note>.

[delta] Then it is no offense to God to receive under one kind only.

[delta] Concerning the worshiping of it when it is lifted up by the Priest.

<margin>The remembrance of. Christ can be everywhere. Under the form of bread.</margin>

---

That, by faith (in that it is believed to be the true body), is also by faith to be worshiped: Not because it has the shape of bread, but because it is the body of Christ, true God and man.

[delta] Concerning also the reserving of it <note>Keeping the consecrated bread in a tabernacle for later use.</note> after it has been consecrated, what are we to understand?

Reason has no place here: To those who receive it, it is a Sacrament. But when the receiving stops, the Sacrament also stops. It is a Sacrament and a Sacrifice to those celebrating and receiving; when the celebration ceases and no one is receiving, the Sacrament and Sacrifice cease <note>original: "Celebrandi, et accipientibus, Sacramentum et Sacrificium est: Cessante celebratione, et nullis accipientibus, cessat Sacramentum et Sacrificium."</note>. For a Sacrament is defined by its institution and the manner of its use. The meaning consists in both.

Tomorrow you shall hear more from me; in the meantime, consider how merciful God is to you through me, and explain this doctrine also to your wives, so that they may also know God truly.

[delta] Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will <note>original: "Gloria in excelsis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis."</note>.

<meta>This page continues the record of a spiritual conference, following a discussion on the union of visible signs and spiritual realities.</meta>

I demonstrated to you yesterday how the visible sign or matter that appeared was united and joined to the invisible thing it signified. In that discussion, I answered in my own form and person; for whoever speaks of God and Christ while expounding the Scriptures ought to speak plainly, truly, and openly, so that what they say may be understood. This is the duty of a preacher. Even so, I—speaking of God and being illuminated for this duty for a time—was humble <note>original: "bare"</note>, because I did not speak of myself. 

But the doctrine I taught you was true. It is worthy to be engraved in golden tablets and placed as a monument upon the altar, where man may see, as in a mirror, how God—through his Sacraments and holy institutions—sanctifies, regenerates, and purifies man for himself. 

<margin>G1</margin> Now to the work intended, which is called in the Holy Art *Gebofal* <note>A term likely derived from the Hebrew "Gevurah" (strength/severity), referring here to a specific branch of Enochian or angelic magic</note>. This is not (as the philosophers have written) the first supernatural step; rather, it is the first supernatural step naturally limited to the 48 Gates of Wisdom, where your holy Book begins. The final step is speaking with God as Moses did, which is infinite. All the other steps have proper limits within which they are contained. 

But understand that "this one work" <note>original: *hoc opus unum*</note> receives multiplication and increase in status <note>original: "dignifieation"</note> by ascending through all the other steps, which are limited according to their own qualities. I have laid a sure foundation of this knowledge; I have taught what it is, the instrument used for it, and the means by which it exists. I have shown the manner of proceeding and its basis. So, nothing is lacking now but the simple and easy untying <note>original: "unkottting"</note> of those things that are wrapped up—not by the nature of the work itself, but by the obscurity and misty <note>original: "caliginous"</note> cloud of your own ignorance. If the cloud is within you, then it must be removed by your own help and consent.

<margin>Δ</margin> <note>This symbol represents John Dee</note> By the favor and help of the Highest, we trust the cloud shall be removed.

...Take heed, therefore, that you do not become conceited, presuming against reason (which binds you together) and the will of God (which teaches you obedience). 

<margin>G2</margin> For pride is hateful before God, and to be in love with yourselves is the greatest ignorance. Shall a dark cellar <note>original: "seller"</note> brag or boast of her beauty because she receives light and clarity from a candle brought into her, or shining into her? You can do no more, [E.K.] <note>Edward Kelley, Dee's medium</note>, for the ripeness of your wit and understanding comes through our presence and our illumination. If we depart, you shall become a dark cellar again and shall think too well of yourself in vain. 

Fuel <note>original: "Matter"</note> is lacking among you; the fire cannot continue. But when you bring more wood, you shall have more fire. I will not visit you again until the seventh day.

<margin>Δ</margin> To our Almighty God, eternal, true, and living, be all praise, honor, glory, and thanksgiving, now and forever. Amen.

If you seek eternal life, or study to please God and glorify him—which is the purpose for which you were created—separate yourselves from the Harlot <note>original: "Harlot"; likely referring to the Roman Catholic Church or a corrupt spiritual state in this prophetic context</note>. Swear yourselves to be her enemy, and hate all those who take part with her. For behold, she has become an enemy of him who created you, a blasphemer of him whom you seek to glorify, and the daughter of him who set himself against the Highest <note>referring to Lucifer or the Antichrist</note>. Therefore, for the sake of your creation, you ought to despise her. For the sake of your redemption, you should neglect her; and for the glory that you seek to attain, you must utterly despise or scorn her.

But here, perhaps, you will say to me as the man said to Christ, the Son of the living God—
<margin>E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, the medium/scryer for John Dee</note> bows and kisses the ground.</margin>
"What shall I do to inherit everlasting life?" I say to you: follow the Commandments. Behold, it is written, "I give you a new commandment: Love one another." How can you love one another without charity? But what is charity? Is it not the gift of the Holy Spirit? You know it is so; you also know that the Holy Spirit is called a Comforter. But consider within yourselves why he is called a Comforter. It is not because he comforts himself, for he is all comfort; rather, it is because he is the comfort of those to whom he has spoken, saying, "I have given you a new commandment: Love one another."

But who are they? They are those who eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, Jesus Christ, the Son of God—true God and man. Unless you do this, you are not of that company to whom Christ said, "I give you a new commandment." For by doing so, you are grafted into Christ, are subject to the commandment, and are tied to charity. In this state, you are refreshed by the Holy Spirit, the continual Comforter and giver of wisdom to those who dwell in Christ.

See, therefore, that no one belongs to Christ who does not have charity; nor does anyone have charity who is not among the company of those who feed on the flesh and blood of Jesus Christ, without which there is no salvation. Therefore, you, E.K., are a liar when you say, "I fear God, I love God, I intend to live well and in obedience," for you do not follow his commandments. You fly from him; therefore, you are not with him.
<margin>* [delta] <note>John Dee's symbol for himself</note> E.K. confessed that he thought so at this instant. Penance. The Church. Fleeing to the Catholic Church <note>original: "Ad Ecclesiam Catholicam consugiendam"</note>.</margin>

But I hear you saying, "I confess myself to Christ before the throne of God." Yet you have not offered yourself to the priest, nor have you laid down your sacrifice. I say to you: you do not truly confess yourself, nor your sins, before God, because you do not come to where he is. It is not that God does not see you, but it is said that he does not hear sinners unless they are penitent. Penance is defined by the Church, and your sorrow is not to be judged by yourself alone. It is necessary, therefore, if you wish to fly to Christ, to enter into the company of those who profess him, where he is present.

## 1585. At Prague. February 23. Saturday. About 2 o'clock in the afternoon. After pouring out prayers to God for light and divine truth, etc. <note>original: "Pragæ. Februarii 23. Saturday A meridie horam circiter 2. Orationibus ad Deum fusis, pro luce et veritate divina, etc."</note> [Dee]

The occasion for coming to the Show-Stone <note>The crystal or "shew-stone" used for scrying</note> was that as we sat together in the heated room <note>original: "Stove"</note>, there was a pat or a stroke or two (not natural) given on the bench and wall. At the same time, I felt a heavy moving thing on my head, and after that, E.K. felt something on his back, as if someone had distinctly written letters. Because of this, we went to understand the will of God, being warned and stirred by these signs.

**E.K.:** Madimi <note>A recurring female spirit or angelic entity</note> is here.
**[Dee]:** **Blessed are the feet of those who preach the peace and favor of the Most High.** <note>original: "Benedicti sunt pedes evangelizantium pacem et favorem altissimi."</note>
**Madimi:** ...... What should I say to you, since you have no faith?
<margin>Faith.</margin>
**Madimi:** Why should I teach you, who despise my instructions <note>original: "documents"</note>? I knock in vain, for you do not hear me. **One seeks one thing, another seeks another; you are mismatched.** <note>original: "Unus unam alius aliam quærit: dispares estis."</note>
**[Dee]:** **God is able to satisfy all people, even the most diverse, if they always seek good things.** <note>original: "Deus potest omnibus et diversissimis satisfacere, bona semper petentibus."</note>
**Madimi:** ...... Shall I speak, or no?
**[Dee]:** Speak in the Name of God; who would not hear the words of the wise and of the mighty, of the good and true?
<margin>Madimi</margin>
**Madimi:** ..... Shall I close my mouth because of your wickedness? Or shall I open my mouth because my Mother has commanded me? I will go back and ask that my mouth may be sewed up with a double thread, for assure yourself I will not come again willingly. But if she says again, "Go," I will come. Oh, why does God give bread to dogs, or allow his sun to shine into the bottomless caves? I know a reason, but yet I am torn in spirit. After prayers to God were finished, the Angel of God quickly appeared.

February 28. In the morning around 6 o'clock. At Limburg. Thursday. Note: I had ordered the horses to be tended to from 4 o'clock in the morning so that by five, or as soon as it was daybreak, we might be riding. In the meantime, while E.K. still lay awake in his bed and I was in the next chamber nearby, organizing the items in my traveling bag <note>original: "male"</note>, E.K. heard a voice (like mine) say "D." At this, he asked me, "What did you say?" I answered that I said nothing. Then he wondered what creature had used that voice. 

Afterward he rose; and when he had been ready a while and sat in the chamber where my bag lay, he said that he felt something crawling, or as if someone were writing on his back, and at length it seemed to ascend into his head. And so I left him and went out into another place and kneeled to pray. Upon the coming in of Thomas Kelly into that room where I kneeled (in the doorway of a little open gallery over the street), I rose up and went in again to E.K. 

He told me that he had slumbered because of the heaviness of his head, and that he seemed to see me praying and Michael <note>The Archangel Michael</note> standing by me. I answered that it was true I had been somewhat inclined to prayer, but that I could not pray as I would, etc. 

Hereupon, immediately he saw Michael over my head with a pen in his hand. Because of this, I was convinced that I was to write something of importance. I made haste to take pen, ink, and paper, and to settle myself to writing, because we were in a hurry to ride—intending to travel 8 or 9 miles that day—and company was waiting for us. One of them was a Jew whose sister is wife to Doctor Salmon, the Jewish doctor of Prague, etc. 

And as I was preparing to wait for something to write, a voice said as follows: 

"Why do you not shut yourself in to hear my voice?" <note>original: "Cur non includis te ad audiendum vocem meam?"</note>

[delta] Hereupon, I did shut all the doors, even the outermost doors. 

A voice said: "In the receptacle, so that the truth may be better proven." <note>original: "In receptaculo, ut magis approbetur veritas."</note>

[delta] Hereupon, I speedily took out the show-stone <note>A crystal or polished stone used for scrying.</note> and set it on the table before E.K.

E.K.: "Now here is Madimi <note>A spirit appearing as a young girl who frequently communicated with Dee and Kelley.</note>; she stands in the white circle and looks into the fire; she kneels. On the outside of her stands Michael with a sword." 

E.K.: "Madimi is gone away, and..."

Michael: Let him draw near to you. <note>original: "approximet ad te"</note> The speedy return of Curtrus was to deliberate with Rodolph <note>Emperor Rudolf II</note> how they might, under the pretense of justice, entangle you. Moreover, he has betrayed his master, and the cause of his master's adversity has its primary root in him. For three years he has acted unjustly and has exposed his Lord’s secrets. Upon this we received great comfort, and so we broke our fast and returned to Prague again before four o'clock in the afternoon. 

**Note:** While I was away, I had left a letter for the courteous Balthasar Frederick, Lord of Ossa, <note>original: "Balthasar Federicus Dominus ab Ossa"</note> to be shared with the Spanish Ambassador, Lord Romfe, and my Lord Kinsky. In it, I begged pardon for my sudden departure, especially since my child was not yet christened. I had given my wife strict instructions not to deliver the letter before Friday night. 

However, it happened that this Mr. Balthasar had sent word of his arrival in Prague with Lord Kinsky (whom I had met riding out of town the previous Friday; he told me then that he would be away for three or four days). Balthasar expressed a desire to speak with me. Because of this, my wife thought it best to send the letter to him early, and she did so shortly before my return home. When I learned of this, I was somewhat sorry. I immediately sent word to Master Balthasar of my return to certify to him that my wife had made a mistake in sending that letter to his Worship before Friday night, at which time she would have seen whether I had truly ridden forth to Brzeg <note>original: "Bressel"; likely Brzeg in Silesia</note>. He then desired to speak with me, and from him I received back my letter, which he had read. He offered himself as most ready to fulfill the requests contained within it.

Now to the main matter: At my return home from Master Balthasar Frederick of Ossa, I found Emericus Sontagius in my wife's heated room <note>original: "stove"; a common term for a room heated by a stove, often used for socializing</note> with Master Kelly. At the sight of me, Emericus was greatly amazed and almost unable or unwilling to speak, except to say, "You are old knights" <note>original: "vos estis veteres equites"</note>. 

Then Mr. Kelly told me that Emericus had informed him that the Emperor <note>Rudolf II</note> had been very melancholy all day yesterday and would speak with no one. Emericus claimed he knew of my journey the moment it happened, and that he learned of it through the Jews—specifically through the Doctor's son, who had tried to help me get the four horses. Emericus labored very hard (without being asked) to persuade me that the Emperor’s first and primary knowledge of my departure came from the Jews. After this (it being now night), he went home.

... This Necessity is two-fold: one (that is to say, the first) is contemplative and fixed. The other is active and leading toward an end. For behold, although he was previously sanctified unto the Lord and made a chosen vessel—wherein, if he continues, he shall necessarily enjoy the reward and glory of the sanctified—yet if he loses that Necessity and flies from his own law and condition, taking part in the filthiness and iniquity of his enemy through Satan or his own flesh, he must of necessity perish. Herein I teach you: he who is first elected <note>term: Election; the theological doctrine that God chooses certain individuals for salvation</note> and applies himself to the necessity of his election—doing the works that are righteous before the Lord and receiving comfort by the visitation of God’s mercy—is sealed to the end of his election in gladness. Through the value and strength of Perseverance, he cannot fall so far that he shall be bruised, or run so far astray that he shall be unable to remember himself.

Is there a Justice that is fixed, a Justice triumphing, a Justice mighty, a Justice unable to be resisted, a Justice that Prayer prevails not against—yes, a Justice in which Hell and the Devil are condemned? This is that Justice; this is that two-edged sword; this is that Iron Mall <note>original: "Mall"; a heavy hammer or mace used as a weapon</note> wherewith those who refuse their Election <note>The theological doctrine that God chooses certain individuals for salvation</note>, or are not elected, following the necessity of wickedness, are and shall be cut in pieces, beaten into small powder, and be cast into the lake of fire and brimstone. 

This is he that seals up the second Hell with the second death. This is what you—O you starvelings, you vagabonds, you stiff-necked and stinking sinners—ought to dread and fear! Has God elected you, and do you disdain it? Has he provided a Seat for you, an Honor for you, a Crown for you, a Wedding Garment for you, and his eternal glory for you? And will you force him to cast it into the fire? Shall the finger of God write your names, and shall the vengeance of God root you out? 

Repent, I say, and fly from your iniquity. Return into the way of the Lord, lest God, seeing your wickedness, your unnatural and inhuman rebellion, and your disobedience against your Father, thrust himself upon your necessity with his justice and vengeance. Are you not afraid of the unspeakable flames and firebrands of Hell, which are prepared for the wicked?

I do not say this so that you should murmur, saying, "Cannot God plant us without this?" but to make it evident to you: That God uses his visible creatures to introduce or lead in (even supernatural) force and wisdom.

<margin>Michael <note>The Archangel Michael</note></margin> A wood grew up and the trees were young, and behold, there arose a great tempest from the North. The Forester came and watched, and said to himself, "The force of this wind is great; see how this young tree beats itself to pieces against the greater one. I will go home and bring my gardening tools <note>original: "ground instruments"</note>, and I will uproot <note>original: "eradicate"</note> it, and I will plant it further away. The Forester told the matter in order to his Master. But behold, his Master rebuked him, saying: "When the winds are not blowing, the trees grow; they are not harmful to one another. Therefore, leave them alone. When the young tree takes root and grows older, its roots shall link themselves with and under the roots of the greater tree. Then, even if the winds come, they shall not be harmful to one another, but shall stand so much more firmly by how much more they are wrapped together. Indeed, when the old tree withers, the younger shall be a strength unto it, and shall add to its age as much as the older added to its youth." And he ceased to dig.

<meta>This page continues the diary of John Dee, detailing his travels and legal disputes in Poland during April 1585.</meta>

"I will sing of the mercies of the Lord forever; who is like my God, who, even when he was angry, showed mercy to those who call upon him with a contrite heart? <note>original: Misericordia Dominum in æternum cantabo, quis sicut Deus meus, qui cum iratus suerit, misericordiam præstavit contrito corde invocantibus</note> Therefore, to my God alone be all praise, honor, glory, and rejoicing, now and forever, Amen."

**April 5.** At Prague. Friday, I took my journey from Prague toward Krakow. May God grant us good speed. Traveling with me were E. K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s medium and assistant</note>, my brother Thomas Kelly, and my servant Hugh Brycket.

**Friday. + Krakow, 1585. April 12.** In the afternoon <note>original: A meridie</note> we arrived at Krakow. As we were within an English mile of the city, on a fair and calm day, there passed about half a mile before us—crossing from the right hand to the left—several whirlwinds, one after another. They whipped up the dust with great force high into the air, shooting forward and then mounting upward, moving south away from us. Likewise, some began on the right hand and came furiously, raising and spiraling the dust into the air toward the south as well, but did not cross our path.

When we arrived at our house, we found that a stranger had been moved into it by the landlords (Mr. John Long, the Judge, and Martin Plutner). Since I had the keys to the storehouse and the street door with me, I ordered my belongings that I brought with me to be moved in, and that night we managed as best we could for lodging. However, the new and forced-in tenants reluctantly allowed me to use one of my own bedsteads, which was in one of the heated rooms <note>term: stove; a room heated by a large ceramic stove, common in Central Europe</note>, and they cleared it for us with much difficulty.

**Saturday and Sunday** we were severely confronted, or rather threatened, that we should have no house there. Also, the coat of arms of a man named Bonar was placed upon the door, as if the house had been officially granted to him by virtue of his office <note>original: ex officio</note>.

**Monday** I informed the Rector <note>likely the head of the university or a high official</note> of the injuries I endured. He courteously sent two Masters of Arts with me to the Proconsul <note>a high-ranking city magistrate</note> to obtain a summons <note>original: Citation</note> for the landlords to appear on Tuesday by 7 o'clock to answer our complaint. This Monday night, Lord Laski <note>Albertus Laski, a Polish nobleman and Dee's patron</note> arrived from Lasko, following a letter he had received from me from Nysa regarding my arrival.

**Tuesday (April 16)** Lord Laski came to the house. In the morning, he wanted to immediately throw all the strangers' belongings out of doors, but at my request, he permitted them to move everything into the lower heated room. In the meantime, I appeared in court with my lawyer or attorney, Mr. Tetaldo (an Italian), a long-time practitioner in Polish and Krakow legal cases. To conclude, I received a decree against my landlords stating that I was entitled to at least a half-year's notice before eviction. Thereupon, John Long gave me notice to vacate by Michaelmas <note>September 29</note>. And so we left the court or town house, called the *Praetorium* in Latin.

This same Tuesday afternoon, Lord Laski went to the King of Poland <note>Stephen Báthory</note> up in the Castle and told him of my arrival and how poorly I had been treated. The King said, "Why did he not throw them out of doors?" 

"I have done so now," said Lord Laski; and the King granted the...

The House was to be held by virtue of office <note>original: "ex officio"</note>. And the next day, the King showed deference by asking to speak with me. On Wednesday, April 17, I went with Lord Lasky <note>Albert Łaski, a Polish nobleman and patron of Dee</note> to the King, to whom I spoke to this effect:

> "May the consolation, peace, and mercy of God be with you, O most serene King. In His presence, I have received a divine admonition to present myself before you, which I now most humbly do. I am most ready to treat with your Royal Majesty with all faithfulness and sincerity regarding those things which are divinely enjoined upon me. I shall not refuse to relate the histories of those mysteries in order, as occasion shall be given, and to perform all other things which I understand to be pleasing to God and to your Royal Majesty, etc." <note>original: "Consolatio, pax, and misericordia Dei sit tibi..."</note>

The King answered:

> "Just as I heard many good things of your person while you were absent, so now your arrival is very pleasing to me. If there is anything in which my grace and favor can be of benefit to you, I will not fail to show myself as your favorer and protector. Regarding these and other greater matters, there will be a more opportune time for speaking after these feast days, at which time I will see to it that you are summoned to me, etc." <note>original: "Ut de vestra persona multa bona audivi..."</note>

Upon this, I made a courtesy <note>a formal bow or gesture of respect</note>, as was appropriate, and stepped back somewhat from the King. Then the Vice-Chancellor and other officers, including the Chief Secretary, brought bills to be read and signed or assigned with the King’s own hand, which he did. After Lord Lasky had watched for a fit time to tell the King of his desire to speak a few words to his Majesty regarding some of his own affairs, and was told to come to his Majesty straightway after dinner, we took our leave with due reverence. We went out of the withdrawing chamber, through his private chamber (where he had said Mass when we first arrived), into the Guard-chamber, and downstairs, etc.

On Friday, I took spiritual <note>original: "Ghostly"</note> counsel from Doctor Hannibal <note>Hannibal Rosselli, a Franciscan theologian</note>, the great divine who had recently published some of his commentaries upon the *Pymander* of Hermes Trismegistus <note>A foundational text of Hermetic philosophy</note>. On Saturday, April 20, I received the Holy Communion at the Bernardines <note>A branch of the Franciscan order</note>, where that Doctor is a professor. This day, E. K. <note>Edward Kelley</note> [received] spiritual counsel and comfort, as his case required.

### 1585. + Krakow. April 24. In Easter-week. Wednesday morning, around 8:00 AM.

After prayers were made to God, both the Lord’s Prayer and others specifically regarding the Ministry of Angels who preside over the obtaining of kingdoms (as was prescribed to us), and while I tried to name someone specifically, immediately E.K. began and followed— <note>original: "Orationibus factis ad Deum..."</note> E.K.: There appears afar off a woman coming, and she is <margin>A woman.</margin> here now; she is all covered in green, as with a cloud. She stands as if in a hollow shell, or a concave oval figure. <margin>Our duty toward King Stephen.</margin>

> Stephen, lift up your head among the stars of Heaven; for the Spirit of God is with you, and you have become the Darling of the Highest, but the Lord will rebuke you for your sins. Behold, you shall stand, and your sword shall be made holy. See therefore that you honor him, labor for him, and obey him, as the anointed and beloved of the Lord. For why? Your servant is guided and shall not stumble, but shall return, so that the name of God may be blessed. **Notes at Krakow.** Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday; May 6, 7, and 8. **E.K.** <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s scryer</note> was very unquiet in mind, and expressed this to me in words. He was upset because **A.L.** <note>Albert Łaski, a Polish nobleman and their patron</note> had not paid him his money, which was long since due. Chiefly, he doubted very much whether **A.L.** would turn to the Lord with all his heart and remain constant. **A.L.**’s former life and ungodly living and dealing offended him so much, and he was so void of any hope, that he became greatly oppressed in mind to find us coupled with such an ungodly man. 

I showed him **A.L.**’s last letters, explaining how he was in a monastery of his own belonging to the Castle Rithwyan (which he had now won by a stratagem from the unjust delays of his adversary), and describing what penance and contrition he was in, what meditations he held, and what godly purposes he had, etc. 

But **E.K.** would not hope for a conversion. Thereupon, he utterly and resolutely intended to leave here with all speed for Prague, and told me to prepare my letters if I wished to send any. He became very blasphemous against God, to my great grief and terror. I feared what the outcome would be, for the blasphemy and rebellion against God and His holy purposes for us were so great that almost nothing worse could be uttered. I used as quiet words as I could, assuring him of God’s mercies, which are always ready, and His helping hand for all those who put their trust in Him and call upon Him in their troubles and times of need. And so I committed him to God for that Tuesday night, it being past nine o'clock. 

On Wednesday morning, as I was at my prayers in my study above his chamber, I made a declaration of this cause and the most grievous perplexity I was in to see my friend and partner (**E.K.**) thus carried away with such a manifold and vehement temptation. **E.K.**, still lying in his bed, called his brother Thomas to him and told him to call for me. Thomas came for me when I had nearly ended my devotions and prayers. I went to him while he was still lying in his bed. After I had wished him a good morning and sat by him on the bench at his bed’s head, he began to speak as follows:

**E.K.** A Spirit appeared to me this morning by my bedside and told me to be quiet. It told me to ask you to go tomorrow with both your...

[Δ] <note>This symbol represents John Dee himself in his journals.</note> I fetched the scrying stone, and after it had been set out for about a quarter of an hour, E.K. saw in it a little naked boy with a white cloth scarf hanging from under his navel down to his knees. **The Boy:** God created all things by the breath of his mouth; he who is also Spirit defends and will defend his own, and those who hope in his name. <note>original Latin: "Creavit, Deus omnia Spiritus oris sui qui etiam Spiritus, defendit and defendet suos, and in nomine suo sperantes."</note>

E.K. says: He throws up his circle and catches it again three times. He stands still and says nothing more yet.

**The Boy:** You who are pierced by the Lord, speak. <note>original Latin: "Perforatus à Domino, loquere."</note>

E.K. says: Now he has turned into water that swirls around, and in the middle of it is blood. Now he has returned to his former shape again.

**The Boy:** The end of all flesh is at hand. And the sickle of the Highest shall reap down the mountains; the valleys shall be without fruit, and the seed of man shall be accursed. 

E.K. says: Now he turns his face toward you [Δ].

**The Boy:** Who is he that the Lord rejoices in, or on whom the Heavens look with a happy countenance? Whose feet are not a burden to the earth, and in whom is the strength of the soul comforted? Who is he that shall rejoice in the Lord? It is he who goes out of himself and looks back at himself, saying, "O you carcass, you are a tomb for me; I am not placed within you for your own beauty, but so that the Lord may be magnified and his creatures honored." 

It is he who shakes off his own self and puts on the armor of affliction, praising and extolling the crown <note>original: "Garland"</note> of the God of Hosts in front of that Great Whore <note>A common Reformation-era reference to the corruptions of the world or the Roman Catholic Church.</note> and in defiance of her congregation. It is he who forsakes his own will to do the will of him who created him. Therefore, whoever does his own will is the servant of damnation <note>original: "Perdition"</note>; but he who waits for the will of God is anointed <note>original: "avointed"</note>. 

Behold, therefore, because you do this—and have looked at yourselves not as being of yourselves, but have acknowledged the power of God and the truth of his message—your honor shall be great. Therefore, do not fear; for look, this crown is prepared for you, and rest is promised <note>original: "sealed"</note> to you by the Highest—to you, your wives, children, and servants.

[Δ] Blessed be your name forever, O eternal, almighty, and most merciful God and King of Glory.

> I remember you, **Laski** <note>Albert Laski, a Polish count and patron of Dee and Kelley</note>, says the Lord; and I will chasten you for your sins. May 22. Wednesday, at Niepołomice <note>A town in Poland near Kraków</note>, in the Royal Court, around 1:30 in the afternoon. # Page 386

In the new garden, which is currently being constructed, the King began to speak. (Lord Albert Lasky <note>Albertus Laski, a Polish nobleman and Dee's patron</note> was present and was commanded to be there by the King.) The King said to me words very nearly to this effect:

"The Lord Palatine <note>referring to Lasky</note> has urged me to hear you speak concerning these great and rare matters. This I have done willingly. However, this must be considered: that all the Prophets and revelations ceased long ago, even in the time of Christ. Nevertheless, if there is nothing in these matters against the honor of God, they are all the more willingly to be heard. Indeed, I do not doubt that God can even now, in many ways, reveal certain secrets to men—even up to these present times—through commands that are unusual and extraordinary."

<insert>—Notes— G1: An option was given in the year of Lasky regarding the correction of Stephen. G2: Today his followers ought to [be heard]. G3: Honor, praise, and glory be to God.</insert>

---

Thereupon I <note>John Dee</note> answered to this effect, although I cannot express the exact same words:

"I consider three main points in your Royal Majesty’s speech, which contain the very marrow of your reasoning. First, concerning the cessation of Prophecies and revelation; second, whether there is anything in our actions or exercises against the honor of God; and third (which is very pleasing to my soul), that you do not prescribe to God any certain ways or times in which He should or must reveal His secrets to men.

Regarding the first point, we are able to assert to your Royal Majesty that the passage of Scripture on this matter is not rightly understood by many. It is understood worst of all by those who wish to prescribe certain ways and times to God’s omnipotence, mercy, and wisdom—asserting that there is no Prophecy in these times, nor would there be after Christ, because all ceased in Christ. 

This is to say that all the Prophecies which concerned Him—specifically concerning the Son of God coming in the flesh, the true Messiah, and the future Redeemer of the human race (and concerning that entire history of Christ which we Christians acknowledge and confess to be completed and perfected)—have indeed now ceased. They have ceased in the sense that those events are neither still to come (as the Jews believe), nor are they to be repeated, since they are already finished and performed just as the Prophets foretold. 

For this reason, when Jesus Christ, hanging on the cross, knew that all the Prophecies concerning Him were fulfilled, and we understand that the target of all Prophecies (before the Christian era) had been hit, and the mystery was completed according to the presence and purpose of God the Redeemer of human conscience, He Himself said, 'It is finished' <note>original: *consummatum est*</note>. For Paul also said to the Jews: 'When they had fulfilled all that was written of Him, taking Him down from the tree, they laid Him in a tomb.' 

And after His Resurrection, Christ Himself said to His disciples (as they were traveling toward the village of Emmaus and talking of His death and..."

<meta>This page continues a theological argument regarding the necessity and persistence of divine revelation and prophecy after the time of Christ, using various New Testament examples to refute those who claim such gifts have ceased.</meta>

(Speaking to those who were arguing and doubting the resurrection) he said, "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe in all that the Prophets have spoken: Was it not necessary for Christ to suffer these things, and so to enter into his glory?" And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself, etc. <note>original: Luke 24:25-27</note> And a little later, he said again to the same people: "For it is necessary that all things be fulfilled which were written in the Law of Moses, and the Prophets, and the Psalms concerning me."

But as for that other opinion—that there would be no more prophets or revelations after Christ—the Scriptures themselves most clearly teach the contrary. For what shall we say of that notable revelation, the *Apocalypse* <note>The Book of Revelation</note> of Blessed John, which came after Christ? It is called a "Prophecy" by John himself, when he says: "Blessed is he who reads and hears the words of this prophecy, and keeps those things which are written in it." <note>original: Revelation 1:3</note> And in the last chapter of the same Apocalypse (or Revelation), he calls it a "book of prophecy" three times. Therefore, it is manifest that there are revelations and prophets after Christ.

Furthermore, what was that revelation made to Paul at his calling and conversion by Jesus Christ himself, as appears in the book of the *Acts of the Apostles*, Chapter 9? What shall we say of the revelation to Cornelius the Centurion? <note>original: Acts 10</note> What of the one to Peter concerning clean and unclean animals? <note>original: Acts 11</note> And Paul himself says: "If I must boast (though it is not profitable), I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord," etc. <note>original: 2 Corinthians 12:1</note> And a little later: "Lest I should be exalted by the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan to buffet me." <note>original: 2 Corinthians 12:7</note>

He also writes: "The mystery was made known to me, as I wrote above; by which, when you read, you may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ, which in other generations was not made known to the sons of men, as it is now revealed to his holy Apostles and Prophets by the Spirit," etc. <note>original: Ephesians 3:3-5</note> Here also it appears that there are Prophets after Christ. And in Chapter 4: "And he gave some to be Apostles, some Prophets, others Evangelists, and others Pastors and Teachers, for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: until we all come into the unity of the faith... unto the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ," etc. <note>original: Ephesians 4:11-13</note>

In this passage, it appears that Prophets will remain in the Church of Christ after Christ's time until we all meet in the unity of faith. We know well that this unity has not yet been achieved since Christ's time; and now, in our own age, we are especially discordant regarding matters of faith. Therefore, it seems that not only Prophets but also very clear Revelations concerning Divine Mysteries are most necessary. 

Consider also the angelic message to Philip, and his invisible transport from place to place by the Spirit. <note>original: Acts 8; Philip was carried away by the Spirit of the Lord after baptizing the Ethiopian eunuch.</note>

O most mighty God, my God, who has joined to us this your Lasky <note>Albert Laski, a Polish nobleman and patron of Dee and Kelley</note> as my most cautious athlete, courageous, and most beloved to me: a man most loving of your Catholic and orthodox religion, and a most sharp enemy of all Anti-Christianity. Who would not wish to obey you with all their strength and greatest zeal, as you have commanded? And you have ordered that we should show him honor and obedience. After our many laborious travels—some direct, others previously (by human judgment) appearing to go backward—lasting over seven months, you have brought us through safely and unharmed by your greatest grace, favor, and help.

As we meet here as your servants in your Name and with one mind, may you deign, by your Fatherly mercy, to purge me of all the filth of my entire life. And by the interceding merits of the Name of your most beloved Son, our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, forgive us—each and every one—whatever we have offended against your Holy and Just Laws, whether willingly, or unknowingly, or through negligence, in word, deed, or thought, up until this very hour. Let him see that we have each been predestined for unique duties in your Holy service since before the beginning of the world, etc.

## The Year 1585. August 6. A single Action, which may be called the Puccian Action. Which lasted from 5:00 in the morning until 11:00.

->PRAGUE. The Puccian Action.<-

Prague. The first part of the Puccian Action. August 6, Tuesday morning, around sunrise, as was commanded of us yesterday. Having poured out prayers according to custom, etc., we being present—John Dee, Edward Kelley, and Francesco Pucci <note>A Florentine radical thinker who joined Dee and Kelley's circle</note>—as was prescribed. The Table of the Covenant was arranged, and a wax candle was lit. 

**Edward Kelley:** Here is one, covered in white to the breast, all dressed in white; he has a long glass in his left hand, full of filthy, loathsome stuff, like pus <note>original: matter</note> or like blood and milk, or curds mingled together. He has a staff about an ell <note>A unit of measurement, roughly 45 inches</note> long in his right hand; he sets the end on the ground and points with his staff toward the **Table of Covenant**. 

**John Dee:** Approach the Lord.

**John Dee:** Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord: O blessed Light of God, URIEL. Glory to you, Lord, King of heaven and earth, who is at rest and who is to come.

<margin>John Dee: The third part of 37½.</margin>

**The voice:** Divide into three parts. 

**URIEL:** It is done.

If you are not children, you are not sons; if you are not sons, you have no Mother; if you have no Mother, you are dogs. You are devourers of the bread of children—currish, senseless, and against God.

Enter, therefore, into judgment with yourselves. Consider that you are created by God. Consider that you are redeemed by God. --- Page 511 ---
<meta>This page continues a sharp polemic against self-appointed teachers and sectarian leaders who claim divine authority without proper calling or spiritual lineage.</meta>

Do you dare to bind the reckless whims of your imaginations to the truth? Is it a small thing to you to establish your own decrees, to sit in judgment against the Spirit of God, and to allow Him no place except by your own prescription? Is it permitted for you, in the presence of the Son of God, to consume entire days—indeed, unjust years—with the children of Satan, that lying brood and deceivers of the world? Have you so thoroughly committed yourselves to the workshop of abomination that you wish to prescribe to the Son of God the time of His future coming and the descent of His Prophets, and to set the limit of the time in which He Himself shall visit the earth?

Moses dared to speak nothing except from the mouth of God. The Prophets did not explain the Law themselves, but rather the voice of God did. The Son of God spoke no words of His own insofar as He was flesh, but spoke the words of His Father. His disciples taught nothing except from the Holy Spirit. Do you dare, therefore, to assume for yourselves the office of teaching and to reveal the hidden secrets of the Most High, when you have not been admitted or called to these things?

Tell me, have you abandoned your trade <note>original: *Mercaturam*</note> and the calculations of your money (acquired through fraud) so that you might be teachers of the Word of God? Are you not ashamed to teach before you understand the matters yourselves? Indeed, are you not ashamed to lead others astray before you even know how to lead them home? You are hypocrites and void of the Holy Spirit.

---

You have become liars and enemies of Christ Himself and of His Holy Spirit. Perhaps you say, "We gain our understanding of the Scriptures from reading them." But answer me: by the help of which spirit do you gain this understanding? What angel appeared to you? Or from which heaven did you receive your instruction? It is possible you will say, "From the Holy Spirit."

O you fool of little intelligence! Do you not understand that the Holy Spirit is the Teacher <note>original: *Paedagogus*</note> of the Church, of the entire flock, and of the congregation of Christ? Therefore, if He is the Teacher of the multitude, it follows that any doctrine, instruction, lesson, or understanding which the Holy Spirit teaches belongs to the multitude. And yet, what multitude of men shares your understanding? Or of what congregation are you a member? Otherwise, you belong to a dispersion. Do you say that you are one of someone's dispersed followers? You tell a lie; you are a fugitive.

Truly, behold, I teach you: your error stands plain before your face. Whoever arrives at an understanding of Scripture ought to strive to reach that understanding according to spiritual Order <note>original: *Ordinationem*</note> and Tradition. But from what spiritual tradition did you obtain your understanding? Or according to what Order was the sense of the Scriptures opened to you? You will say (perhaps) that you were informed by the Holy Fathers, and that you obtained your understanding through the same spirit by which they taught. You can certainly say such a thing, but it is certain you do not act accordingly. For which of the ancient Fathers would couple human reason with the Word of God, or...

--- Page 512 ---
<meta>This page continues the author's defense of traditional Church authority and the apostolic succession, specifically addressing the interpretation of Scripture and the role of the Papacy.</meta>

Who has restricted the understanding of Scripture to the teachings of the Pagans? <note>original: "Ethnicorum astrinxit disciplinæ"</note> I tell you that the ancient Fathers were dear to Christ and were participants in heavenly visions and celestial consolations. These visions and heavenly comforts did not teach them a new way to explain the Scriptures; rather, they confirmed and illuminated with light the mysteries of the Holy Spirit declared by the Apostles, who themselves laid the foundations of the Church. 

Therefore, whatever you might learn from the ancient Fathers, you learn from the Apostles; and whatever you understand from the Apostles, you possess from the Holy Spirit. But if you interpret the Fathers according to your own personal sense and whim, and not according to the sense of the Apostles, you certainly do not have the Holy Spirit, but rather a spirit of lies. 

Therefore, show yourself to be humble and fall down before the Lord. Set aside your own human reasoning and cling to the Lord; labor to understand His word through His Holy Spirit. You must of necessity find this Holy Spirit—and you shall find Him—in the invisible Church until the end of the world. 

I will speak clearly to you (so that the truth may appear powerfully in the light): whoever is contrary to the will of God—which was handed down to His Church, published by the Apostles, nourished by the Holy Spirit, shared with the world, delivered through Peter to Rome, expressed there by him, and retained and sustained by his successors—this person is contrary to God and His truth. 

**Luther** has received his reward. **Calvin** has received his. All the rest, as many as have erred and willfully run into devious paths by separating themselves from the Church and Congregation of Christ—obstinately and by the instinct of the Devil (their father)—have received their reward. Against them the Son of God shall pronounce judgment, saying: "Go, you deceivers, into the fire of Gehenna <note>hell</note>, prepared from the beginning for your Father and his children." 

Among yourselves, you rise up asserting that the Pope is the **Antichrist** (for you distinguish him by that name). Certainly, a man might be evil and fall away from his calling, but he can never be the Antichrist. For the Antichrist is he who is the son of the Devil, a man born of flesh and blood from an impious and deceitful harlot, who shall seduce the people. Swollen with the power of his father, he will resist God on Earth among men, just as his father did in Heaven among the Angels, utterly denying the omnipotence of God and opposing himself to Him. 

O you fools of little understanding! When the keys of Heaven were entrusted to the Apostles—which is to say, the same authority and power of Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, to forgive the sins of men and to exclude sinners from Heaven—and when it was also said to those same Apostles, "Get behind me, Satan," you do not have enough intelligence to look into these mysteries of the Most High. If the Son of God both commended and rebuked His disciples, why then can a Bishop <note>original: "Episcopus"</note> not be considered both good and evil? If it follows from this that good and evil can exist in a Bishop, by the same reasoning it can be inferred...

<summary>The author argues that true scriptural interpretation must align with Apostolic tradition and the Roman Church, condemning Reformers like Luther and Calvin while defending the Papacy against the "Antichrist" label by distinguishing between a flawed man and the ultimate theological enemy.</summary>

--- Page 513 ---
<meta>This page continues the author's defense of episcopal authority and the necessity of remaining within the established Church, warning against individual interpretation of Scripture without authorized guidance.</meta>

The nature of episcopal authority <note>original: *authoritatis Episcopalis*</note> does not depend on whether a bishop is good or bad. Rather, that goodness or badness affects the life of the bishop himself: if he is good, he will reap the benefit of his goodness; but if he is bad, he is a liar, for his own life contradicts his teaching. Furthermore, if God permits many to sit in the holy place who are defiled by the spirit of Ananias <note>Ananias was a high priest mentioned in Acts 23 who was criticized by St. Paul; also a reference to the figure in Acts 5 who lied to the Holy Spirit.</note> because of the sins of the people, that is due to your own sins and rebellious nature, so that you may receive your punishment. Even so, His Church does not become obscure or dark. Therefore, open your eyes and understand: cling to the Church for the love of the Church itself, and not for the sake of men. Do not despise the Church because of the iniquities of men.

<margin>Matthew chapter 16; Acts 23</margin>

Instead, submit your necks to her holy yoke and to the ordination which will lead you to that Congregation which is governed by the Spirit of God. In that place, you will understand that the secrets of the Book of God have been explained according to the sense of your ancient Fathers, whose understanding came from the divinity of the Holy Spirit. You cannot receive authority from yourselves, and without authority, you can do nothing. Therefore, since your own authority is non-existent, why do you seize the works of the Church into your own hands? It is one thing to seek some understanding of the Scriptures, but it is quite another to teach the Scriptures according to one's own understanding. For he who teaches, teaches by authority; but if he does not have authority, he is a usurper or an intruder. 

My brothers, consider yourselves well. Consider that you are children, and that you are not your own masters but belong to another. Therefore, do nothing as if it came from yourselves, but follow (like good children) the footsteps of your Mother. She is a pure Virgin Mother and is always informed by the wisdom of the Comforter <note>original: *Paracleti*; referring to the Holy Spirit</note>, who must provide food for you (her children) and educate and instruct you in her way. Simplicity and obedience are worth much before the Lord, that is certain; but curiosity is a devil. Have you not read that the bread of the saints is not to be thrown before dogs? Examine yourselves deeply to see whether you are dogs or not. See whether your life is holy, your works right and just, your patience abundant, and your affliction great for the sake of the Lord. If you do not find yourselves to be in this state, you are not children; if you are not children, you are not sons; if you are not sons, you have no mother. If you have no mother, you are devourers of that bread which belongs to the children—dog-like, senseless, and against God. 

Therefore, descend into a judgment of your own state. Consider the Father: by God you were created. Consider the Son: by God you were redeemed. Consider the Holy Spirit: you are also under the spiritual protection and consolation of God. This God has ordained a congregation for you—a holy and sanctified society for your nourishment.

Always together like brothers, under his wings and at his table; he who feeds you with the bread of life and understanding—namely, with the body and blood of Jesus Christ, the son of the living God. Moreover, he feeds you with the bread of understanding so that you may understand the will of your Father who is in Heaven; and with obedience, so that when you have known him, you may become obedient in your deeds. This obedience is the very goal of your calling. Therefore, do not shake off the yoke of obedience in any way, nor at the same time push away from yourselves the cup of understanding; for by that reasoning, your Father’s will would remain hidden from you. 

But in my judgment, you are starving; your intestines are shriveled, and your bones and muscles are wasting away. What is the cause of this? When did you last receive that bread of the Lord? When did you receive nourishment? Oh, you of little faith and even less understanding, you wander and run astray. You are blind; you do not obey your Father’s will. Return, return, and say such things within yourselves: 

"O eternal God and kind Father, great indeed is your care and mercy toward us, whom you have led back home after we were driven into error by Satan and the spirit of darkness. You have set before us—who were blind, though our sight is now restored—the true path and the straight line of understanding. O how happy are we, whom you hold so dear, and whose salvation is of such great concern to you! Therefore, we will celebrate your name with praises and turn back from our errors. We will confess our sins and observe your precepts. For you alone, O Lord, are just and true, and your mercy is eternal. Your laws are sweet, and your loving-kindness is powerful among us. Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of Hosts <note>original: Zebaoth</note>. Let all honor, praise, and glory be given to you forever. Amen."

# THE BOOK OF RESURRECTION. Prague, April 30. The Pact, or Covenant of the Sabbath-rest. 1586. Třeboň <note>original: Threbone</note>

[Graphic omitted] [Graphic omitted] We arrived on October 14. [Graphic omitted] [Graphic omitted] September 14, 1586. [Graphic omitted] In May 29, a Decree of Exile was issued against us by the Emperor Rudolf. [Graphic omitted] On August 8, permission to return was granted by Lord Rosenberg, who obtained leave for us to come to his estates.

### A miracle and a deed to be remembered forever.

As E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s medium and associate</note> stood at the end of the gallery by his chamber, looking over into the vineyard, he seemed to see a little man—the gardener—in all his usual behavior and clothing, who is the chief workman or overseer of Mr. Carpio’s laborers in that same vineyard. He seemed to very skillfully prune some of the trees. At length, he approached the wall near E.K. and, holding his face turned away, he said to him, "I pray you, tell the Lord Doctor <note>John Dee</note> to come to me" <note>original Latin: Quæso dicas Domino Doctori quod veniat ad me</note>. And so he went away, appearing to cut the trees here and there very skillfully. Finally, over the cherry trees by the house on the rock in the garden, he seemed to mount up in a great pillar of fire.

E.K. told his wife to go and see who was in the garden. She came back up and brought him word: "Nobody." E.K. then came to me and said, "I think there is some wicked spirit that would deceive me," and he told me what I have noted above. Then I said, "I will go into the garden," and I asked E.K. to come with me.

We went down the path that this creature had taken, but we saw nothing. We went to the banqueting house in the vineyard, but that place did not please us. So, we went along the path by the cliff side and sat down on the bank by the great pile of vine-stakes lying at the very south end of the vineyard. We had not sat there even seven or eight minutes <note>original: half a quarter of an hour</note> when I spotted something under the almond tree on its south side. This was the westerly almond tree—the one standing on the western side of the straight path that leads from the north toward the south in the vineyard.

I spotted (I say) what looked like a sheet of fair white paper being tossed to and fro in the wind. I rose and went to it, and—to the praise of God’s truth and power—there I found three of my books lying, which had been so diligently burned on the tenth day of April last.

1. The first of the three books was *The Book of Enoch*.
2. The second was *The 48 Angelic Keys* <note>original: 48 Claves Angelicæ</note>.
3. And the third was the book of my collection of the thirty "Aires" <note>spiritual realms or dimensions</note>, entitled *The Book of Earthly Knowledge, Aid, and Victory* <note>original Latin: Liber Scientiæ terrestris auxilii et victoriæ</note>.

Thereupon, as E.K. came to me, I fell on my knees, yielding great thanks to Almighty God; E.K. did the same. His mind and body were marvelously affected at the sight of the said books, which showed no sign that they had ever been in the fire—neither in their color, their scent <note>original: favour</note>, nor was anything missing from them. After we had sat for half an hour under the aforementioned almond trees, praising God and wondering at the miracle, suddenly the very same gardener appeared by us, looking like...

This Gardener <note>A spiritual being appearing in the form of a gardener</note> went before Edward Kelley, and his feet seemed not to touch the ground by a foot's height. And coming there, the spiritual creature seemed to set one of his feet on the post on the right hand outside the furnace mouth, and with the other to step to the furnace mouth, and so to reach into the furnace. The bricks which stopped the mouth of the furnace were now plucked away, all except for one brick's thickness. As he reached into the furnace, there appeared a great light, as if there had been a window in the back of the furnace. Also, to Edward Kelley, the hole—which was no larger than the thickness of a single brick—seemed now more than three or four bricks wide.

He went before in a little fiery cloud, and Edward Kelley followed with the books under his arm all along the gallery. He came down the stairs by Francesco Pucci’s chamber door, and then his guide left Edward Kelley; and he brought me the books to my place under the almond tree.

At dinner this day at the Archbishop’s table, his heart and thoughts dwelt very much upon it, etc. At these words of his, I rejoiced greatly to perceive the workings of the Most High in hearing his faithfully offered prayer. I saw that the answer which I read to him was so appropriately applied to his prayer, as he himself also perceived with great comfort and spiritual joy. He entreated me earnestly that I would pray to God that the Emperor <note>Emperor Rudolf II</note> might be restored to the favor of God, as he was when I first declared my message to him from the Most High. 

I answered that whatsoever the God of Heaven and Earth should appoint me to say or do unto his Majesty, I would most willingly rejoice in the faithful doing of it. I added that it was my duty as a Christian to pray for his Majesty, but I could not promise that my prayer would be heard; however, I would highly rejoice if his Imperial Majesty would so conduct himself in God’s judgment as might be meritorious in the sight of our Redeemer. Such words and matters as these passed between us. 

And he said that he would in all points fulfill the advice and warning of God expressed in this "Action" <note>term: Action; Dee’s term for a spiritual session or séance</note>, and would marry a maiden as he was commanded. On this day, he acknowledged and accounted himself a happy man. 

<margin>G3</margin> And concerning our mutual bond—by means of each of us being given to the other by the God of Heaven and Earth—he vowed and promised that he would regard it in all points to the best of his skill and power, etc. These and other such good seeds for the service of God being sown between us, he went toward his palace in the Court, and I went to the waterside, and so over to the coach waiting for me, and so came home. God be praised.

Right Honorable SIR,

Although I have traveled a hundred miles (from Prague to this Leipzig Fair) almost in vain, I had hoped either to meet my servant there with an answer to my former letters sent last November to her Majesty (at which time I also wrote to your Honor and several others), and so to have sent word back from Leipzig as quickly as the occasion required. Now, I find neither servant, nor letter from him, nor even a word of mouth. Yet, despite all this—and whatever the hindrance or delay may be (whether my letters were kept from her Majesty, or whether the manifold, urgent, and most weighty public affairs are hindering or delaying her Majesty’s most gracious, discreet, and wise resolution in this matter, or whatever other cause has resulted in this long and wonderful <note>original: "wonderful"; here meaning "astonishing" or "surprising"</note> delay in receiving an answer)—despite all this, I thought it good, before I board my coach, to visit and most humbly salute your Honor. I do so very faithfully, dutifully, and sincerely, with the same great goodwill that my letter written to your Honor some years ago intended to show (though that letter was then a stumbling block to your Honor and others because of the strength of the phrases used within it).

The truth is, right Honorable, that the merciful providence of the Highest, shown through His great and abundant graces upon me and mine, is so wonderful and mighty that very few can believe it unless they are present witnesses. Therefore, one can easily judge how hard these things are to be believed in a place where my entire life and actions were interpreted in a contrary sense, and where a sentence of death was contrived and decreed against the innocent.

I am forced to be brief. That which England suspected was also here, for these last two years, almost secretly in doubt, under question, and subject to Imperial and Royal consultation. It has been discussed, pried into, and peered into by honorable spies fawning about me and by others. At length, both the chief Roman <note>original: "Romish"</note> power and the Imperial dignity have resolutely reached a point where, on one hand, they are sorry for having so lately corrected their erroneous judgment against us and about us, and they seek means to deal with us so that we might favor both the one and the other. On the other hand, they have sent to Rome for as great an authority and power as can be devised; and likewise here, all other means and ways are being contrived to see how, by force or by fear, they may make us glad to follow their whims.

But it is all in vain, for we do not fear human force, as I have plainly and often declared to the Princes. Otherwise than in pure truth and godliness, we will not favor anyone. My words may seem very marvelous in your Honor’s ears, but mark the end: we have had (and shall have) to deal with no children <note>original: "babes"</note>. I have very often, and upon many of their requests...

To all Christians who, with great zeal for His glory, suffer the cross, tribulation, and persecution from the rancid and rotten Babylonian whore <note>original: *scorto Babylonico*; a common Protestant Reformation-era pejorative for the Roman Catholic Church</note> in the most turbulent ocean of this world: may we, by the example of Jesus Christ who is in the Father, and by the power and help of the Holy Spirit, be able to endure all these things patiently for the glory of His name and the salvation of our souls. Amen.

It will perhaps seem strange to your Lordships that I, an unknown man, write to those I do not know. You may attribute a good part of this fault to the most righteous grief which I conceived from a rumor spread and brought to me concerning your Lordships. For I cannot sufficiently marvel at the stubborn zeal of that Babylonian beast, which leaves nothing untried, moving every stone, by which it strives not only to harm but to utterly destroy men of your nation, especially those who are pious and lovers of God. 

On the eleventh day of this past month, the Papal Legate <note>original: *Legatus Pontificius*; the Pope's official representative</note> offered a "Book of Supplications" (as they call it) to his Imperial Majesty. In this book, he falsely charges your Lordships with Necromancy <note>original: *Nicromanciæ*; the practice of communicating with the dead or black magic</note> and other prohibited arts, and heavily accuses you with other slanders. I might have been able to obtain copies of this book, but I was informed of the matter too late; nor is it safe or without suspicion to ask the man who translated it from Italian into Latin. 

Therefore, since I know for certain that all these charges against your Lordships—as Christian men and philosophers—are vain, I wished to write this letter both to support and warn you, so that the Legate may find your Lordships more prompt and prepared to respond. I ask, therefore, that you receive this in the spirit in which it was written: namely, a Christian spirit, upright and sincere. Farewell, and commend me to Christ in your prayers.

**Postscript:** I would have sent these letters to your Lordships some days ago, but I was informed that you had set out on a journey. However, after I learned from the noble servant of Lord von Bickerstein (Ferdinand Harnik) that your Lordships had returned to this our country, I could not neglect to signify by these letters that which it interests you to know.

I had been tossed about on a certain intricate journey through mountains, through valleys, through the densest forests, through open fields, and through deep snow that was almost impassable for us. Yet (with the Most High always protecting us), we have finally returned healthy and safe, with both our horses and your Highness’s carriage unharmed. For this prosperous success, we give the highest thanks to the Most High, and we confess that infinite thanks are owed by us to your Highness. 

While I was away, that Apostolic Nuncio <note>The Pope's diplomatic representative in Prague, Germanico Malaspina, who was suspicious of Dee’s occult activities.</note> began to either believe false things against us too lightly and complain rashly, or to devise perverse things from his own mind. Truly, if they continue in this way (having now had a sufficiently accurate experience of us for two years), those who ought to surpass all men in piety and wisdom (at least common men) declare themselves to be the most envious, malicious, and perverse of all men—thirsting for human blood, proud, executioners of the innocent, and ruinous slanderers of the godly in Christ, etc. 

Truly (I say), we shall be compelled to shake the dust from our shoes and betake ourselves to other parts of the world. And unless we had that consideration for your Highness which we ought to have, and unless we considered ourselves protected (as it were) by your Highness’s guard, however armed—besides that invincible, invisible army of God the Best and Greatest—we would attempt to depart from this kingdom immediately. 

His Imperial Majesty <note>original: "Cæsarea Majestas," referring to Holy Roman Emperor Rudolf II.</note> ought also to take care that in some way, and very quickly, it may be perceived by this whole Kingdom that we two are not only true Catholics, but also most loving of true piety and Christian peace. It is not necessary that I pour out more through these letters in a certain fervor of my spirit. But let us both look back most diligently and circumspectly at the inestimable Gift of God, which He has conferred upon us both. For we are as if three; but in one God, we ought to be as one man. Note this mystery: **I.D.E.K.W.R.** <note>Likely a cipher or initials representing John Dee, Edward Kelley, and perhaps Wilhelm von Rosenberg (Vok z Rožmberka), their patron.</note> For he who has me, also has E.K. <note>Edward Kelley, Dee's medium and companion.</note>; and him whom I hold as mine, he also must be considered to belong to my E.K. May that Almighty God who created all things join your most Illustrious Highness to us as a minister and co-operator of His divine Justice and Glory, and preserve you for a very long time. 

At Prague, May 26, in the year 1586. 
Your most Illustrious Highness’s most faithful servant in Christ, 
**John Dee.**

For unavoidable, serious, and justifiable reasons, it has been decided that your Majesty <note>referring to Emperor Rudolf II</note>, in the Kingdom of Bohemia as well as in your other Principalities and Lands, can no longer indulge or allow the presence of [John Dee and his associates]. Therefore, it is now your Majesty's final will and strict command that [John Dee], together with his wife, children, and all his followers, as well as his associates and subordinates—under penalty of your Majesty's severe and inevitable punishment and displeasure—shall depart from here within the next six consecutive days. He must immediately remove himself from your Majesty's Kingdom of Bohemia and all other Kingdoms, Electorates, and Lands belonging to your Majesty. He is never to return or be found within them again. Should he or his followers or subordinates act in disobedience, your Majesty will be forced to take strict action and punishment, which your Majesty would prefer to avoid. Your Majesty did not wish to withhold this final notice from him. This is your Majesty's firm will and intention.

**Decreed in the Secret Council of the Imperial Majesty. Prague, May 29, Anno 1586.**
**E. Waldstein. Saalfeld. Mynssnik. Doctor of Law.**

To be delivered to **John Dee**, <term>Doctor</term> <note>original: "Decret Doctor"</note> in your Majesty's Kingdom of Bohemia as well as other Lands.

In the year 1586, on the 18th of June, in **Erfurt**, Thuringia: The most illustrious Lord **Rosenberg** <note>Vilém z Rožmberka, a high-ranking Bohemian noble and patron of Dee</note> had sent **Johann Carpio** to us with his letters, primarily so that he might understand the will of God concerning his future wife and other matters. Regarding the questions and petitions of the most illustrious Lord, Kelley was divinely commanded to place a clean sheet of paper upon the Altar before a Priest celebrating the Mass. This he did on the year and day written above, in the morning between 6 and 7 o'clock, in the **Monastery of the Minor Order of St. Francis**, while a senior Monk was celebrating the Mass. 

When the Mass was finished, the words which follow were found beautifully written upon the paper. But on the following day, after they had been transcribed for the most illustrious Prince, all the lines and letters immediately vanished, and nothing remained visible on that paper afterward.

The rebel, who is too much devoted to the pleasures of this world, has long since wasted away, provoked by the wrath of my fury. Therefore, you must turn neither to the left nor to the right, but only toward the fulfillment of my will. Blessed is he who is obedient to me and to the commands of my father, and who is adorned with perseverance. But cursed is he who is a liar in his works and loses my word; for he shall be a scandal to many, and a disgrace to the peace of my Gospel. 

I have appointed you, William <note>original: "Gulielme"; referring to John Dee, whose middle name was Maria but here addressed perhaps in a symbolic or spiritual sense, or as a patronymic reference</note> (because you have joined your hands to me), to be a David for the slaying of Goliath, and by so appointing you, I have brought you forward. Use the world, therefore, for my glory, and lift up your body in me, so that my justice may be placed within it as is due. You are to utterly trample and root out the most wicked and foul pride of those who have turned my seat into a footstool of blasphemy and abomination. For you shall be blessed in the strength of my hand and spirit, because I have heard your prayers. 

Do not, therefore, neglect the time of your visitation; but rage with zeal and the sharpest indignation. Take the virgin who is joined to your walls <note>likely referring to a woman living in the same house or a specific spiritual match</note> as your wife; she is prepared for your loins and your old age. Love her with devotion and cherish her with affection, so that my promised blessing upon you and upon her may be made manifest. 

Furthermore, beware that you do not allow my servants—whom I have prepared to help you—to be snatched from your hands by others through your own negligence or fear, like sheep taken from your fold by evil arts and iniquity. For who shall steal away that which has been given by me? Think on this, therefore, and take care by remaining watchful over what has been harmed until now. For I will break the bridle of Satan and of your enemies. May the blessing of the Father and of my Spirit, and consolation from me (to whom all power is subject), be with you and upon you. Finally, having been warned, cease from your sins, so that when you speak my word, your life may be supported by my light and grace.

### MEMORANDUM

Be it remembered that Mr. Francis Pucci, a Florentine <note>Francesco Pucci (1543–1597), an Italian philosopher and lawyer who became involved with Dee and Kelley</note>, whom I left in our house at Prague when I went to Leipzig, had in the meantime been at Frankfurt am Main. He left Prague on about the same day that the Bishop of Piacenza, the Apostolic Nuncio <note>The Pope's diplomatic representative</note>, presented a libel to the Emperor against us, filled with the most horrible untruths, etc. At his departure from Prague, he had that Nuncio’s blessing, etc. 

In the meantime, and after his return to Prague again, it so happened that on the 30th of May last, I received the Emperor’s command for me, my companion <note>Edward Kelley</note>, and all my household to depart within six days out of Prague, and consequently out of all his kingdoms, dukedoms, and lands. 

This we did, and we came to Erfurt in Thuringia, and eventually to Kassel, to which we had moved our goods and family because the Senators of Erfurt would give us no permission to hire any house there. This was attempted both by Lord Schonberg in the name of Lord Rosenberg <note>Vilém Rožmberk, a high-ranking Bohemian noble and patron of Dee and Kelley</note> (which was rejected), and also attempted again by me and E.K. <note>Edward Kelley</note> on July 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14. And on Tuesday (the 15th day of June) Doctor...
