Regarding this transformation <note>original: *metamorphosi*</note> and the admirable course of our affairs, as well as our many wanderings, I shall express something that fits the situation perfectly. Having been divinely informed some years ago, and subsequently called out of England, we escaped many great dangers of the sea, not only by the most powerful hand of Almighty God, but also miraculously. We have been liberated thus far from the various fraudulent and cruel plots and attempts of men against us and our lives. To that same God of ours, we sing praises and thanks with a grateful mind, a joyful mind, and a mind truly most loving of the Christian, Catholic, and Apostolic Religion—and (by God’s confirming grace) one that shall remain most tenacious in the future.

But behold, nevertheless, those who are even considered to be legitimate sons of our same pious mother (the Holy Catholic Church) suddenly procured a mandate issued by the Emperor's command to send us—their brothers, who were living among them and before them in Prague in all modesty, quiet, peace, and civil justice—into a kind of exile or extermination. No cause for such a violent mandate was declared to us at all, neither privately nor publicly. But only by common report and courtly account did we understand, from a certain pamphlet presented by you to his Sacred Imperial Majesty, that the greatest indignation and, as it were, a burning anger of the Emperor had been stirred up against us. 

From this, a most bitter mandate was sent to us from the Bohemian Chancery in the name of his Sacred Imperial Majesty (with no cause or legitimate reason for the mandate expressed in it). It ordered that within the next six following days, I, my companion <note>likely referring to Edward Kelley</note>, our wives, all my children—even our infant Michael (born and baptized in Prague and still hanging at his mother's breasts)—as well as my male and female servants, and all my household, should depart from Prague itself, and consequently from the whole of Bohemia and any other Kingdoms, Duchies, and lands of his Sacred Imperial Majesty, never to return, under the danger of a terrible penalty to be inflicted.

We, however, without any delay, prepared ourselves to obey this Imperial mandate faithfully and humbly. We saw to it that our movable goods and the equipment of our pilgrimage—both our library and domestic items—were packed into two large wagons. Of our remaining goods, we gave one part to friends and dispersed and distributed another part to the poor. However, you should know that another part was removed from the face of the earth (for reasons not unpleasing to God) the day before our departure. But the best part, by Divine command, on the tenth day of April (when we were also divinely informed of this entire affliction and persecution), we committed to the flames. At that time, those things of that same "best part"—which no natural or common fire could ever hurt or consume—were received by visible angelic ministry out of the very highest flames into Divine, Angelic, and invisible custody. I recognize those breaths of discord, the rumors spread by envious men, and the suspicions cast upon us without certain evidence—all of which go against a faith proven by no small arguments. To the Supreme Pontiff <note>The Pope</note>, sitting in his watchtower over the entire Christian Republic, your persons have deservedly been placed under suspicion. In this way, you have been scrutinizing the minds of Princes and the inner recesses of their courts. This is because of your great skill in the hidden arts and sciences, by which the common people and the unlearned can easily be deceived. 

For since you are great astrologers, he said, and it is easy for you to obtain the horoscopes <note>original: "geneses"</note> of princes, and since you also possess familiar spirits and are skilled in the magical arts, you could without difficulty propose things—under the name of good angels—which actually flow from a spirit that is an enemy to the Church. 

Therefore, the Supreme Pontiff (to whom those two Princes are especially to be watched over, seeing as they live and reign among heretics) acted prudently when he ordered that an inquiry be made into your conduct and doctrine. However, it happened beyond his expectation and will that you were expelled without your case being heard. He said he truly grieved for our plight and was ready to assist so that you might justify yourselves; he asserted more than once that this was his wish.

For this reason, he encouraged me to go to the Most Illustrious Lord Rosenberg <note>Vilém z Rožmberka (William of Rosenberg), a powerful Bohemian nobleman and patron of alchemy</note> and signify to him his good inclination toward you. For he will easily obtain from the Supreme Pontiff that your case be heard here; and if he favors you, as he has done until now, he himself will also assist you with every service. He said he would be the first to prostrate himself at your knees if you turn out to be such men as some proclaim you to be.

I therefore went straight to the Most Illustrious Lord Rosenberg. But I had to return four times before I was admitted. On the 27th day, finally being admitted, I explained my devotion toward you and your affairs, and how the Illustrious Lord Nuncio <note>The papal ambassador</note> was disposed toward you. Finally, I prayed that he would not abandon that patronage and defense which he had undertaken for these most pious foreigners—who were appealing from a Caesar <note>The Emperor, likely Rudolf II</note> who was poorly informed to a Caesar better informed, and who desired their innocence to be proven to God and men.

He replied kindly: that you were not very well known to him; that he had spoken twice with the elder and only once with the younger <note>Likely referring to Dee and Kelley</note>; that he judged you learned, pious, and endowed with excellent gifts. He believed this trouble had happened to you because of some evil report, a disadvantage to which the affairs of princes are often subject. He said it was your duty to bear it with a calm mind. He did not repent of having favored you, and if he knew what you most specifically requested of him, he would take care to see that your wishes were met. Then it seemed right to me to say a few things regarding the great hope you had conceived of him...

And [I asked] how you could have sent me without letters to him. But they were included in the packet of Master John Carpion, which I immediately brought forward. At that moment, Master Carpion replied that he would not take it poorly if I gave them to him directly. I handed the packet to him, and he said he would read it thoroughly and give me an answer the following day. 

I then departed from him to go to the Illustrious Lord Nuncio <note>The Papal Nuncio, the diplomatic representative of the Pope</note>. Having found some free time, I resolved to discuss with him at length—both on my own behalf and through the Illustrious Florentine Ambassador—the notable injury done to you. I explained how hard you have worked so that you might be able to settle near Catholic churches, and how inhumanely you are being treated in lodgings and cities because of this Imperial prejudice. 

I informed him of the squalid and cramped conditions in which you have left your families, such that you have been unable even to unpack your furniture and books. I warned him that he should feel pity for the plight of Master Dee, who is now advanced in years, or rather an old man, and has never suffered such things until now. I argued that his hardships should not be considered those of an ordinary man, as he is a man of sixty years with four tender and most sweet children (the eldest of whom has scarcely passed his seventh year) and a most beloved wife; he cares for these dear pledges more than for himself. 

I showed what a great stumbling block this would be to English Catholics and others, and what an opportunity would be given to heretics to envy the ecclesiastical order. I declared the danger threatening that order if God should perhaps permit your talents to be used to arm their enemies to punish them. I demonstrated that God has, at other times, been accustomed to punish Catholic Jews by means of heretical Israelites. <note>A rhetorical historical parallel suggesting God uses outsiders to discipline His people.</note> 

Finally, I declared how absurd it is for you to be condemned without your case being heard, if you had deserved it; how much more absurd if you have deserved no such thing; and most absurd of all, since honor is rather owed to you by the Catholic Church. Since you ask for nothing more than to be allowed to clear your names, I argued that nothing more reasonable could be devised, and that there is no other way for the error committed to be corrected and for this business to be properly directed and restored.

He read your letters to me—that is, Master Dee’s letters—concerning matters that are, in some way, common to both of you. He said he does not believe the things contained in them regarding divine warnings and miracles. He asked that I myself explain the obscure passage concerning the burned books. He heard from me my eyewitness testimony regarding those burned items, and how I heard from you that they had been restored by heaven. 

Finally, he concluded that in those letters there are many things worthy of praise, many things to be wondered at, and likewise many things incredible. But, noting that they are not impossible for God, he is withholding his judgment; he does not wish to pronounce anything certain until the matter is thoroughly investigated. Nevertheless, he said he would reply to you kindly and give me letters for you, which he did later on the 28th. I am sending those letters to you along with these. ...so that you may compare [his words] with his deeds, and according to your wisdom and piety, take counsel and write back if it seems worth the effort. For as much as I can gather from his conversations, it seems to him that a new mandate is necessary from the Supreme Pontiff <note>The Pope</note> and the Emperor; nor can he promise or determine anything except by the words of his Master. Therefore, as far as I can see, the matter will be dragged out longer than we would wish, unless our Lord and heavenly Pontiff provides for us in another way. 

On the 28th and 29th, I found the Illustrious Lord Rosenberg <note>original: Rosenbergium; likely a member of the prominent Bohemian noble family</note> so busy that I could not be admitted, but he signaled through his chamberlain that he greatly desired for us to speak, and so I should return on the 30th. In the meantime, I was again with the Illustrious Lord Nuncio, who was soon to depart for the Monastery of Saint Charles, where he will stay as long as these summer heats rage. 

And as it happened conveniently during our talk, I thought it best to ask the man whether he approved of my opinion regarding how to distinguish—by certain signs and boundaries—the true Word of God from that which is false and counterfeit. This is necessary since an evil angel can transform himself into an angel of light, and false apostles not infrequently transfigure themselves into the Apostles of Christ. 

I said that two things seemed necessary to me for this judgment to be made properly: 
First, in the person listening, there must be a good inclination and a soul well-disposed toward the Creator, depending entirely upon Him, so that he holds nothing more important than pleasing Him; such a person does not doubt God's goodness and truth toward those who flee to Him to drink in the good spirit. 

Second, in the speech proposed in the name of God, those properties are required which befit such a great Author. <gloss>Paul</gloss> describes these graphically when he says: "For the word <gloss>G1</gloss> of God is living and effective, and sharper than any two-edged sword, reaching even to the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intentions of the heart; and there is no creature invisible in His sight." <note>Hebrews 4:12</note> 

God agrees with this, <gloss>G2</gloss> saying through <gloss>Jeremiah</gloss>: "The prophet who has a dream, let him tell a dream; and he who has my words, let him tell my words. What has the chaff to do with the wheat? says the Lord. Are not my words like fire? says the Lord, and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces?" <note>Jeremiah 23:28-29</note> 

I concluded, therefore, that a person who trusts in God perceives the truth of God's word by that effectiveness and ardor by which he feels himself affected. For the voice of a wolf or a strange shepherd cannot move a true sheep to follow him for long. I argued that this is the rule by which I would judge that divine sentences can be distinguished from non-divine ones. 

He approved of my opinion and added that without a good zeal in the listeners, the effectiveness of divine speeches does not appear, as is clear from the history of Christ. For while the simple Israelites said, "Never has a man spoken like this," and similar things about Christ's doctrine, the Pharisees and perverse priests mocked and despised Him.

**MEMORANDUM:** In the year 1586, on the 17th day of October, in the afternoon. After new disturbances and quarrels with Francesco Pucci <note>Francesco Pucci (1543–1597) was a Florentine philosopher and lawyer who initially joined Dee’s circle but became a source of significant conflict.</note> regarding money which he desired to have from us—out of generosity, and in the name of God, and as if from the servants of God, rather than from Edward Kelley as Edward Kelley—we (myself and E.K.) decided on a course of action. This was to avoid the many scandals which he had spread and devised against us concerning his 800 Florins. This money had been offered and returned to God by him, and previously refused when we were ready to pay him (at which time we showed him 630 Ducats in the presence of God, so that he might take from it what he judged to be his).

We decided, I say (with good hope that we would not offend God), to lay out the sum of 800 Florins before him in the presence of witnesses. If he asserted that it was owed to him, he could receive it if he wished; but if he denied that 800 Florins or any money was owed to him by us, then we wanted that also pronounced before witnesses, and made known by a signed document <term>chirographo</term> <note>original: "chirographo"; a formal written record or deed signed by the parties involved.</note> at appropriate times and places.
<margin>The first use.</margin>

We went, therefore, from the Castle to the Provost's House. Having called together several scribes of the Illustrious High Prince (Lord Rosenberg) <note>William of Rosenberg (1535–1592), a powerful Bohemian nobleman and patron of Dee and Kelley.</note>, we set out two large bags of money. From these (where two thousand ducats and more than 400 <unclear>Doleti</unclear> were counted upon the table), 800 Florins were counted out. When the dilemma was proposed to him (which I noted above), he was content to receive the money; however, he wished to sign that he had received it "in the name of God" and from us "as from the servants of God." 

We, however, protested that we would in no way take it upon ourselves to say this was from God, except insofar as it was to avoid great and many scandals against us. We left it to his free judgment there to say whatever seemed best to him and was [fitting] for him. He therefore accepted the money by his own choice and counted it. From this, a document was written by the hand of the High Prince’s scribe (Paul Wolf, who was present with various witnesses who signed their names, as can be seen in the document itself). Let us give thanks to God. For we hope that we shall now enjoy better peace and be more free from his venomous and restless tongue. May God convert him and be merciful to him; and as he said to us, may He now make him a minister useful to His Divine Majesty.

**Francesco Pucci.**
+ At Trebon. In the year 1587, January 21, at 9:00 in the morning.

### Friday, Session III. In the afternoon. 

A long delay. Many prayers were made, and those faithful servants of God were invited—those who had even promised their help in times of necessity. It was a long and strange delay, and no appearance was made to the boy himself. Finally, by a wonderful stroke of luck or by divine fate, Mr. Edward Kelley <note>E.K.</note> came to us, and I noted what followed. 

<term>Δ</term> <note>This triangle symbol represents John Dee himself.</note> He sat down by us. Arthur was still standing before me at the table, which was covered in the best manner, with only the <term>Stone</term> <note>The crystal or "shew-stone" used for scrying.</note> placed upon it. Kelley asked if anything appeared. We answered "No," even though I have called many times and prayed earnestly that some of our former friends might show themselves to the boy—specifically <term>Madimi</term>, <term>Il</term>, <term>Is</term>, and especially <term>Uriel</term>. I asked for Uriel because he was the first who appeared to join Kelley, myself, and the spirits together; therefore, he might also be the director in transferring Kelley's office <note>The role of the medium or seer.</note> to Arthur. 

Then Kelley said, "I marvel that you had no vision here. For while I was thinking somewhat of Arthur and his progress in the feat of <term>skrying</term> <note>The practice of looking into a crystal to receive spiritual visions.</note>, I came here into the gallery and heard you praying. For whatsoever you have done unto other men, even the self-same shall fall upon you; but happy is he who receives justice not through the terror of malediction <note>original: "maldicion"; meaning a curse or damnation</note>, but through the grace and mercy of God. 

The Apostle Paul abounded in carnal lust: he was also offensive unto his brethren so that he despaired, and was ready to have left his vocation, until the Lord said unto him, "My mercy and grace suffice for you." Believe me, that we are from above. Which considered: consider also, that as you cannot comprehend the heavens, so likewise can you not comprehend the wisdom of God, who says, "I will be merciful unto whom I please; and unto whom I will not, I have none in store." Foolish is he that asks why? And behold I say unto you, stumble not against God. Who is he that made you? Who is he that has given you power to look up towards heaven? 

You are fools, and of little understanding: this day says God unto you, "Behold, you have become free: do that which most pleases you. For behold, your own reason rises up against my wisdom. You are not content to be heirs, but you would be Lords—yes, Gods—yes, the judges of the heavens. Therefore, do even as you please; but if you forsake the way taught you from above, behold, evil shall enter into your senses, and abomination shall dwell before your eyes, as a recompense for those you have wronged: and your wives and children shall be carried away before your face."

The Almighty God of heaven and earth be my comfort, as I desire comfort in his service; and give me wisdom as I desire it for his honor and glory, Amen. 

**E.K.** <note>Edward Kelley, John Dee’s scryer.</note> I see a white pillar; and upon the pillar, I see four heads. She <note>Referring to the spirit or "she-angel" appearing in the stone.</note> ties the pillar round about with a band. The four heads are like two [human] heads, and two wolves' heads. Now there comes a thing like a white crown of crystal, and it stands upon all four heads. The heads seem to be enclosed by the necks within the pillar. Now she takes the pillar and goes up with it. Now she brings a half-moon down, and written in it is the following:

**Madimi** <note>The name of the spirit speaking; often appeared as a young girl.</note> Behold, do you see this? With that which you thought to overthrow and most infect, you are utterly overthrown, and shall never return again.

Now, my heart was deeply distressed for many reasons. Edward Kelley believed he now had a just and sufficient excuse to stop dealing with these spirits altogether, which, as seen in the earlier parts of these proceedings, had been his prayer to God for a long time. After we left the chapel and sat down for dinner—the four of us whose heads were shown united in a single pillar, as described previously—I found an opportunity to explain the great grief (mine especially) caused by this new command. We were told that, either as a test or as a literal command to be executed, we were to share our wives in common among the four of us. This was a shocking concept to the women, and they hoped for a more comforting outcome to the situation. With that, we ended the conversation.

After dinner, while Edward Kelley was alone, there appeared to him little creatures about a cubit <note>about 18 inches</note> high. They went to the still where he was distilling the spirit of wine <note>alcohol/ethanol</note> out of a <term>Ketorto</term> <note>original: "Ketorto"; likely a retort, a glass vessel used for distillation</note>. One of them, who identified himself as Ben, said it was useless to hope for the best spirit of wine that way. He showed Kelley how to distill and separate it more effectively, and even how to obtain oil from the spirit of wine as it burned in the lamps. 

Ben then began to ask Kelley what country he was from. When Kelley answered that he was an Englishman, Ben asked how he had come here. Kelley replied, "By sea." Ben then asked, "And who helped you survive the marvelous and great dangers of the sea?" He used this as an opening to speak of the many blessings God had granted us until now. 

This spirit, Ben, then said many other things (as Mr. Kelley told me on Saturday night after supper, <insert>Ben was the one who delivered the alchemical powder to Kelley during the digging in England. Note: this was perhaps conditional on the fates of Queen Elizabeth, Kelley, and King Philip.</insert> continuing his talk almost until two o'clock in the morning). Ben claimed that he was the one who had delivered or placed the powder into Kelley's hands. He also said, either then or at the latest the next day, that unless Kelley complied with God's will regarding this last command <note>referring to the "cross-matching" of their wives</note>, he would strip the <term>vertue</term> <note>inherent power or medicinal efficacy</note> and force from the powder so that it would become useless, and Kelley would become a beggar. 

Regarding me, Ben said that I did wrong to demand proof or testimony now that this latest doctrine was truly from Almighty God. He claimed that I would be led as a prisoner to Rome, and so forth. He spoke of England, saying that around July or November, Her Majesty the Queen would be destroyed by a strike from heaven, and that around the same time, the King of Spain would die. He also claimed that the current Pope would be killed while at Mass before two years had passed. He said another would become Pope, the fifteenth of his name <note>original: "Decimus quintus"</note>, and that he would begin to reform things but would shortly be stoned to death by the Cardinals. After that, he claimed there would be no Pope for several years. Regarding England, he said that after the death of our dear Queen, a member of the House of Austria—made powerful by the death of the King of Spain—would...

**Note:** When **E.K.** <note>Edward Kelley, Dee’s medium or "scryer"</note> had shown me this note, I immediately brought out my book of the **Tables of Enoch** and found the four letters **t T b d** to be the first four letters of the four principal squares standing around the **black Cross**. I realized that here they were to be placed differently than I had previously set them. 

In my first attempt at placing them together, I remember having doubts about how to join them, for they were given separately, each by themselves. Secondly, I found the four characters, except they were somewhat inverted and one of them was closed; I found none exactly like them, but very similar. These characters belonged to one of each square. 

Thirdly, I interpreted these numbers contained between the lines (some more and some fewer) to be words to be gathered out of the **Table of Letters**. There were as many words as there were distinct groups of numbers: specifically, 41. Based on this, we began to count the squares where the letters stood in the **Tables of Enoch** as I had them, but we could not find the words exactly, though we came somewhat near. 

Being tired and desiring to know the meaning of that **cipher**, we stopped until after supper. that is to say, appearances, shows made, and voices uttered by the spirits named within this book. Regarding the rest of the spirits, whoever they may be, from the beginning of these events (as appears at large by the records), I have not only doubted and disliked their insinuations and the doctrine they uttered, but also—desiring to shun and avoid the danger and inconvenience that might result from them, their actions, or the intent of their doctrine, or which might happen to my own injury in various ways—I sought many times to depart from these exercises. 

Furthermore, I boldly (as the servant of the Son of God) inveighed against them, urging them to depart or to give a better reason for their unknown and incredible words and speeches. At the same time, I often and on many occasions in a friendly manner exhorted the Right Worshipful Master **John Dee** (the chief follower of these things), as also appears in the records, to regard the health of his soul and the successful progress of his worldly reputation (which is great throughout Europe), as well as the future well-being of his wife and children. I urged him to beware of these spirits and to give them up entirely. 

In this, although I labored in a friendly and brotherly way, my labor seemed to be lost and my counsel despised by him. Moreover, I was pressed with his replies to the contrary and his promises; in that case, he even staked the loss of his soul's health if these spirits were not of God. Upon having, as it were, some further taste of them, or an opinion grounded upon the frailty of zeal, he did not cease to pawn his soul to me on their behalf. His persuasions were the chief and only cause of my continuing with them for so long. 

And now also at this moment, and a few days prior, having manifest occasion to think they were the servants of Satan and the children of darkness—because they clearly urged and commanded in the name of God a damnable doctrine, contrary to the Laws of God, His Commandments, and the Gospel delivered to us by our Savior Christ as a touchstone—I openly expressed to them my dislike of their proceedings. I brotherly admonished the said Worshipful and my good friend Mr. **John Dee** to beware of them. 

Now, having just occasion to determine what they were, to consider all these things I have mentioned before, and wisely to leave them—especially because they themselves (as appears by their own words) gave us a <term>Quietus est</term> <note>original: "Quietus est"; a Latin legal term meaning "he is quit," signifying a formal release from a debt or obligation</note>, or a passport of freedom, since we would not follow the doctrine they delivered.

Regarding the intention of the said Mr. Dee in receiving these messages as if from God; and in a way, moved by the zeal I saw him hold for the true worship and glory of God—which was to be promoted by us (as was promised by the spirits)—I decided to humble myself and yield to his opinion and determination. I gave up all my own reasoning, or whatever else <margin>The women.</margin> for the love of God. 

But the women <note>Jane Dee and Joan Kelley</note> utterly disliked this last doctrine <note>The command for the two men to share their wives in common</note>. After consulting among themselves, they gave us this answer: the previous spiritual actions did not offend them at all, but rather comforted them. Therefore, they believe this latest message—which does not agree with the rest (which they think to be according to the good will and wholesome Law of God)—makes them afraid, because it is expressly contrary to the Commandment of God. 

Thereupon, desiring God not to be offended by their ignorance, they required another "action" <note>A spiritual session or séance</note> for better information on this matter. In the meantime, through vowing, fasting, and praying, Mrs. Dee has covenanted <margin>An action required by the women.</margin> with God to abstain from eating fish or meat until His Divine Majesty satisfies their minds according to His established Laws, which are received throughout all Christendom. 

To this request of theirs to have another session, I <note>Edward Kelley</note> absolutely answer that my simplicity before the Highest is such that I trust He will excuse me. Because the sum of this doctrine, given in His name, requires an obedience which I have already offered (as is written before), I consider myself discharged of my duty. Therefore, I have no further reason to hazard myself any more in any spiritual action. 

Wherefore, I answer that if it is lawful for them to call this doctrine into question, it is even more lawful for me to doubt the great peril involved; considering that to return to the spirits where we have already been given an absolute answer would be folly, and might result in great inconvenience for me. Therefore, beseeching God to have mercy upon me and to satisfy their petitions, doubts, and vows, I finally answer that I will, from this day forward, meddle no more in this matter. 

April 22, 1587. By me, EDWARD KELLEY.

Wednesday, in the afternoon.</margin> The aforementioned Covenant was framed by me, John Dee, as nearly as I could according to the intent and faith required of us, to be notified and declared by the works of unity both spiritual and corporal. Now, it was thought necessary by the women as well as by ourselves to understand the will of God and his good pleasure: whether this Covenant and the form of words performed is and will be acceptable, and according to the liking of his Divine Majesty. And whether, upon the act of corporal knowledge <note>original: "corporal knowledge"; a legal and archaic term for sexual intercourse</note> being performed on both our parts, it will please his Divine Majesty to seal and warrant unto us most certainly and speedily all his divine, merciful, and bountiful promises and blessings. -> Magnificent men, brothers, and dearest friends. <-

Today at 9:00 in the morning, letters were brought to me from Lord Schomberg, which were dated March 5th, and they should have already come into my hands before now. From these letters, I understand that he is expecting a response from Lord Holck regarding Münsterberg. Since the Almighty Moderator and Ruler of all things has delegated you to this ministry and to oversee this work, I know nothing of what is to be done, nor can any counsel of mine be added so that I might arrange, know, or wish for anything, except what has seemed best to that most wise Moderator. 

Therefore, I transmit everything to you. Pray diligently, and whatever pleases the Most High and Most Powerful Lord, let it be done; and also inform me in all things, for in such great matters I gladly desire and wish to obey. And so, I would not want to let this day pass without immediately sending word back to you. Meanwhile, I commend both you and myself to the goodness and immense mercy of Almighty God. 

Dated at Krumlov, March 16, 1587. 
Your friend and brother, William, by his own hand.

Yet God has been your keeper and, having created you, has allowed you to live to this great age. Furthermore, you consider your own birth and your advanced years, thinking that by the natural course of aging, your time is likely coming to an end.

<margin>Note</margin> John Dee, that is the plain meaning: when it is said "not to do you good," it is because it will take somewhat too long. Since you are ready for it now, it shall be hastened forward with all the speed that is within God's will, in order to do you good. And now that I have spoken plainly to you in this case, my time appointed by God is at hand.

<margin>John Pontoys' note</margin> John Dee, you have fulfilled two questions concerning John Pontoys; look in your note.

**John Pontoys** Oh, that I might be fit to serve you in Bartholomew’s absence.

**Raphael**.... John Dee, in the name of the Most High, I answer you regarding this desire of his, wherein he craves from the hands of God to obtain the sight of His blessed creatures <note>i.e., to be granted the spiritual vision to see the angels as Dee and his scryers do</note>; but hereafter it shall be made known to you what God will do for him regarding that desire. And now, let all power and glory be given to the Almighty who has made heaven and earth; let His name be magnified and praised everlastingly. Amen, Amen.

**Δ** .... Amen.

**Δ** .... All praise, all thanks, all honor and glory be yielded unto God by all His creatures, now and forevermore. Amen.

<meta>This page continues the records of John Dee's spiritual conferences, specifically noting a request left by his associate John Pontoys and a lengthy passage in the "Enochian" or Angelic language.</meta>

... John Pontoys' note, which he wrote and left on my study table on the morning of September 7th. "If it may stand with the will and permission of the Almighty, whose name be blessed forevermore, I would desire to know: 1. My proper Angel. 2. The end of the Polish troubles. 3. Oh, that I might be fit to serve you in Bartholomew's <note>Bartholomew Hickman, another of Dee's assistants</note> absence."

Under John Pontoys' note, which is sewn over, is written the following: "The location of Basel on the Map of Europe. To the left or nearest side. Basel City. 2 feet and about 4 inches to the edge of the map below; 4 feet and a finger's width from Basel."
